sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מה דין הקונה בהמה מישראל כשאינו יודע אם ילדה.

sub.desc_en: Shmuel rules it is a doubtful firstborn (בכור ספק), because the buyer intends to slaughter it and the seller might not care to inform him.
sub.desc: שמואל פוסק שהבכור ספק, כי המוכר חושב שהלוקח רוצה לשחיטה ואינו מודיע.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan rules it is definitely non-sacred (חולין ודאין), reasoning that if the animal had not given birth, the seller would inform the buyer of the prohibition.
sub.desc: שמואל פוסק שהבכור ספק, כי המוכר חושב שהלוקח רוצה לשחיטה ואינו מודיע.

sub.desc_en: A baraita supports Rabbi Yochanan, stating that if the seller did not inform the buyer, the buyer may go and slaughter the animal without concern.
sub.desc: ברייתא מסייעת לרבי יוחנן: אם לא הודיעו המוכר, הלוקח שוחט ואינו נמנע.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects: does this baraita not refute Rav and Shmuel?
sub.desc: ברייתא מסייעת לרבי יוחנן: אם לא הודיעו המוכר, הלוקח שוחט ואינו נמנע.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves: there the matter depends on the seller (the baraita's case), while here the matter depends on the buyer (the dispute's case), so no refutation.
sub.desc: ברייתא מסייעת לרבי יוחנן: אם לא הודיעו המוכר, הלוקח שוחט ואינו נמנע.

items.text: משנת רבי אליעזר בן יעקב – בהמה ששפעה חררת דם
items.text_en: Mishnah: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov on an animal that discharged a clot of blood
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that if a large animal discharged a clot of blood, it must be buried and is exempt from the firstborn offering. The Gemara cites Rabbi Chiya that the clot does not transmit impurity through touch or carrying, and questions why it must be buried.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת שבהמה גסה ששפעה חררת דם – תיקבר ופטורה מן הבכורה. הגמרא מקשה: הרי אינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא, מדוע תיקבר?

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that if a large animal discharged a clot of blood, it must be buried and is exempt from the firstborn offering.
sub.desc: המשנה קובעת שבהמה גסה ששפעה חררת דם – תיקבר ופטורה מן הבכורה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Chiya teaches that the clot does not transmit impurity through touch or carrying.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מכיוון שהחררה אינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא, מדוע יש לקבור אותה?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the clot must be buried if it does not transmit impurity.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מכיוון שהחררה אינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא, מדוע יש לקבור אותה?

items.text: The status of a stillborn animal that exempts from bechorah
items.text_en: The status of a stillborn animal that exempts from bechorah
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why a stillborn animal that exempts its mother from bechorah does not transmit impurity through touch or carrying. Rabbi Yochanan answers that it is nullified by the majority (of the mother's body). The Gemara connects this to a similar principle held by Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and Rabbi Shimon.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why a stillborn animal that exempts its mother from bechorah does not transmit impurity through touch or carrying, given that it seems to be a viable offspring.
Rabbi Yochanan answers that the stillborn is nullified by the majority (of the mother's body), so it does not transmit impurity.

sub.text: Gemara's connection to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and Rabbi Shimon
sub.text_en: Gemara's connection to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and Rabbi Shimon
sub.desc_en: The Gemara notes that Rabbi Yochanan's principle aligns with the views of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and Rabbi Shimon, citing a mishnah where Rabbi Shimon holds that a fetus can be absorbed before birth.

items.text: Definition of 'pikah' for stillborn fetuses
items.text_en: Definition of 'pikah' for stillborn fetuses
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that stillborn fetuses do not require an opening in the grave until their head is rounded like a 'pikah'. The Gemara debates what a 'pikah' is: Rav Huna says it is a ball of wool, and a baraita records disputes between Rabbi Meir (woof), Rabbi Yehuda (warp), and Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok (when the 'tefifiyot' appear). Rav Huna and Rav Dimi report multiple traditions about different types of 'pikah', and Ravin clarifies that for a woman it is like the woof, for an animal like the warp.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites the Mishnah that stillborn fetuses do not require an opening in the grave until their head is rounded like a 'pikah'.
The Gemara asks what a 'pikah' is.
Rav Huna answers that it is like a skein of wool.
Chiyya bar Rav asks Rav Huna to clarify whether it is a skein of warp or woof threads.
Rav Huna cites a baraita with three opinions: Rabbi Meir says warp, Rabbi Yehuda says woof, and Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok says when the 'tefifiyot' appear.
The Gemara asks what 'tefifiyot' are.

sub.text: Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel citing Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok
sub.text_en: Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel citing Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok
sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel citing Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok explains that in Jerusalem they described it like a mule bending to urinate, with a skein emerging from within a skein.
Rav Huna reports that he heard two halakhot about skeins (warp and woof) but cannot explain them.
Rav Dimi in the name of Rabbi Yochanan reports three halakhot about skeins (warp, woof, and a large one for sack makers) but cannot explain them.
Ravin in the name of Rabbi Yochanan clarifies that for a woman the skein is like warp, and for an animal like woof.
The Gemara cites a baraita about the large skein of sack makers used as a measure for a clod from a beit haperas or from the land of the gentile nations.

items.text: Brine purchased from an am ha'aretz
items.text_en: Brine purchased from an am ha'aretz
items.desc_en: Reish Lakish states in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesi'ah that brine bought from an am ha'aretz can be purified by touching it to water. The Gemara analyzes this: if water is the majority, the immersion purifies it; if brine is the majority, brine cannot become impure. The minority of water is nullified by the majority. Rabbi Yirmeya limits this to dipping bread, but for a pot, the minority water is not nullified because it is a 'min b'mino' that can be reawakened. Abaye challenges this concept of reawakened impurity, and Rav Dimi cites a case of terumah to support it.

sub.text: Reish Lakish in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesi'ah
sub.text_en: Reish Lakish in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesi'ah
sub.desc_en: Reish Lakish states that brine bought from an am ha'aretz is purified by touching it to water.
The Gemara explains the reasoning: if water is the majority, immersion purifies it; if brine is the majority, brine is insusceptible to impurity, and the minority water is nullified.
Rabbi Yirmeya limits the purification method to dipping bread, but for a pot, the minority water finds its own type and is revived.
Abaye challenges Rav Dimi, questioning whether nullified impurity can be revived.
Rav Dimi supports his position by citing a mishna about a se'ah of impure teruma that fell, implying that nullified impurity can indeed be revived.

items.text: מחלוקת רבי אליעזר וחכמים בתערובת תרומה טמאה
items.text_en: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages
items.desc_en: Rabbi Eliezer rules that the mixture should be left to rot, as he assumes the se'ah that fell is the same one that rose. The Sages argue that the mixture can be consumed in certain ways, such as being eaten as crumbs or roasted, as long as no single location contains an egg's bulk of terumah.
items.desc: רבי אליעזר סובר שמרימים סאה אחת ומניחים לה להירקב, כי ייתכן שזו הסאה שנפלה. חכמים סוברים שהסאה שנפלה מתבטלת במאה, אך יש להיזהר שלא תבוא במגע עם מים כדי שלא תטמא את החולין.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states Rabbi Eliezer's position: the se'ah of terumah that fell into 100 se'ah of hullin must be removed and left to rot, because he assumes the same se'ah that fell is the one that rose.
sub.desc: רבי אליעזר פוסק שסאה אחת תורמת מהתערובת ותרקב, משום שסאה שנפלה היא הסאה שעלתה.

sub.desc_en: The Sages respond that the mixture can be consumed in specific ways — as crumbs, roasted, kneaded with fruit juice, or divided into dough portions — provided no single location contains an egg's bulk of terumah.
sub.desc: חכמים חולקים ואומרים שהסאה עולה באחד ומאה, ובלבד שלא יהא במקום אחד כביצה.

items.text: תנא עלה: פירוט דעת חכמים
items.text_en: Gemara's citation of a baraita
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites a baraita that elaborates on the Sages' ruling, stating that those hullin are treated in a specific manner.
items.desc: הברייתא מוסיפה כי לדעת חכמים, התערובת נחשבת כחולין ומותרת באכילה בתנאים מסוימים, כמו אכילה יבשה או קליות, או חלוקה לכמויות קטנות.

items.text: דין תערובת תרומה טמאה בחולין טהורים
items.text_en: Rabbi Eliezer's ruling and Ulla's rationale
items.desc_en: The Gemara presents Rabbi Eliezer's solution for a mixture of terumah and non-sacred dough: eat it in small pieces or with fruit juice, ensuring no egg-sized portion in one place. Ulla explains the reason is a decree lest one bring a kab of impure non-sacred dough from elsewhere and nullify it in the majority, but the minority 'awakens' the impurity.
items.desc: עולא מסביר את גזירת חכמים שלא להתיר לערב תרומה טמאה בחולין טהורים במים, שמא יביא קב טמא ממקום אחר ויבטלנו ברוב, אך המין הטמא יתעורר מחדש כשימצא את מינו.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what the solution is for Rabbi Eliezer regarding a mixture of terumah and non-sacred dough, and presents his ruling: eat it in small pieces or with fruit juice, ensuring no egg-sized portion in one place.
sub.desc: פותח בשאלה מה יעשו בתרומה טמאה לדעת רבי אליעזר, ומציע פתרונות מעשיים.

sub.desc_en: Ulla explains the reason for Rabbi Eliezer's ruling: a decree lest one bring a kab of impure non-sacred dough from elsewhere and nullify it in the majority, but the minority 'awakens' the impurity.
sub.desc: פותח בשאלה מה יעשו בתרומה טמאה לדעת רבי אליעזר, ומציע פתרונות מעשיים.

items.text: קושיית אביי: טהרה מעוררת טומאה?
items.text_en: Challenge: Can purity awaken impurity?
items.desc_en: A challenge is raised: if impurity can awaken impurity, can purity awaken impurity? The question implies that the logic of 'awakening' should not apply to a mixture of pure terumah and non-sacred dough.
items.desc: אביי מקשה על דברי רב דימי: אם טומאה מעוררת טומאה, כיצד טהרה יכולה לעורר טומאה?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara challenges: if impurity can awaken impurity, can purity awaken impurity? The question implies that the logic of 'awakening' should not apply to a mixture of pure terumah and non-sacred dough.
sub.desc: אביי מקשה על רב דימי: אם טומאה מעוררת טומאה, כיצד טהרה יכולה לעורר טומאה?

items.text: קושיה מאפר פרה אדומה ותשובת רב דימי
items.text_en: Objection from ashes and resolution
items.desc_en: An objection is brought from a mishna about a mixture of valid ash and kiln ash, where the majority determines impurity. If impurity is considered present, even if not touching, it should impart impurity via carrying. Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina resolves that it is pure from touch but impure via carrying.
items.desc: אביי מקשה מברייתא על אפר פרה אדומה שנתערב באפר מקלה, שאם הרוב אפר מקלה אינו מטמא במגע, אך לטמא במשא? רב דימי משיב בשם רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא שאכן מטמא במשא.

sub.desc_en: The gemara objects from a mishna about valid ash mixed with kiln ash: if impurity is considered present, even if not touching, it should impart impurity via carrying.
sub.desc: אביי מקשה מברייתא על אפר פרה אדומה שנתערב באפר מקלה: אם הרוב אפר מקלה, אינו מטמא במגע, אך לטמא במשא?

sub.text_en: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina's resolution
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina resolves that the mixture is pure from touch but impure via carrying.
sub.desc: רב דימי משיב בשם רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא שאכן מטמא במשא.

items.text: קושיה מנבילה בשחוטה ותשובת רב דימי
items.text_en: Objection from Rav Chisda and resolution via Rabbi Chiyya
items.desc_en: Another objection is raised from Rav Chisda's statement that a neveilah is nullified by a slaughtered animal, but it should still impart impurity via carrying. The Gemara resolves that the version taught by Rabbi Chiyya states that neveilah and slaughtered nullify each other, and Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina says it is pure from touch but impure via carrying.
items.desc: אביי מקשה מדברי רב חסדא שנבילה בטילה בשחוטה, ואם כן לטמא במשא? רב דימי משיב שהם שונים את הברייתא לפי רבי חייא, האומר שנבילה ושחוטה מבטלות זו את זו, ורבי יוסי ברבי חנינא מודה שמטמא במשא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects from Rav Chisda's statement that a neveilah is nullified by a slaughtered animal, arguing that even if nullified for touch, it should still impart impurity via carrying.
sub.desc: אביי מקשה מדברי רב חסדא שנבילה בטילה בשחוטה, ולפי הסברא שטומאה בטילה נחשבת כקיימת, היה ראוי שתטמא במשא.

sub.text_en: Gemara's resolution via Rabbi Chiyya's version
sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the version taught by Rabbi Chiyya states that neveilah and slaughtered nullify each other, and Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina rules it is pure from touch but impure via carrying.
sub.desc: רב דימי דוחה את הקושיה: הם שונים את הברייתא לפי רבי חייא, האומר שנבילה ושחוטה מבטלות זו את זו, ורבי יוסי ברבי חנינא מודה שמטמא במשא.

items.text: קושיה מחררת דם של בהמה גסה
items.text_en: Objection from Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and silence
items.desc_en: A further objection is brought from a mishna where Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov rules that an animal that discharged a blood clot must be buried and is exempt from the firstborn. Rabbi Chiyya teaches it imparts no impurity via touch or carrying. The Gemara asks why it should not impart impurity via carrying, and the interlocutor is silent.
items.desc: אביי מקשה מברייתא של רבי אליעזר בן יעקב על חררת דם שאינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא, ומשתיק את רב דימי.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects by citing a mishna where Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov rules that an animal that discharged a blood clot must be buried and is exempt from the firstborn.
sub.desc: אביי מקשה מברייתא של רבי אליעזר בן יעקב על חררת דם שאינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא, ומשתיק את רב דימי.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Chiyya teaches that the blood clot imparts no impurity via touch or carrying.
sub.desc: אביי מקשה מברייתא של רבי אליעזר בן יעקב על חררת דם שאינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא, ומשתיק את רב דימי.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the clot should not impart impurity via carrying, even if it does not via touch.
sub.desc: אביי מקשה מברייתא של רבי אליעזר בן יעקב על חררת דם שאינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא, ומשתיק את רב דימי.

sub.desc_en: The interlocutor is silent, unable to answer the objection.
sub.desc: אביי מקשה מברייתא של רבי אליעזר בן יעקב על חררת דם שאינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא, ומשתיק את רב דימי.

items.text: תירוץ אפשרי: טומאה סרוחה
items.text_en: Possible distinction: foul impurity
items.desc_en: The Gemara suggests a distinction: perhaps the case is different because the impurity is foul (serucha). This works for bar Pada, who distinguishes between severe impurity (up to a ger) and light impurity (up to a dog), but not for Rabbi Yochanan, who holds a different view.
items.desc: הגמרא מציעה תירוץ: אולי חררת דם היא טומאה סרוחה שאינה מטמאה כלל, ומביאה את דעת בר פדא ורבי יוחנן לגבי דרגות טומאה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests a possible distinction: perhaps the case is different because the impurity is foul (טומאה סרוחה), which might affect the rule.
sub.desc: הגמרא מציעה תירוץ: חררת דם היא טומאה סרוחה שאינה מטמאה כלל, ומביאה את דעת בר פדא ורבי יוחנן לגבי דרגות טומאה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara notes that this distinction works for Bar Pada, who distinguishes between severe impurity (up to a ger) and light impurity (up to a dog), but not for Rabbi Yochanan, who holds a different view.
sub.desc: הגמרא מציעה תירוץ: חררת דם היא טומאה סרוחה שאינה מטמאה כלל, ומביאה את דעת בר פדא ורבי יוחנן לגבי דרגות טומאה.

items.text: Opening question on the previous Mishnah
items.text_en: Opening question on the previous Mishnah
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions the Mishnah's statement that both a viable and non-viable birth are permitted to a dog, asking why the non-viable one is not already fit for a dog.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah permits both a viable and non-viable birth to a dog, since the non-viable one is already fit for a dog.

items.text: מחלוקת בר פדא ורבי יוחנן בטומאת נבילה
items.text_en: Bar Padda and Rabbi Yochanan dispute on the definition of neveilah
items.desc_en: Bar Padda distinguishes between severe impurity (until a ger) and light impurity (until a dog), while Rabbi Yochanan holds both until a dog. The Gemara explains Bar Padda's scriptural basis and addresses a counter-argument about a putrid carcass.
items.desc: בר פדא ורבי יוחנן נחלקו מתי נבילה מטמאת: בר פדא מבדיל בין טומאה חמורה (עד לגר) לקלה (עד לכלב), ורבי יוחנן סובר ששתיהן עד לכלב. הגמרא מביאה מקור לבר פדא מפסוק, ומתרצת את שיטת רבי יוחנן למעט נבילה שהסריחה מעיקרא.

sub.desc_en: Bar Padda states that severe impurity (טומאה חמורה) applies until the carcass is fit for a ger (convert), while light impurity (טומאה קלה) applies until it is fit for a dog.
sub.desc: הסתמא מציגה את מחלוקת בר פדא ורבי יוחנן בדין טומאת נבילה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan holds that both severe and light impurity apply only until the carcass is fit for a dog.
sub.desc: הסתמא מציגה את מחלוקת בר פדא ורבי יוחנן בדין טומאת נבילה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks for the scriptural basis of Bar Padda's distinction.
sub.desc: הסתמא מציגה את מחלוקת בר פדא ורבי יוחנן בדין טומאת נבילה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains that Bar Padda derives his position from the verse 'לֹא תֹאכְלוּ כׇל נְבֵלָה לְגֵר' (Do not eat any neveilah; give it to the ger), implying that only a carcass fit for a ger is called neveilah.
sub.desc: הסתמא מציגה את מחלוקת בר פדא ורבי יוחנן בדין טומאת נבילה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks how Rabbi Yochanan interprets the same verse.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת כיצד רבי יוחנן מפרש את הפסוק, ומשיבה שהוא ממעט נבילה שהסריחה מעיקרא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that Rabbi Yochanan uses the verse to exclude a carcass that became putrid from the outset (הסריחה מעיקרא) from the category of neveilah.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת כיצד רבי יוחנן מפרש את הפסוק, ומשיבה שהוא ממעט נבילה שהסריחה מעיקרא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that Bar Padda could also use the verse to exclude a putrid carcass, so why does he need a separate exclusion?
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת כיצד רבי יוחנן מפרש את הפסוק, ומשיבה שהוא ממעט נבילה שהסריחה מעיקרא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that a putrid carcass from the outset requires no verse to exclude it, as it is merely dust (עפרa בעלמא הוא).
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת כיצד רבי יוחנן מפרש את הפסוק, ומשיבה שהוא ממעט נבילה שהסריחה מעיקרא.

items.text: דין חררת דם של בהמה גסה
items.text_en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov on a gushing animal and Rabbi Yochanan's explanation
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that a large animal that gushes a clot of blood must be buried and exempts the firstborn. Rabbi Chiya adds it does not transmit impurity. Rabbi Yochanan explains this is due to nullification in the majority, and the Gemara questions why it is not considered never fit at all, answering that it was initially fit through its mother.
items.desc: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב פוסק שחררת דם של בהמה גסה תיקבר והבהמה פטורה מהבכורה. רבי חייא מוסיף שאינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא. רבי יוחנן מסביר שטעם ההיתר הוא משום ביטול ברוב, ולא משום שלא היתה ראויה מעולם, כי בתחילה היתה ראויה על ידי אמה.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah cites Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov's ruling that a large animal that gushes a clot of blood must be buried and is exempt from the firstborn obligation.
sub.desc: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב פוסק שחררת דם של בהמה גסה תיקבר והבהמה פטורה מהבכורה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Chiya adds a baraita that the clot does not transmit impurity either by contact or by carrying.
sub.desc: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב פוסק שחררת דם של בהמה גסה תיקבר והבהמה פטורה מהבכורה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan explains that the ruling is based on the principle of nullification in the majority (ביטול ברוב).
sub.desc: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב פוסק שחררת דם של בהמה גסה תיקבר והבהמה פטורה מהבכורה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the explanation invokes nullification in the majority, suggesting instead that the clot was never fit for impurity at all.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מדוע צריך טעם של ביטול ברוב, הרי חררת דם מעולם לא היתה ראויה לאכילה?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the clot was initially fit for impurity through its mother (אגב אימיה), so nullification in the majority is needed to explain its current status.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מדוע צריך טעם של ביטול ברוב, הרי חררת דם מעולם לא היתה ראויה לאכילה?

items.text: טומאת ציר של עם הארץ
items.text_en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov on brine and Rav Nachman's explanation
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that pure brine into which any water falls becomes impure. Rav Nachman says this implies amei ha'aretz are suspected of mixing half water into brine. The Gemara questions why half is significant, and answers that even less than half would be nullified, but here the small amount makes it half, and half is not nullified. Alternatively, the impurity is rabbinic and they did not decree for half-and-half.
items.desc: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב פוסק שציר טהור שנפל לתוכו מים כל שהוא – טמא. רב נחמן מסביר שעם הארץ חשוד לערב מים בציר עד חצי, והמים הקטנים מצטרפים לחצי ומבטלים את ההיתר. הגמרא דנה באפשרות של פחות מחצי, ומתרצת שטומאת עם הארץ וטומאת משקין דרבנן, ולא גזרו בחצי וחצי.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites the Mishnah where Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov rules that pure brine (ציר) into which any water falls becomes impure.
sub.desc: הבאת משנת רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: ציר טהור שנפל לתוכו מים כל שהוא – טמא.

sub.text_en: Rav Nachman quoting Rabbah bar Avuha
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman in the name of Rabbah bar Avuha explains that this Mishnah implies that amei ha'aretz (עמי הארץ) are suspected of mixing half water into brine.
sub.desc: הבאת משנת רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: ציר טהור שנפל לתוכו מים כל שהוא – טמא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the suspicion specifically concerns half water, since even less than half would be significant.
sub.desc: הבאת משנת רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: ציר טהור שנפל לתוכו מים כל שהוא – טמא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that the small amount of water becomes half the mixture, and half is not nullified (בטל) by the majority.
sub.desc: הבאת משנת רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: ציר טהור שנפל לתוכו מים כל שהוא – טמא.

sub.desc_en: Alternatively, the Gemara resolves that the impurity of amei ha'aretz and of liquids is rabbinic, and the Sages decreed only for a majority but not for a half-and-half mixture.
sub.desc: תירוץ ראשון: יש לגרוס 'עד מחצה', כלומר עם הארץ חשוד לערב מים עד חצי, לא פחות.

items.text: משנת רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: בהמה מניקה מן הגוי
items.text_en: Mishnah: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel on a nursing animal from a non-Jew
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that one who buys a nursing animal from a non-Jew need not suspect that the offspring belongs to another animal. Similarly, if one sees firstborn and non-firstborn animals nursing, there is no concern that the offspring have been switched.
items.desc: המשנה פוסקת שהלוקח בהמה מניקה מן הגוי אינו חושש שמא בנה של אחרת היה, וכן הנכנס לעדרו ורואה מניקות אינו חושש שמא החליפו ולדות.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel rules that one who buys a nursing animal from a non-Jew need not worry it is another's offspring, and similarly if one sees nursing firstborns and non-firstborns in his flock, he need not worry about swapped young.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין הלוקח בהמה מניקה מן הגוי ובהנכנס לעדרו ורואה מניקות, וקובעת שאין חוששים להחלפת ולדות.

sub.text_en: Mishnah: continuation of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's statement
sub.desc_en: The Mishnah adds that if one sees firstborn and non-firstborn animals nursing together, there is no concern that the offspring have been switched.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין הלוקח בהמה מניקה מן הגוי ובהנכנס לעדרו ורואה מניקות, וקובעת שאין חוששים להחלפת ולדות.

items.text: בירור דברי רב: הלכה בכל הפרק בר מפלוגתא
items.text_en: Gemara: Rav's ruling on the entire chapter and the dispute over its application
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman in Rav's name states that the halakha follows the entire chapter except for one dispute. Rav Sheshet questions which dispute Rav meant, considering various possibilities. The Gemara concludes that Rav meant the dispute of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and that the baraita is not actually a dispute.
items.desc: רב נחמן בשם רב קבע שהלכה בכל הפרק בר מפלוגתא. רב ששת תמה על קביעה זו, ומברר לאיזו משנה התכוון רב. לאחר שלילת אפשרויות שונות, מסיקה הגמרא שהכוונה לרבן שמעון בן גמליאל, ורב בא להשמיע שברייתא החולקת על משנה אינה נחשבת פלוגתא.

sub.text_en: Rav Nachman in the name of Rav
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman reports in the name of Rav that the halakha follows the entire chapter except for one dispute.
sub.desc: רב נחמן בשם רב קובע כלל: הלכה בכל הפרק כדעת התנא הסתום, חוץ ממקום שנחלקו במפורש.

sub.desc_en: Rav Sheshet objects, suggesting Rav was dozing when he said this, and asks which dispute Rav meant.
sub.desc: רב ששת תמה על דברי רב, ומטיל ספק אם אמרם מתוך ערנות, ושואל לאיזו משנה התכוון.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests Rav might have referred to the first mishna, but notes that Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva disagree there.
sub.desc: רב נחמן בשם רב קובע כלל: הלכה בכל הפרק כדעת התנא הסתום, חוץ ממקום שנחלקו במפורש.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests Rav might have meant Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, but notes that his mishna is already accepted as 'kav ve-naki' (a small but clean measure).
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה גם את האפשרות שהכוונה לרבי אליעזר בן יעקב, שכן הלכה כמותו ממילא ואין צורך בכלל זה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests Rav might have meant Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, but notes that a baraita disputes his opinion.
sub.desc: רב ששת תמה על דברי רב, ומטיל ספק אם אמרם מתוך ערנות, ושואל לאיזו משנה התכוון.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests Rav might have meant Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam, but notes that Rav already ruled in accordance with him.
sub.desc: רב ששת תמה על דברי רב, ומטיל ספק אם אמרם מתוך ערנות, ושואל לאיזו משנה התכוון.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests Rav might have meant the hair of a blemished firstborn, but notes that Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis disagree there.
sub.desc: רב ששת תמה על דברי רב, ומטיל ספק אם אמרם מתוך ערנות, ושואל לאיזו משנה התכוון.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that Rav meant Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and teaches that a baraita contradicting a mishna does not constitute a dispute.
sub.desc: הגמרא מיישבת: הכוונה לרבן שמעון בן גמליאל, ורב בא להשמיע שברייתא החולקת על משנה אינה נחשבת פלוגתא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara notes that Rav's ruling about the halakha following the entire chapter except for disputes is reiterated.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מאחר שכבר אמר רב שהלכה בכל הפרק בר מפלוגתא, מה חידש בקביעתו כאן?

items.text: Clarifying the ruling of Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam
items.text_en: Clarifying the ruling of Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah needed to state 'the halakhah is like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam' if it already said 'the halakhah is like the entire chapter'. It explains that without the explicit ruling, one might think the dispute with the baraita is a real dispute, but the explicit ruling teaches that the baraita's dispute is not a real dispute, and the halakhah follows Rabbi Yosei.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah needed to explicitly state 'the halakhah is like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam' if it already said 'the halakhah is like the entire chapter', and suggests that without the explicit ruling, one might think the dispute with the baraita is a real dispute.
The Gemara answers that the explicit ruling teaches that the halakhah follows Rabbi Yosei against Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and that the baraita's dispute is not a real dispute.

items.text: The baraita and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's principle
items.text_en: The baraita and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's principle
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites a baraita: one who buys a nursing animal from a gentile, the offspring that comes after it is a doubtful firstborn, because the animal may nurse even if it did not give birth. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: the matter is in its presumptive status (the animal is presumed to be nursing its own offspring). A second baraita illustrates this: if one enters his flock at night and sees certain patterns, he need not worry that the young have switched mothers.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks which baraita is being referenced regarding the dispute between Rabbi Yosei and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

The Gemara cites a baraita: one who buys a nursing animal from a gentile, the offspring that comes after it is a doubtful firstborn, because the animal may nurse even if it did not give birth; Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says the matter is in its presumptive status (the animal is presumed to be nursing its own offspring).

sub.text: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's additional statement
sub.text_en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's additional statement
sub.desc_en: A second baraita illustrates Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's principle: if one enters his flock at night and sees certain patterns, he need not worry that the young have switched mothers.

items.text: The doubt about Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's principle
items.text_en: The doubt about Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's principle
items.desc_en: The Gemara raises a doubt: does Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's principle mean that an animal does not nurse unless it gave birth, so if it gave birth we suspect it might nurse another's young? Or does it mean that it only nurses its own, and not another's? The practical difference is whether one would be liable for violating 'it and its young' (slaughtering a mother and its offspring on the same day) if the animal is nursing another's young.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a doubt about Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's principle: does it mean an animal nurses only if it gave birth (so we suspect it might nurse another's young if it gave birth), or does it mean it nurses only its own and not another's?
The Gemara explains the practical difference: whether one is liable for violating 'it and its young' (slaughtering a mother and its offspring on the same day) if the animal nurses another's young.

items.text: First and second attempts to resolve the doubt
items.text_en: First and second attempts to resolve the doubt
items.desc_en: The Gemara attempts to resolve the doubt from the baraita: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says one need not worry that the offspring was of another, implying only if it had a child from the beginning. But the Gemara rejects this, noting the wording 'was' not 'is'. A second attempt from another baraita: if one sees nursing animals, he need not worry about switching, because an animal does not abandon its own to nurse another's. This suggests it only nurses its own.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara proposes to resolve the doubt by citing Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's statement that a buyer need not worry the offspring was of another.
The Gemara objects that the baraita uses 'הָיָה' (was) not 'הוּא' (is), implying the exemption applies only if the animal had a child from the beginning, not to a current doubt.
The Gemara brings a second baraita: if one sees nursing animals in his herd, he need not worry about switching, suggesting an animal only nurses its own.
The Gemara explains the reason: an animal does not abandon its own offspring to nurse another's, so the nursing animal is assumed to be the mother.

items.text: Third attempt and rejection
items.text_en: Third attempt and rejection
items.desc_en: The Gemara tries to resolve from the phrase 'the matter is in its presumptive status', arguing that the beginning of the baraita is analogous to the end. But the Gemara rejects this, saying each case is different, and the word 'and thus' refers only to the exemption from firstborn status.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara attempts to resolve the uncertainty by citing the baraita's phrase 'דבר בחזקתו' (the matter is in its presumptive status), arguing that the beginning of the baraita is analogous to its end, so just as the end refers to the animal's own offspring, the beginning also refers to its own.

The Gemara rejects the analogy, stating that each case is different and the word 'וכן' (and thus) in the baraita refers only to the exemption from firstborn status, not to the identity of the offspring.

items.text: Rabbi Yochanan's ruling about a pig and its implications
items.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan's ruling about a pig and its implications
items.desc_en: Rabba bar bar Chanah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: If one saw a pig following a ewe, the offspring is exempt from firstborn status (like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel) but forbidden for eating (like the Rabbis). The Gemara questions this: if he is uncertain about the halakhah, why is it exempt? And if he is certain, why the unusual phrase 'until he comes and teaches righteousness to you'? The Gemara explains that Rabbi Yochanan was certain the halakhah follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, but was uncertain whether Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that a birth mother nurses or any mother nurses. The pig case is necessary because a pig nurses even non-birth offspring, so it teaches that even in such a case the exemption applies.

sub.text: Rabba bar bar Chanah in the name of Rabbi Yochanan
sub.text_en: Rabba bar bar Chanah in the name of Rabbi Yochanan
sub.desc_en: Rabba bar bar Chanah reports Rabbi Yochanan's ruling: a pig following a ewe exempts the offspring from firstborn status but forbids it for eating until Elijah comes.

The Gemara asks: the exemption from firstborn status follows whom? And the prohibition on eating follows whom? It answers: the exemption follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and the prohibition follows the Rabbis.
The Gemara objects: if the prohibition follows the Rabbis, why does Rabbi Yochanan say 'until he comes and teaches righteousness to you' instead of 'until the matter becomes known to you'?

The Gemara objects further: if Rabbi Yochanan were uncertain about the halakhah, why would he exempt from firstborn status? And how could he be uncertain, given his own rule that the halakhah follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel everywhere except three cases?

The Gemara answers: Rabbi Yochanan was certain the halakhah follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, but uncertain whether Rabban Shimon holds that only a birth mother nurses or any mother nurses; the Gemara then asks why the pig case was needed rather than a lamb case for the law of 'it and its young'.

The Gemara resolves: the pig case was necessary because a pig nurses even non-birth offspring, so it teaches that even in such a case the exemption applies, since there is a concern that the pig might nurse the lamb.

items.text: Rabbi Yochanan's unresolved question
items.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan's unresolved question
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes that Rabbi Yochanan said 'I require' (or 'I ask'), indicating that the doubt about whether a non-birth mother nurses remains unresolved.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that Rabbi Yochanan's statement 'I require' (or 'I ask') indicates that the doubt about whether a non-birth mother nurses remains unresolved.

items.text: שאלת אחרי בריבי על חזיר הכרוך אחר רחל
items.text_en: Question about a pig following a ewe
items.desc_en: Aḥai bar Ribi asks whether a pig that follows a ewe is considered a firstborn. The Gemara clarifies the inquiry: it concerns either the law of firstborn according to the Rabbis or the law of consumption according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. The question remains unresolved (teiku).
items.desc: אחרי בריבי שואל על חזיר ההולך אחר רחל: האם הרחמים מעידים על ייחוס הוולד לבכורה, והאם החזיר מותר באכילה. הגמרא מבררת את כוונת השאלה ומציגה ספקות בשתי הסוגיות, ומסיימת בתיקו.

sub.desc_en: Aḥai bar Ribi asks whether a pig that follows a ewe is considered a firstborn, and the Gemara initially questions the relevance of the inquiry.
sub.desc: אחרי בריבי שואל על חזיר ההולך אחר רחל, והגמרא מבררת מהו הספק: אם הוא על בכורה, היה צריך לשאול על טלה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies that the question applies either to the law of firstborn according to the Rabbis or to the law of consumption according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת שהשאלה כפולה: לעניין בכורה לפי רבנן, ולעניין אכילה לפי רשב''ג.

sub.text_en: Gemara's analysis of the firstborn aspect
sub.desc_en: The Gemara analyzes the firstborn aspect: even according to the Rabbis who say the ewe loves its offspring, does it love only its own kind or also a different species?
sub.desc: הגמרא מפרשת את הספק בבכורה: האם רחמי הרחל על החזיר מוכיחים שהוא מינה, או שמא מרחמת גם על שאינו מינה.

sub.text_en: Gemara's analysis of the consumption aspect
sub.desc_en: The Gemara analyzes the consumption aspect: even according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, does the ewe love only its own kind or also a different species?
sub.desc: הגמרא מפרשת את הספק באכילה: האם הרחמים מוכיחים שהחזיר מותר באכילה, ומסיימת בתיקו.

sub.desc_en: The question remains unresolved (תיקו).
sub.desc: הגמרא מפרשת את הספק באכילה: האם הרחמים מוכיחים שהחזיר מותר באכילה, ומסיימת בתיקו.

items.text: משנת רבי יוסי בן המשולם על תלישת שיער בבכור
items.text_en: Mishnah: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam's ruling
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam permits making a place with a hatchet on both sides of a firstborn and plucking the hair, as long as it is not moved from its place. Similarly, one may pluck hair to inspect a blemish.
items.desc: המשנה מביאה את דעת רבי יוסי בן המשולם: השוחט בכור מותר לתלוש שיער בסכין משני צדדי הצוואר, ובלבד שלא יזיז את השיער ממקומו, וכן מותר לתלוש שיער כדי לראות מקום מום.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam's ruling that one may make a place with a hatchet on both sides of a firstborn and pluck the hair, provided it is not moved from its place, and similarly one may pluck hair to inspect a blemish.
sub.desc: המשנה מביאה את דעת רבי יוסי בן המשולם: מותר לתלוש שיער בסכין משני צדדי הצוואר בעת שחיטת בכור, ובלבד שלא יזיז את השיער ממקומו, וכן מותר לתלוש שיער כדי לראות מקום מום.

items.text: גמרא: דין תלישת שיער ביום טוב
items.text_en: Gemara: Applying the ruling to Yom Tov
items.desc_en: Rav rules that the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam. The Gemara asks whether the same leniency applies on Yom Tov, debating whether plucking is considered shearing or merely an unintended act. Rav Huna initially sends them to inquire of Rav Ḥananel, who confirms Rav's ruling, and then Rav Huna permits it on Yom Tov. A supporting statement from Rav Ḥananya bar Shelemya in Rav's name is cited.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה את דברי רב שהלכה כרבי יוסי בן המשולם, ושואלת מה הדין ביום טוב. רב הונא שולח לשאול את רב חננאל, ומשיב שמותר לתלוש ביום טוב. רב חנניה בר שלמיה מוסר בשם רב שמותר.

sub.desc_en: Rav rules that the binding law (הלכה) follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam.
sub.desc: רב פוסק שהלכה כרבי יוסי בן המשולם.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks Rav Huna whether the same leniency applies on Yom Tov (a festival day).
sub.desc: רב פוסק שהלכה כרבי יוסי בן המשולם.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests one possible reason: Rabbi Yosei holds that plucking (תולש) is not considered shearing (גוזז), so on Yom Tov it would be forbidden as an act of uprooting something from its growth.
sub.desc: רב פוסק שהלכה כרבי יוסי בן המשולם.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara offers an alternative reason: Rabbi Yosei holds that plucking is indeed shearing, but he permits it because it is an unintended act (דבר שאין מתכוון), and on Yom Tov such an act is permitted.

sub.text_en: Rav Huna's instruction and Rav Ḥananel's response
sub.desc_en: Rav Huna sends the questioners to Rav Ḥananel, who confirms that Rav ruled the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam.
sub.desc: רב הונא שולח את השואלים לשאול את רב חננאל אם רב אמר הלכה כרבי יוסי בן המשולם.

sub.desc_en: Rav Huna rules that the same leniency applies on Yom Tov and it is permitted.
sub.desc: רב הונא שולח את השואלים לשאול את רב חננאל אם רב אמר הלכה כרבי יוסי בן המשולם.

sub.text_en: Rav Ḥananya bar Shelemya in Rav's name
sub.desc_en: A supporting statement is cited: Rav Ḥananya bar Shelemya reports in Rav's name that the same leniency applies on Yom Tov.
sub.desc: רב הונא שולח את השואלים לשאול את רב חננאל אם רב אמר הלכה כרבי יוסי בן המשולם.

items.text: Opening Mishnah excerpt
items.text_en: Opening Mishnah excerpt
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that plucking hair from a firstborn animal with a blemish is permitted.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that plucking hair from a firstborn animal with a blemish is permitted.

items.text: Gemara's challenge: Rav's apparent contradiction
items.text_en: Gemara's challenge: Rav's apparent contradiction
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions Rav's consistency: he forbids grinding a certain spice on a Festival, which seems to contradict his ruling here. The Gemara resolves that Rabbi Shimon would agree in that case due to the principle of 'inevitable consequence'.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara challenges Rav's consistency by citing a ruling of Rav forbidding grinding a certain spice on a Festival.
The Gemara resolves that in that case even Rabbi Shimon would agree due to the principle of inevitable consequence (פסיק רישיה ולא ימות).

items.text: Further challenge and resolution: Rav's actual view
items.text_en: Further challenge and resolution: Rav's actual view
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites conflicting traditions about Rav's ruling on the law following Rabbi Yehuda or Rabbi Shimon. It resolves that Rav holds 'an unintended act is forbidden', but plucking is not the same as shearing, and on a Festival it is permitted because it is an indirect uprooting.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara challenges Rav's position by citing conflicting traditions: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi reports Rav ruled like Rabbi Yehuda, while Rav Chanan bar Ami reports Shmuel ruled like Rabbi Shimon, and Rav Chiyya bar Avin teaches without names that Rav ruled like Rabbi Yehuda and Shmuel like Rabbi Shimon.

The Gemara resolves that Rav holds 'דבר שאין מתכוין (an unintended act) is forbidden', but plucking (תולש) is not the same as shearing (גוזז), and on a Festival it is permitted because it is an indirect uprooting (עוקר דבר מגידולו כלאחר יד).

items.text: דחיית הטענה שתלישה אינה גיזה
items.text_en: Objection: Plucking is indeed shearing
items.desc_en: The Gemara objects that plucking is considered shearing, citing a baraita where one who plucks a wing is liable for three sin-offerings. Resh Lakish explains that plucking is liable as shearing. The Gemara distinguishes a wing because that is its normal manner.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה מברייתא וריש לקיש שתלישה נחשבת גיזה לעניין שבת, ומתרצת שכנף שונה כי דרכה בכך, אך שיער אינו דרכו בתלישה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that plucking is indeed shearing, citing a baraita where one who plucks a wing is liable for three sin-offerings.
sub.desc: הגמרא מיישבת את הסתירה בדעת רב: הוא אוסר דבר שאין מתכוין, אך תלישה אינה נחשבת גיזה, וביום טוב ההיתר הוא משום שעוקר דבר מגידולו כלאחר יד.

sub.desc_en: Resh Lakish explains that plucking is liable as shearing, cutting as severing, and plucking as smoothing.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה מברייתא וריש לקיש שתלישה נחשבת גיזה לעניין שבת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara distinguishes a wing because that is its normal manner of plucking.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה מברייתא וריש לקיש שתלישה נחשבת גיזה לעניין שבת.

items.text: Rav and Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam: alignment and contradiction
items.text_en: Rav and Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam: alignment and contradiction
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam and vice versa, citing a baraita where Rabbi Yosei permits shearing a red heifer's hair with scissors. The Gemara attempts to distinguish the red heifer as not subject to shearing, but then notes that consecrated property is forbidden in shearing by rabbinic law. It concludes that the red heifer is uncommon.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam and whether Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam holds like Rav, implying that Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam would then hold that a non-intentional act (דבר שאין מתכוין) is forbidden.
A baraita is cited where Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam permits shearing the red heifer's hair with scissors, indicating he does not consider it a forbidden act of shearing.

The Gemara initially distinguishes the red heifer as not subject to shearing (לאו בת גיזה), but then cites a baraita that extends the prohibition of shearing to all consecrated animals through a verbal analogy.

The Gemara resolves that the red heifer is consecrated for Temple upkeep (קדשי בדק הבית), which is only rabbinically forbidden in shearing, and since the red heifer is uncommon (לא שכיחא), the rabbis did not apply their decree to it.

items.text: Proposal to redeem and shear the red heifer
items.text_en: Proposal to redeem and shear the red heifer
items.desc_en: The Gemara suggests redeeming the red heifer to non-sacred status, shearing it, then re-sanctifying it. It rejects this because its blood is expensive, and Shmuel's ruling that redemption can be done even with a small amount applies only after the fact, not initially.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara proposes redeeming the red heifer to non-sacred status, shearing it, then re-sanctifying it.
The Gemara objects that the red heifer's blood is expensive, making redemption impractical.
The Gemara proposes applying Shmuel's ruling that redemption can be done even with a small amount.
The Gemara rejects the proposal, noting that Shmuel's leniency applies only בדיעבד (after the fact), not לכתחילה (a-priori).

items.text: Alternative resolution: Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei, but not vice versa
items.text_en: Alternative resolution: Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei, but not vice versa
items.desc_en: The Gemara offers an alternative: Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam, but Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Rav.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara offers an alternative resolution: Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam, but Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Rav.

items.text: The law of plucking hair to examine a blemish
items.text_en: The law of plucking hair to examine a blemish
items.desc_en: The Mishnah teaches that one may pluck hair to examine a blemish, provided he does not move it from its place. Rav Ashi quotes Resh Lakish that this is only by hand, not with a tool. The Gemara clarifies a baraita about using a knife. Then it discusses whether the plucking is permitted initially or only after the fact, concluding from Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam's ruling that it is permitted initially.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that one may pluck hair provided he does not move it from its place.
Rav Ashi quotes Resh Lakish that the Mishnah's permission applies only by hand, but with a tool it is forbidden.
The Gemara objects by citing a baraita that permits clearing space with a cleaver (a tool).
The Gemara resolves the objection by emending the baraita to read 'for a cleaver' (i.e., one clears space with his hands for the cleaver, not with the cleaver itself).
The Gemara raises a dilemma whether the Mishnah's permission to pluck hair to examine a blemish is לכתחילה (the ideal standard) or only בדיעבד (after the fact).
Rabbi Yirmeya cites a baraita where Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam permits plucking entangled wool to show a blemish, indicating it is permitted לכתחילה (the ideal standard).
The Gemara concludes from the baraita that the plucking is permitted לכתחילה (the ideal standard).
Rav Mari notes that the Mishnah itself supports this conclusion with the phrase 'and likewise one plucks the hair to examine the place of a blemish.'
The Gemara questions what 'and likewise' refers to: if it refers to the prohibition of moving the hair, then it is unnecessary, since the case of slaughter already implies it.
The Gemara concludes that 'and likewise' must refer to the permission to pluck, not the restriction.
The Gemara confirms that the Mishnah permits plucking לכתחילה (the ideal standard).

items.text: משנת סיום: שיער שנשר מהבכור
items.text_en: Mishnah: Hair of a blemished firstborn that fell out
items.desc_en: The Mishnah presents a case: hair of a blemished firstborn that fell out and was placed in a window, then the animal was slaughtered. Akavya ben Mahalalel permits it.
items.desc: המשנה עוסקת בשיער של בכור בעל מום שנשר בעודו חי והונח בחלון, ולאחר מכן נשחט הבכור. עקביא בן מהללאל מתיר את השיער בהנאה, וחכמים אוסרים.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah presents the case of hair from a blemished firstborn that fell out and was placed in a window, then the animal was slaughtered; עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל (Akavya ben Mahalalel) permits the hair.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין שיער בכור בעל מום שנשר בעודו חי והונח בחלון, ולאחר שחיטת הבכור – עקביא בן מהללאל מתיר את השיער בהנאה.

items.text: Mishnah: Dispute about wool from a dead blemished firstborn and the law of dangling wool
items.text_en: Mishnah: Dispute about wool from a dead blemished firstborn and the law of dangling wool
items.desc_en: The Mishnah records Rabbi Yosei's clarification that Akavya ben Mahalalel permitted wool that fell off a blemished firstborn after death, while the Sages forbid it. It then states the rule for dangling wool: what appears with the shearing is permitted, what does not is forbidden.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah records Rabbi Yehuda's version of the dispute: Akavya ben Mahalalel permitted wool that fell from a blemished firstborn after death, while the Sages forbid it, and Rabbi Yosei corrects that the dispute is specifically about wool that fell before death and was left in a window.
The Mishnah states the rule for dangling wool on a firstborn: what appears with the shearing is permitted, what does not is forbidden.

items.text: Gemara's initial question and resolution of the Mishnah's wording
items.text_en: Gemara's initial question and resolution of the Mishnah's wording
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions the Mishnah's implication that in the case of a slaughtered animal it is permitted, asking why it would need to be stated. It resolves that the dispute is only about a dead animal, while all agree that slaughter permits the wool.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions the Mishnah's implication that in the case of a slaughtered animal it is permitted, asking why it would need to be stated if even a dead animal permits the wool.
The Gemara resolves that the dispute between Akavya and the Sages is only about a dead animal, while all agree that slaughter permits the wool.

items.text: ביאור מחלוקת עקיבא וחכמים על ידי ריש לקיש
items.text_en: Reish Lakish's distinction: dispute only when an expert permitted
items.desc_en: Rabbi Assi in the name of Reish Lakish states that the dispute between Akavya and the Sages applies only when an expert permitted the animal; otherwise all agree it is forbidden, due to a decree lest one delay slaughter.
items.desc: רבי אסי בשם ריש לקיש מבאר שהמחלוקת היא במקרה שהתירו מומחה, וחכמים גזרו שמא יבוא לשהתייה, ואילו עקיבא לא גזר. אבל בלא התירו מומחה, הכל מודים שאסור.

sub.desc_en: Reish Lakish resolves the dispute between Akavya and the Sages: it applies only when an expert permitted the animal, otherwise all agree it is forbidden due to a decree lest one delay slaughter.
sub.desc: רבי אסי בשם ריש לקיש מבאר שמחלוקת עקיבא וחכמים היא דווקא כשהתירו מומחה, מחשש שמא ישהה, אבל בלא התירו מומחה הכל מודים שאסור.

items.text: קושיית רב ששת על ריש לקיש ותירוץ רבא
items.text_en: Rav Sheishet's objection and resolution via the Mishnah of mixed wool
items.desc_en: Rav Sheishet raises an objection from a Mishnah about blemished animals that forbid wool in any amount, with Rabbi Yosei saying 'yevaker'. The Gemara explains that this refers to wool of a blemished firstborn mixed with non-sacred wool, and the dispute is between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei. Rava concludes that 'yevaker' means checking whether an expert permitted it.
items.desc: רב ששת מקשה מברייתא על דברי ריש לקיש, ומסביר רב נחמן בשם רבה בר אבוה שהברייתא עוסקת בתערובת גיזות של בכור בעל מום עם גיזות חולין, והמחלוקת היא בין רבי יהודה לרבי יוסי. רבא מתרץ ש'יבוקר' הכוונה לבדוק אם התירו מומחה.

sub.desc_en: Rav Sheishet raises an objection from a Mishnah stating that blemished animals forbid wool in any amount, with Rabbi Yosei saying 'yevaker' (he shall examine).
sub.desc: רב ששת מקשה מברייתא על דברי ריש לקיש, ששם נאמר שבעלי מומין אוסרים בכל שהוא ורבי יוסי אומר יבקר.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what 'yevaker' means, questioning whether it implies the first Tanna forbids even after examination.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מה פירוש 'יבקר', ומקשה שאם הכוונה לחפש את בעל המום, הרי התנא קמא לא אמר שאוסר.

sub.text: רב נחמן בשם רבה בר אבוה
sub.text_en: Rav Nachman citing Rabbah bar Avuha
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman citing Rabbah bar Avuha explains that the Mishnah deals with wool of a blemished firstborn mixed with non-sacred wool, and the dispute is between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei.
sub.desc: רב נחמן בשם רבה בר אבוה מסביר שהברייתא עוסקת בתערובת גיזות של בכור בעל מום עם גיזות חולין, והמחלוקת היא בין רבי יהודה לרבי יוסי.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks again what 'yevaker' means, suggesting it might refer to checking whether the blemish is permanent or temporary, even without expert permission.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: הרי הברייתא אומרת 'יבוקר', ומשמע שצריך לבדוק אם המום קבוע או עובר, אפילו בלא התרת מומחה, בניגוד לדברי ריש לקיש.

sub.desc_en: Rava resolves that 'yevaker' means checking whether an expert permitted it; if so, it is permitted, and if not, it is forbidden.
sub.desc: רבא מתרץ ש'יבוקר' הכוונה לבדוק אם התירו מומחה, ואם לא – אסור, ובכך מיישב את הברייתא עם דברי ריש לקיש.

items.text: Ravin's report and the dispute between Rabbi Yirmeya's and Rabbi Assi's versions
items.text_en: Ravin's report and the dispute between Rabbi Yirmeya's and Rabbi Assi's versions
items.desc_en: Ravin reports the matter to Rabbi Yirmeya, who criticizes the Babylonians for not knowing Rabbi Yochanan's view that the dispute is when one checked and did not find a blemish, based on a tannaitic dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Sages. Rabbi Assi cites Rabbi Yochanan differently, saying the dispute is when one checked and found a blemish, based on a dispute between Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. The Gemara explains the reasoning behind each position.

sub.desc_en: Ravin reports the matter before Rabbi Yirmeya, who criticizes the Babylonians for saying a dark teaching.
Rabbi Yirmeya states that they did not hear Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba's report in the name of Rabbi Yochanan that the dispute is when one checked and did not find a blemish.
The Gemara explains that the dispute is based on the tannaitic dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Sages regarding presumption of impurity.
The Sages say one must dig until reaching bedrock or virgin soil.
Rabbi Assi cites Rabbi Yochanan differently, saying the dispute is when one checked and found a blemish, based on a dispute between Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
The Gemara cites a baraita about a field with a lost grave, where Rabbi says the found grave is the lost one, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says the entire field must be checked.
The Gemara explains why Rabbi Assi and Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba each reject the other's version, based on the likelihood of a blemish disappearing or a new blemish appearing.

items.text: קושייה על ריש לקיש מברייתא על תולש צמר מבכור תם
items.text_en: Objection from a baraita about a perfect firstborn
items.desc_en: A baraita is cited stating that one who plucks wool from a perfect firstborn is forbidden even if a blemish later developed and it was slaughtered, because it was perfect at the time of plucking.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה על דברי ריש לקיש מברייתא האומרת שהתולש צמר מבכור תם, אפילו שנולד בו מום ושחטו, אסור. מכאן משמע שהאיסור תלוי בהיותו תם בתחילה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects by citing a baraita that forbids plucking wool from a perfect firstborn (תָּם), even if a blemish later developed and it was slaughtered, because the prohibition is based on its status at the time of plucking.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על ריש לקיש מברייתא האומרת שהתולש צמר מבכור תם, אפילו שנולד בו מום ושחטו, אסור, ומשמע שהאיסור תלוי בהיותו תם בתחילה.

items.text: תירוץ הגמרא לקושיית רבי אסי
items.text_en: Gemara's question on the Mishnah's implication
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions the Mishnah's ruling that a blemished animal is permitted even without expert permission, and notes that the Tanna calls such an animal 'tam' (unblemished) when not permitted by an expert.
items.desc: הגמרא מתרצת את הסתירה בין דברי רבי אסי לברייתא: התנא קורא לבהמה 'תם' כל זמן שלא התירוה מומחה, אף אם יש בה מום.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions the Mishnah's implication that a blemished animal is permitted even without expert permission.
The Tanna clarifies that wherever an expert did not permit it, the animal is still called 'tam' (unblemished).

items.text: ברייתא: מחלוקת עקביא בן מהללאל וחכמים
items.text_en: Baraita dispute between Akavya and the Sages
items.desc_en: A baraita presents a dispute about wool plucked from a firstborn: for a tam (unblemished) animal it is forbidden; for a blemished one, Akavya ben Mahalalel permits and the Sages forbid. Rabbi Yehuda limits Akavya's permission to wool that fell off and was placed in a window before slaughter. Rabbi Yosei adds that Abba Chalafta agrees it is permitted, but the Sages said to leave it in the window in case of hope; after slaughter all agree it is permitted, but after death the dispute remains.
items.desc: הברייתא מציגה מחלוקת בדין התולש צמר מבכור תם שנפל בו מום ונשחט, ובדין בכור בעל מום שתלש ממנו ואחר כך מת. רבי יהודה ורבי יוסי מצמצמים את המחלוקת למקרים שונים.

sub.desc_en: The baraita presents the initial dispute: for an unblemished firstborn, plucked wool is forbidden; for a blemished firstborn that died, Akavya ben Mahalalel permits and the Sages forbid.
Rabbi Yehuda limits Akavya's permission to wool that fell off and was placed in a window before slaughter, not to plucked wool from a dead animal.

Rabbi Yosei adds that Abba Chalafta agrees the wool is permitted after slaughter, but the Sages said to leave it in the window in case of hope; after slaughter all agree it is permitted, but after death the dispute remains.

items.text: קושיית הגמרא: רבי יוסי כתנא קמא
items.text_en: Gemara's analysis: Is the dispute about expert permission?
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes that Rabbi Yosei seems redundant with the first Tanna, and suggests the difference is whether expert permission was given: the first Tanna requires it, while Rabbi Yosei permits even without expert permission.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה שדברי רבי יוסי זהים לתנא קמא, ומציעה שהמחלוקת ביניהם היא בדין התירו מומחה: תנא קמא דורש היתר מומחה ורבי יוסי מתיר אף בלאו הכי.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: Rabbi Yosei's opinion seems identical to the first tanna's, so perhaps the real dispute between them concerns whether an expert deemed the animal permitted for slaughter.
The Gemara answers: The first tanna holds that expert permission is required, whereas Rabbi Yosei permits use of the wool even without expert permission.

items.text: רבא: שלוש מחלוקות בדבר
items.text_en: Rava's resolution: Three distinct disputes
items.desc_en: Rava rejects the previous answer and explains that all agree expert permission is required; rather, there are three disputes about whether the dispute applies after death or after slaughter. The first Tanna holds they dispute about death, and the same applies to slaughter. Rabbi Yehuda holds that after death all agree it is forbidden, and the dispute is about slaughter. Rabbi Yosei holds that after slaughter all agree it is permitted, and the dispute is about death.
items.desc: רבא דוחה את ההצעה וקובע שהכל מודים שצריך היתר מומחה, וקיימות שלוש מחלוקות בדבר: תנא קמא תולה מחלוקת עקביא וחכמים במת והוא הדין לשחטו; רבי יהודה תולה אותה בשחטו; ורבי יוסי תולה אותה במת.

sub.desc_en: Rava rejects the previous answer and establishes that all agree expert permission is required; he then explains that the three Tannaic positions represent three distinct disputes: the first Tanna holds they dispute about death (and the same applies to slaughter), Rabbi Yehuda holds that after death all agree it is forbidden and the dispute is about slaughter, and Rabbi Yosei holds that after slaughter all agree it is permitted and the dispute is about death.

Rava completes his resolution by detailing Rabbi Yehuda's and Rabbi Yosei's positions: Rabbi Yehuda holds that after death all agree it is forbidden and the dispute is about slaughter, while Rabbi Yosei holds that after slaughter all agree it is permitted and the dispute is about death.

items.text: Rav Nachman rules like Rabbi Yehuda
items.text_en: Rav Nachman rules like Rabbi Yehuda
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman rules the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda, citing a Mishnah in Bekhorot that supports his position: wool of a blemished firstborn that fell off and was placed in a window, then slaughtered, is disputed by Akavya and the Sages.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman rules the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda, citing a Mishnah in Bekhorot that supports his position: wool of a blemished firstborn that fell off and was placed in a window, then slaughtered, is disputed by Akavya and the Sages.

items.text: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak's proof from the Mishnah
items.text_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak's proof from the Mishnah
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak proves that the Mishnah's ruling about wool that appears with the shearing being permitted and not appearing being forbidden aligns only with Rabbi Yehuda's view that the dispute is about slaughter. The Gemara systematically eliminates other possibilities (Rabbi Yosei, Akavya, death scenario) and concludes it must be Rabbi Yehuda's position that the dispute is about slaughter.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak opens by asserting that the Mishnah's ruling (wool that appears with the shearing is permitted, that which does not appear is forbidden) supports his position.
The Gemara asks: Whose view does the Mishnah reflect? If it is Rabbi Yosei's view regarding slaughter, both Akavya and the Sages would permit the wool, contradicting the Mishnah's distinction.
The Gemara considers if the Mishnah reflects the death scenario: according to the Sages both would be forbidden, and according to Akavya the ruling would be reversed, neither matching the Mishnah.
The Gemara concludes it must be Rabbi Yehuda's view, but then asks: if it is the death scenario, both Akavya and the Sages would forbid, again not matching the Mishnah.

The Gemara resolves: it must be Rabbi Yehuda's view that the dispute is about slaughter, and the Mishnah follows the Sages who forbid the wool that does not appear with the shearing, proving the point.

items.text: בעיית רבי ינאי: צמר מעולה תמימה
items.text_en: Rabbi Yannai's inquiry about wool from a perfect olah
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yannai asks about wool that became detached from a perfect olah (burnt offering). He clarifies that for chatat and asham, which come for atonement, they are not left to grow wool; for bekhor and maaser, which are not for atonement, they are left. The question is about olah, which is for atonement but may be left.
items.desc: רבי ינאי שואל על צמר שניתלש מעולה תמימה מה דינו. הגמרא דוחה את האפשרות לתלוש במזיד, ומבארת שאין שאלה בחטאת ואשם (שאינם מתשהים) ולא בבכור ומעשר (שמתשהים), אלא בעולה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yannai asks about the status of wool that became detached from a perfect olah (burnt offering), clarifying that the question is not about active plucking (which is obviously forbidden) but about wool that fell off on its own.

sub.text: Gemara's clarification of the inquiry's scope
sub.text_en: Gemara's clarification of the inquiry's scope
sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains that for chatat and asham (sin and guilt offerings), which come for atonement (כפרה), the animal is not left to grow wool, so the question does not arise; for bekhor and maaser (firstborn and tithe), which are not for atonement, the animal is left, so the wool is permitted; the question is specifically about olah, which is for atonement yet may be left to grow wool.

items.text: בירור דין גיזת בכור תם שנפל בו מום
items.text_en: Gemara's question about delaying a firstborn for a burnt offering
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether one delays giving a firstborn animal to the priest if it could serve as a burnt offering, which also provides atonement. It attempts to resolve this from a baraita about plucking wool from a firstborn, but deflects the proof by distinguishing between plucking and natural falling. It concludes with the different teachings of Akavya and the Rabbis.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה האם יש חשש שישהה עולה תמימה, ומביאה ראיה מברייתא העוסקת בתולש צמר מבכור תם. הגמרא דוחה את הראיה ומבארת שהברייתא נשנתה בלשון 'תולש' כדי להראות כוחו דעקביא, והמשנה בלשון 'נשר' כדי להראות כוחן דרבנן.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether one delays giving a firstborn animal to the priest if it could serve as a burnt offering, which also provides atonement.
The Gemara attempts to resolve the question by citing a baraita about plucking wool from a firstborn, inferring that one does not delay a burnt offering.
The Gemara deflects the proof by asserting that even naturally shed wool is prohibited, and the baraita's wording highlights Akavya's lenient position on blemished animals.
The Gemara resolves that the mishna uses 'shed' to show the Rabbis' strictness, while the baraita uses 'plucks' to show Akavya's leniency.

items.text: הגדרת צמר המדולדל
items.text_en: Definition of detached wool (צמר המדולדל)
items.desc_en: The Mishnah mentions wool that is 'not visible with the shearing.' Rabbi Elazar quoting Resh Lakish defines it as wool whose root is turned toward its head. Rav Nathan bar Oshaya defines it as wool that does not compress with the shearing. The Gemara then explains why Resh Lakish does not accept the other opinion.
items.desc: הגמרא מבארת מהו צמר שאינו נראה עם הגיזה: ריש לקיש אומר כל שעיקרו הפוך כלפי ראשו, ורב נתן בר אושעיא אומר כל שאינו מתמעך עם הגיזה. הגמרא מסבירה מדוע ריש לקיש לא אמר כשיטת רב נתן בר אושעיא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what the Mishnah means by wool that is 'not visible with the shearing.'
רבי אליעזר (Rabbi Elazar) citing ריש לקיש (Resh Lakish) defines it as any strand whose root is overturned toward its head.
רב נתן בר אושעיא (Rav Nathan bar Oshaya) defines it as any strand that does not compress together with the fleece.
The Gemara asks why ריש לקיש (Resh Lakish) did not state his definition in accordance with רב נתן בר אושעיא (Rav Nathan bar Oshaya).
רבי אילעא (Rabbi Ile'a) explains that ריש לקיש (Resh Lakish) holds it is impossible for a fleece to lack dangling hairs, so he defines the prohibition more narrowly.

items.text: משנה: זמן חיוב ישראל לטפל בבכור
items.text_en: Mishnah: Obligation to care for a firstborn and its eating period
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states the minimum days an Israelite must care for a firstborn before giving it to a priest: 30 days for small cattle, 50 for large cattle (Rabbi Yose says 3 months for small). If the priest asks during that time, the Israelite may not give it. But if it has a blemish, the priest may take it immediately to eat. A firstborn is eaten within its year, and if a blemish develops within the year, it may be kept for up to 12 months, but only 30 days thereafter.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת עד כמה זמן חייב ישראל לטפל בבכור לפני נתינתו לכהן: בדקה שלושים יום ובגסה חמישים יום, ורבי יוסי אומר בדקה שלושה חודשים. עוד נקבע שאם אמר הכהן בתוך הזמן 'תנהו לי' אין נותנים לו, ואם הוא בעל מום מותר, וכן בזמן המקדש בתם. כמו כן הבכור נאכל שנה בשנה, ואם נולד בו מום בתוך שנתו רשאי לקיימו כל שנים עשר חודש, ואם לאחר מכן אינו רשאי לקיימו אלא שלושים יום.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens by asking until when an Israelite must tend to a בכור (firstborn) before giving it to the priest.
The Tanna Kamma answers: thirty days for small cattle and fifty days for large cattle.
רבי יוסי (Rabbi Yose) disagrees, saying that for small cattle the period is three months.
The Mishnah rules that if the priest asks for the animal within that period, the owner may not give it to him.
The Mishnah permits giving the animal immediately if it is a בעל מום (blemished) and the priest says he will eat it.
The Mishnah permits giving an unblemished animal during the Temple period if the priest says he will sacrifice it.
The Mishnah states that a בכור (firstborn) is eaten within its year, whether it is תם (unblemished) or בעל מום (blemished).
The Mishnah cites the verse 'לפני ה׳ אלהיך תאכלנו שנה בשנה' (you shall eat it before the Lord your God year by year) as the source.
The Mishnah rules that if a blemish develops within its first year, the owner may keep it for the entire twelve months.
The Mishnah rules that if the blemish develops after twelve months, the owner may keep it only thirty days.

items.text: Gemara: Scriptural derivation for the waiting period
items.text_en: Gemara: Scriptural derivation for the waiting period
items.desc_en: Rav Kahana attempts to derive the waiting period from a comparison between giving firstborn sons and firstborn animals. The Gemara suggests the opposite derivation, but the discussion is interrupted.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks for the scriptural source of the waiting periods for a firstborn animal, and Rav Kahana cites verses connecting the treatment of firstborn sons and animals.

The Gemara objects that the derivation could be reversed, arguing that the verse 'כן תעשה לשורך' (so shall you do to your ox) might refer to the immediately preceding context rather than the firstborn.
The discussion is interrupted mid-argument, leaving the objection unresolved.

items.text: Rava's derivation and a baraita supporting the Mishnah
items.text_en: Rava's derivation and a baraita supporting the Mishnah
items.desc_en: Rava derives the waiting period from the word 'תַּעֲשֶׂה' (you shall do), which adds an additional action for the ox (large cattle). The Gemara asks if it could be 60 days, and answers that the matter is left to the Sages. A baraita confirms this derivation.

sub.desc_en: Rava derives the waiting period for an ox from the word 'תַּעֲשֶׂה' (you shall do), which adds an additional action for the ox.
The Gemara objects that the additional action could imply 60 days instead of 50.
The Gemara resolves that the exact number is left to the Sages, who determined 50 days.
A baraita is cited that explicitly derives the waiting period from the verse and confirms that the matter is left to the Sages.

items.text: Tosefta elaborating on the Mishnah
items.text_en: Tosefta elaborating on the Mishnah
items.desc_en: The baraita repeats the Mishnah's ruling and adds Rabbi Yose's reason: because its care is extensive (its teeth are thin).

sub.text: Tosefta citing the Mishnah's framing question
sub.text_en: Tosefta citing the Mishnah's framing question
sub.desc_en: The baraita restates the Mishnah's question and the anonymous ruling: thirty days for a small animal, fifty days for a large one.
רבי יוסי (Rabbi Yose) disagrees, ruling three months for a small animal because its tending is extensive.
A תָּנָא (tanna) supplies the concrete reason for רבי יוסי's position: the animal's teeth are thin, so it needs more care.

items.text: Reason for not giving the firstborn to the priest early
items.text_en: Reason for not giving the firstborn to the priest early
items.desc_en: Rav Sheshet explains that if the Israelite gives the firstborn to the priest during the waiting period, it appears as if the priest is assisting in the threshing floor (a forbidden practice). A baraita expands on the prohibition of priests, Levites, and poor people receiving tithes as payment for assisting in such labor, citing verses warning against profaning sacred things.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the owner may not give the firstborn to the priest within the waiting period.
Rav Sheshet explains that giving the firstborn early makes the priest appear like one who assists at the threshing floor for payment, which is prohibited.

A baraita expands the prohibition: priests, Levites, and poor people who assist in various labor settings may not receive תרומה (priestly portion) or מעשר (tithe) as wages, and doing so profanes the sacred items, citing verses from Malachi and Numbers.
The Gemara explains why the baraita cites a second verse: to show that the offense carries a death penalty, not just desecration.

items.text: Opening Mishnah and its explanation
items.text_en: Opening Mishnah and its explanation
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that the benefit of choosing the priest (tovat hana'ah) belongs to the owner. It gives an example: an Israelite who set aside terumah from his produce, and another Israelite found him and offered a sela to give it to his priest-daughter's son—this is permitted. But if the recipient was a priest giving to another priest, it is forbidden.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states the rule that the benefit of choosing the priest (tovat hana'ah) belongs to the owner, and illustrates with a case of an Israelite giving terumah to a priest through another Israelite, which is permitted, but forbidden if both are priests.

items.text: Gemara's question and answer about the Mishnah's omission
items.text_en: Gemara's question and answer about the Mishnah's omission
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Tanna did not mention the other priestly gifts (matnot kehuna). It answers that terumah has sanctity of the body (kedushat haguf), so since it cannot be redeemed, one will not come to err with it. But the other gifts have sanctity of monetary value (kedushat damim), so one might err with them, as their sanctity can be redeemed for four zuz, and one might treat them as unconsecrated.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Tanna (Mishnah) only mentions terumah and not the other priestly gifts (מתנות כהונה).
The Gemara answers that terumah has inherent sanctity (קדושת הגוף) and cannot be redeemed, so there is no risk of error.
The Gemara explains that other priestly gifts have monetary sanctity (קדושת דמים) and can be redeemed, leading to potential confusion and treating them as חולין (ordinary produce).

items.text: תרומת חוץ לארץ – מותרת בסיוע בבית הגרנות
items.text_en: Rava's statement on terumah from outside Israel
items.desc_en: Rava states that terumah from outside Israel (terumat hutz la'aretz) does not have the prohibition of a priest assisting at the threshing floor (kohen hamesaye'a beveit hageranot). Rav Chama gave it to his attendant.
items.desc: רבא אומר שאין איסור 'כהן המסייע בבית הגרנות' בתרומת חוץ לארץ, ורב חמא נותן תרומת חוץ לארץ לשמשו כשכר.

sub.desc_en: Rava rules that the prohibition of a priest assisting at the threshing floor (כוהן המסייע בבית הגרנות) does not apply to terumah from outside the Land of Israel.
sub.desc: רבא פוסק שתרומת חוץ לארץ אינה אסורה משום כהן המסייע בבית הגרנות.

sub.desc_en: Rav Chama would give terumah from outside the Land to his attendant, illustrating the lenient practice.
sub.desc: רבא פוסק שתרומת חוץ לארץ אינה אסורה משום כהן המסייע בבית הגרנות.

items.text: Shmuel's statement on nullification of terumah from outside Israel
items.text_en: Shmuel's statement on nullification of terumah from outside Israel
items.desc_en: Shmuel says that terumah from outside Israel is nullified in a majority (bateilah berov). Rabbah would nullify it in a majority and eat it during his days of impurity.

sub.desc_en: Shmuel rules that terumah from outside the Land is nullified by a majority (בטילה ברוב).
Rabbah would nullify such terumah by a majority and eat it even in his state of ritual impurity.

items.text: Rav Huna's practice with terumah wine
items.text_en: Rav Huna's practice with terumah wine
items.desc_en: Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua, when he encountered terumah wine, would mix two measures of unconsecrated wine and one measure of terumah wine, and then take one measure. From then on, he would mix one and take one.

sub.desc_en: Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua would mix two measures of חולין (ordinary wine) with one measure of terumah wine and take one, demonstrating nullification by majority.
Later, Rav Huna would mix one measure of terumah with one of חולין and take one, showing even greater leniency.

items.text: הקלות נוספות בתרומת חוץ לארץ: אכילה ואחר כך הפרשה, ואיסור רק בטומאה היוצאת מהגוף
items.text_en: Shmuel's additional leniencies for terumah from outside Israel
items.desc_en: Shmuel states two leniencies: one may eat and then separate terumah from outside Israel, and it is only forbidden to one from whom impurity emanates from his body (e.g., a zav), and only for eating, not for touching.
items.desc: שמואל מתיר לאכול תחילה ואחר כך להפריש תרומת חוץ לארץ, ואוסר אותה רק למי שטומאתו יוצאת מגופו (באכילה, לא בנגיעה).

sub.desc_en: Shmuel states that one may eat terumah from outside Israel and then separate it afterwards.
sub.desc: שמואל מתיר לאכול תחילה ואחר כך להפריש תרומת חוץ לארץ.

sub.desc_en: Shmuel adds that terumah from outside Israel is only forbidden to one whose impurity emanates from his body, and only for eating, not for touching.
sub.desc: שמואל מוסיף שתרומת חוץ לארץ אסורה רק למי שטומאתו יוצאת מגופו, ובאכילה דווקא, לא בנגיעה.

items.text: הלכה למעשה: נדה מפרשת חלה בחוץ לארץ
items.text_en: Ravina's practical ruling for challah from outside Israel
items.desc_en: Ravina concludes that a niddah may cut challah (the dough offering) and a minor priest may eat it. If there is no minor priest, she takes it at the beginning of the baking, throws it into the oven, and then separates another challah so that the law of challah is not forgotten, and an adult priest eats it.
items.desc: רבינא פוסק שנדה יכולה להפריש חלה בחוץ לארץ, וקטן אוכלה. אם אין קטן, זורקה לתנור ומפרישה חלה אחרת כדי שלא תשתכח תורת חלה, וגדול אוכלה.

sub.desc_en: Ravina rules that a menstruant woman may cut חלה (challah) and a minor priest may eat it; if no minor priest is available, she throws it into the oven and then separates another חלה to preserve the institution of חלה, which an adult priest may eat.
sub.desc: רבינא פוסק הלכה למעשה שנדה מפרשת חלה בחוץ לארץ, קטן אוכלה, ואם אין קטן – זורקה לתנור ומפרישה חלה אחרת כדי שלא תשתכח תורת חלה, וגדול אוכלה.

items.text: שאלה: טמא מת וטבילה לאכילת תרומת חוץ לארץ
items.text_en: Story of Rav Nachman, Rav Amram, and Rami bar Chama
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman, Rav Amram, and Rami bar Chama were traveling on a boat. Rav Amram went to relieve himself. A woman came and asked them: May one who is impure from a corpse immerse and eat terumah from outside Israel? Rav Nachman said to Rami bar Chama...
items.desc: רב נחמן ורמי בר חמא נשאלים על ידי אשה האם טמא מת יכול לטבול ולאכול תרומת חוץ לארץ. התשובה נקטעת.

sub.desc_en: A narrative describes Rav Nachman, Rav Amram, and Rami bar Chama traveling on a boat; a woman asks whether a person impure from a corpse may immerse and eat terumah from outside the Land.
sub.desc: האשה שואלת את רב נחמן ורמי בר חמא האם טמא מת יכול לטבול ולאכול תרומת חוץ לארץ.

sub.text_en: Rav Nachman's question to Rami bar Chama
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman turns to Rami bar Chama to address the woman's question.
sub.desc: האשה שואלת את רב נחמן ורמי בר חמא האם טמא מת יכול לטבול ולאכול תרומת חוץ לארץ.

sub.text_en: Rav Nachman to Rami bar Chama
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman turned to Rami bar Chama, setting up the next exchange.
sub.desc: האשה שואלת את רב נחמן ורמי בר חמא האם טמא מת יכול לטבול ולאכול תרומת חוץ לארץ.

items.text: דין טמא מת האוכל תרומת חו"ל
items.text_en: Gemara's discussion on immersion for terumah outside Israel
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether immersion is effective for a tamei met to eat terumah outside Israel. Ramy bar Chama advises not to heed the elder, then Rav Amram reports Rav's ruling that a tamei met may immerse and eat terumah outside Israel, but Mar Zutra in the name of Rav Sheshet rules that only a tamei sheretz may do so, and the halakha does not follow either opinion.
