items.desc: רב עמרם מביא בשם רב שטמא מת טובל ואוכל בתרומת חו"ל, אך הגמרא פוסקת שאין הלכה כמותו. גם דעת רב ששת נדחית.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether immersion alone is effective for a tamei met (one impure from a corpse) to eat terumah outside Israel, given that the purification process requires the sprinkling of the ashes of the red heifer (הזאה).
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: וכי יש לנו אפר פרה להזות? ומביאה את דברי רמי בר חמא שאמר שלא יחושו לזקן.

sub.desc_en: Ramy bar Chama advises not to heed the elder (the one who raised the question), implying the ruling is lenient.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: וכי יש לנו אפר פרה להזות? ומביאה את דברי רמי בר חמא שאמר שלא יחושו לזקן.

sub.desc_en: Rav Amram reports Rav's ruling that a tamei met (one impure from a corpse) may immerse and eat terumah outside Israel.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: וכי יש לנו אפר פרה להזות? ומביאה את דברי רמי בר חמא שאמר שלא יחושו לזקן.

sub.desc_en: Mar Zutra in the name of Rav Sheshet rules that only a tamei sheretz (one impure from a creeping creature) may immerse and eat terumah outside Israel, and the halakha does not follow either opinion.
sub.desc: הגמרא פוסקת שאין הלכה כרב, ומביאה את דברי מר זוטרא בשם רב ששת.

items.text: Gemara's inference from the Mishnah
items.text_en: Gemara's inference from the Mishnah
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes that the Mishnah's phrase 'a blemish was born within its year' implies that we count the animal's own year, not the calendar year. It then asks for the source of this rule.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara infers from the Mishnah's phrase 'a blemish was born within its year' that we count the animal's own year, not the calendar year.
The Gemara asks for the scriptural source of this rule.

items.text: Rav Yehuda's answer from the verse
items.text_en: Rav Yehuda's answer from the verse
items.desc_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav cites the verse 'before the Lord your God you shall eat it year by year' and explains that the year referred to is the year of the firstborn itself.

sub.text: Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav
sub.text_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav
sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav cites the verse 'before the Lord your God you shall eat it year by year' and explains that the year referred to is the year of the firstborn itself.

items.text: לימוד 'שנה בשנה' – שני ימים ולילה אחד
items.text_en: Devei Rav's teaching on two days and one night
items.desc_en: Devei Rav taught from the phrase 'year by year' that the firstborn is eaten for one day in one year and one day in the next, meaning it is eaten for two days and one night.
items.desc: דבי רב דורשים 'שנה בשנה' שהבכור נאכל לשני ימים ולילה אחד, בדומה לשלמים.

sub.desc_en: Devei Rav teaches from the verse 'שָׁנָה בְּשָׁנָה' (year by year) that the firstborn is eaten for two days and one night.
sub.desc: דבי רב דורשים את הפסוק 'שנה בשנה' ללמד שהבכור נאכל לשני ימים ולילה אחד, בדומה לשלמים.

items.text: מקור שנתו של הבכור מקדשים
items.text_en: Source for Devei Rav's derivation
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks how Devei Rav derived this, and explains that they learned from sacrifices. Rav Acha bar Yaakov cites the verse 'a lamb in its first year' to show that the year is the animal's own year, not the world's count.
items.desc: הגמרא מבארת שדבי רב למדו שנת הבכור מקדשים, וקדשים עצמם נלמדים מ'כבש בן שנתו' – שנתו שלו.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks from where Devei Rav derived that the year is counted from the animal's birth.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהיכן דבי רב למדו ששנת הבכור נמנית משעת לידתו, וממשיכה לשאול מהיכן למדו זאת בקדשים עצמם.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that Devei Rav learned from sacrifices, then asks how the sacrifices themselves derive this.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהיכן דבי רב למדו ששנת הבכור נמנית משעת לידתו, וממשיכה לשאול מהיכן למדו זאת בקדשים עצמם.

sub.desc_en: Rav Acha bar Yaakov cites the verse 'כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ' (a lamb in its first year) to prove that the year is the animal's own year, not the world's count.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהיכן דבי רב למדו ששנת הבכור נמנית משעת לידתו, וממשיכה לשאול מהיכן למדו זאת בקדשים עצמם.

items.text: מקור אכילת הבכור לשני ימים ולילה אחד
items.text_en: Rav's source for two days and one night
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks how Rav derived that the firstborn is eaten for two days and one night. It answers that the verse 'and their flesh shall be yours, like the breast of the wave offering and like the right thigh' compares the firstborn to the breast and thigh of a peace offering, which are eaten for two days and one night.
items.desc: רב למד מהפסוק 'ובשרם יהיה לך כחזה התנופה' שהבכור נאכל כשני ימים ולילה אחד, כשלמים.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks from where Rav derived that the firstborn is eaten for two days and one night.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהיכן לומד רב שהבכור נאכל לשני ימים ולילה אחד.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that Rav derived it from the verse comparing the firstborn to the breast and thigh of a peace offering, which are eaten for two days and one night.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהיכן לומד רב שהבכור נאכל לשני ימים ולילה אחד.

items.text: מחלוקת על זמן אכילת בכור: לימוד מ'והיה לך'
items.text_en: Continuation of the dispute about the source for the blemished firstborn
items.desc_en: The Gemara continues to analyze the biblical derivation for the law of a blemished firstborn. Each 'V'idakh' (and the other) offers a different interpretation of the verses, arguing that the Torah adds a special status for the blemished firstborn or that the verse teaches that it is given to the priest.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה במקור הדין שבכור נאכל לשני ימים ולילה אחד. יש הסוברים שלומדים מ'והיה לך' שמוסיף הויה אחרת, ויש החולקים ומפרשים את הפסוק לעניין בכור בעל מום.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that the other side could derive the law from the breast and thigh of the thanksgiving offering.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על חכמי בית רב: אם לומדים זמן אכילת בכור מ'חזה ושוק', הרי אפשר לטעות ולומר שמדובר בחזה ושוק של תודה הנאכלים ליום ולילה אחד בלבד.

sub.desc_en: The first answer argues that the verse 'לְךָ יִהְיֶה' adds a special status for the blemished firstborn.
sub.desc: רב יהודה משיב שהפסוק 'לך יהיה' מוסיף הויה אחרת בבכור, כלומר זמן אכילה נוסף, ואין ללמוד מתודה.

sub.desc_en: The second answer argues that the verse 'יִהְיֶה לָּךְ' teaches that a blemished firstborn is given to the priest, a rule not found elsewhere in the Torah.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על חכמי בית רב: אפשר לפרש את 'יהיה לך' כלמד על בכור בעל מום שנותנו לכהן, ולא לעניין זמן אכילה.

sub.desc_en: The third answer argues that the verse 'וּבְשָׂרָם' includes both unblemished and blemished firstborns, while the other side says it refers to all firstborns of Israel.
sub.desc: רב יהודה משיב שהפסוק 'ובשרם' מלמד על אחד תם ואחד בעל מום, ואילו חכמי בית רב דוחים שזה נאמר על בכורות של כל ישראל בלבד.

items.text: Question about the time limit for keeping a blemished firstborn
items.text_en: Question about the time limit for keeping a blemished firstborn
items.desc_en: The Gemara raises a question about the Mishnah's statement: if a blemish appears within the first year, one may keep the animal for twelve months. The question is whether this means that after the year, one may keep it for thirty days, or that only if the blemish appears within the year may one keep it for twelve months, but if it appears after the year, one may keep it only for thirty days.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a question about the Mishnah's statement: whether the permission to keep a blemished firstborn for twelve months applies only when the blemish appears within the year, or whether after the year one may keep it for thirty days.

items.text: Bringing a baraita to resolve the question
items.text_en: Bringing a baraita to resolve the question
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita that discusses a firstborn in the present time. It states that before it is shown to a sage, one may keep it for two or three years. After it is shown, if a blemish appears within the year, one may keep it for twelve months; after the year, one may not keep it even for a day, but due to returning lost property to its owner, they said one may keep it for thirty days.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita that rules: for a firstborn in the present time, before it is shown to a sage one may keep it two or three years; after it is shown, if a blemish appears within the year one may keep it twelve months.
The baraita concludes: after the year one may not keep it even a day, but due to returning lost property to its owner they said one may keep it thirty days.

items.text: Further question about the thirty days
items.text_en: Further question about the thirty days
items.desc_en: The Gemara continues to question: Are the thirty days after the year, or before the year?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a further question: Are the thirty days granted after the year or before the year?

items.text: Bringing another baraita and Rabbi Elazar's statement
items.text_en: Bringing another baraita and Rabbi Elazar's statement
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita: If a blemish appeared on the fifteenth day within the year, they complete for him fifteen days after the year. This supports Rabbi Elazar, who says that they give him thirty days from the hour the blemish appeared. Another version: Rabbi Elazar derives from a verse that for a blemish within the year, they give thirty days after the year.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita: if a blemish appeared on the fifteenth day within the year, they complete for him fifteen days after the year, and concludes that this supports Rabbi Elazar's position.

sub.text: Alternative version of Rabbi Elazar's statement
sub.text_en: Alternative version of Rabbi Elazar's statement
sub.desc_en: An alternative version: Rabbi Elazar derives from the verse 'לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה' that the days considered a year are thirty days, giving thirty days after the year for a blemish within the year.

items.text: Refutation of Rabbi Elazar
items.text_en: Refutation of Rabbi Elazar
items.desc_en: The Gemara raises an objection from the baraita: If a blemish appeared on the fifteenth day within the year, they complete for him fifteen days after the year. This implies completion, yes, but giving from scratch, no. This is a refutation of Rabbi Elazar.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita: if a blemish appeared on the fifteenth day within the year, they complete for him fifteen days after the year — implying completion (השלמה) but not giving from scratch (מתנה), which refutes Rabbi Elazar's position that one gives thirty days from the moment the blemish appeared.

items.text: Mishnah: Slaughtering a firstborn and showing its blemish
items.text_en: Mishnah: Slaughtering a firstborn and showing its blemish
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states: One who slaughters a firstborn and shows its blemish – Rabbi Yehuda permits it, Rabbi Meir says: Since it was slaughtered without the permission of an expert, it is forbidden. One who is not an expert and sees a firstborn, and it is slaughtered on his word – it must be buried, and he pays from his own pocket.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens with the case of one who slaughters a firstborn and then shows its blemish, presenting the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda (permits) and Rabbi Meir (forbids because it was slaughtered without expert permission).
The Mishnah adds the rule for a non-expert who sees a firstborn and it is slaughtered on his word: the animal must be buried and he pays from his own pocket.

items.text: Gemara's explanation of the dispute and a supporting baraita
items.text_en: Gemara's explanation of the dispute and a supporting baraita
items.desc_en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah explains that everyone agrees that blemishes of the eye (דוקין שבעין) are forbidden because they change. The dispute is only about blemishes of the body: Rabbi Meir decrees that blemishes of the body are forbidden because of blemishes of the eye, while Rabbi Yehuda does not decree. A baraita supports this, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak adds a clarification.

sub.desc_en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah explains the dispute: all agree that blemishes of the eye (דוקין שבעין) are forbidden because they change, and the dispute is only about blemishes of the body, where Rabbi Meir decrees them forbidden due to blemishes of the eye and Rabbi Yehuda does not.

A baraita supports this: Rabbi Yehuda permits blemishes of the body but forbids those of the eye, while Rabbi Meir forbids both, and the gemara clarifies that the baraita's phrase 'because they change' actually means 'because of the changing ones' (i.e., blemishes of the eye).
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak adds a clarification (the content of which is not fully given in the excerpt, but the move marks his statement).

items.text: Inference from the Mishnah that Rabbi Meir imposes a penalty
items.text_en: Inference from the Mishnah that Rabbi Meir imposes a penalty
items.desc_en: The Gemara infers from the Mishnah's phrasing that Rabbi Meir penalizes a non-expert who slaughtered a blemished firstborn without authorization, concluding that the mishnah supports this view.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara infers from the Mishnah's phrasing that Rabbi Meir penalizes a non-expert who slaughtered a blemished firstborn without authorization.

items.text: Inquiry about whether all witnesses change their testimony
items.text_en: Inquiry about whether all witnesses change their testimony
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether all witnesses change their testimony or only some, and the practical difference for relying on witnesses. Rabbi Yoshiya's statement that there are both reliable and unreliable witnesses resolves the inquiry.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks whether the reason witnesses are distrusted is that all change their testimony, or only some change while others remain reliable.
The Gemara clarifies the practical difference: if all change, they are all liars; if only some change, we can still rely on the others.

sub.text: Rabba bar bar Chana citing Rabbi Yoshiya
sub.text_en: Rabba bar bar Chana citing Rabbi Yoshiya
sub.desc_en: Rabba bar bar Chana reports that Rabbi Yoshiya showed him specific witnesses who change, implying that only some witnesses change their testimony, not all.

items.text: Mishnah about a non-expert who slaughtered a firstborn
items.text_en: Mishnah about a non-expert who slaughtered a firstborn
items.desc_en: The mishnah states that if a non-expert saw a firstborn and it was slaughtered on his word, the animal is buried and he pays from his own pocket. The Gemara questions whether this supports Rabbi Meir's view, but deflects that it might refer to eye blemishes, which are universally accepted.

sub.desc_en: The mishnah states that a non-expert who saw a firstborn and it was slaughtered on his word must bury it and pay from his own pocket, and the Gemara deflects the suggestion that this supports Rabbi Meir by noting it may refer to eye blemishes, which are universally accepted.

items.text: Payment scale for a non-expert and the reason for it
items.text_en: Payment scale for a non-expert and the reason for it
items.desc_en: The baraita specifies that the non-expert pays a quarter for a small animal and half for a large one. Rav Pappa explains this is based on the amount of loss, and Rav Huna bar Manoach in the name of Rav Acha bar Ika adds that the decree was due to goat herders.

sub.desc_en: The baraita states the payment scale: a quarter for a small animal and half for a large one.
The gemara asks for the reason behind this differential payment scale.
Rav Pappa explains that the scale corresponds to the amount of loss: a large animal causes greater loss, a small one lesser loss.
The gemara objects: if the reason is the loss, why not pay exactly according to the loss rather than a fixed fraction?

sub.text: Rav Huna bar Manoach citing Rav Acha bar Ika
sub.text_en: Rav Huna bar Manoach citing Rav Acha bar Ika
sub.desc_en: Rav Huna bar Manoach in the name of Rav Acha bar Ika resolves that the fixed scale is a decree due to goat herders, who might otherwise cause excessive loss.

items.text: Mishnah about a judge's erroneous ruling
items.text_en: Mishnah about a judge's erroneous ruling
items.desc_en: The mishnah states that if a judge errs in a ruling, his action stands but he pays from his own pocket, unless he is an expert appointed by the court, in which case he is exempt.

sub.desc_en: The mishnah states the law of a judge who errs: his action stands but he pays from his own pocket, unless he is an expert appointed by the court, in which case he is exempt.

items.text: Gemara's analysis of the judge's liability
items.text_en: Gemara's analysis of the judge's liability
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether the mishnah supports Rabbi Meir's view on indirect damage. Rabbi Ila'a explains that the case involves physical action. The Gemara then clarifies scenarios for each clause, with Ravina explaining that acquitting a liable party involves returning a pledge.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks whether the mishnah's ruling about a judge who errs supports Rabbi Meir's view that one is liable for indirect damage (גרמא).
Rabbi Ila'a in the name of Rav answers that the mishnah refers to a case where the judge physically handled the property, not mere indirect causation.
The Gemara questions how the case of acquitting a liable party (זיכה את החייב) can involve physical action, since the judge merely declares him exempt.
Ravina explains that the judge had taken a pledge from the liable party and returned it to him, thus physically causing the loss.
The Gemara clarifies the remaining clauses: declaring pure items impure involves touching them with a creeping animal, and declaring impure items pure involves mixing them with his own produce.

items.text: Story of Rabbi Tarfon and the blemished cow
items.text_en: Story of Rabbi Tarfon and the blemished cow
items.desc_en: The mishnah recounts that Rabbi Tarfon fed a cow whose womb was removed to dogs, and the sages permitted it. Rabbi Tarfon lamented his loss, but Rabbi Akiva told him he was exempt as an expert appointed by the court.

sub.desc_en: The mishnah recounts the case of a cow whose womb was removed, which Rabbi Tarfon fed to dogs, and the sages in Yavneh permitted it.
Todos the physician testifies that in Alexandria, cows and sows have their womb removed to prevent birth, supporting the permissibility of the blemished cow.
Rabbi Tarfon laments his loss, but Rabbi Akiva reassures him that as an expert appointed by the court (מומחה לבית דין), he is exempt from payment.

items.text: Gemara's objection and resolution regarding Rabbi Tarfon
items.text_en: Gemara's objection and resolution regarding Rabbi Tarfon
items.desc_en: The Gemara objects that Rabbi Tarfon should have been required to return the cow because he erred in a matter of Mishnah. The Gemara explains that Rabbi Akiva gave two reasons: first, the error was in a matter of Mishnah and should be reversed, but second, even if it was a judgment error, as an expert he is exempt from payment.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that Rabbi Tarfon should have been required to return the cow because he erred in a matter of Mishnah, which is reversible.

The Gemara explains that Rabbi Akiva gave two reasons: first, the error was in a matter of Mishnah and should be reversed, but second, even if it was a judgment error, as an expert Rabbi Tarfon is exempt from payment.

items.text: נוטל שכר לראות בכורות – אין שוחטין על פיו
items.text_en: Mishnah about a paid examiner of firstborns
items.desc_en: The mishnah states that one who takes payment to examine firstborns cannot have animals slaughtered on his word unless he is an expert appointed by the court.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת שהנוטל שכר לראות בכורות אין שוחטין על פיו אלא אם כן הוא מומחה, משום חשש שהשכר משפיע על שיקול דעתו.

sub.desc_en: The mishnah rules that one who takes payment to examine firstborns cannot have animals slaughtered on his word unless he is an expert appointed by the court.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין הנוטל שכר לראות בכורות, שאין שוחטין על פיו אלא אם כן הוא מומחה.

items.text: Opening Mishnah: Payment for animal inspection
items.text_en: Opening Mishnah: Payment for animal inspection
items.desc_en: The Mishnah describes that in Yavneh, the Sages permitted a certain person to take payment for inspecting animals: four issar for small cattle and six for large, whether the animal was unblemished or blemished.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that in Yavneh, the Sages permitted a certain person to take payment for inspecting animals: four issar for small cattle and six for large, whether the animal was unblemished or blemished.

items.text: Gemara: Reason for the payment and concern about suspicion
items.text_en: Gemara: Reason for the payment and concern about suspicion
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks why payment is taken, explaining that the blemished animal requires more work. It questions why payment is also taken for unblemished animals, answering that otherwise people would suspect the inspector of taking a bribe to declare a blemished animal as unblemished. It then addresses a counter-argument that people might think an unblemished animal is actually blemished, concluding that the Sages instituted payment only once, not twice.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the fee differs between small and large cattle, and answers that it is due to the difference in labor involved.

The Gemara questions why the Mishnah includes both a blemished and an unblemished animal: for a blemished animal, the payment is justified because the inspector permits it for use, but for an unblemished animal, people might suspect that the inspector is declaring it blemished just to collect the fee.
The Gemara answers that the same suspicion could arise in reverse, but the Sages instituted the fee only once (for the initial inspection), not twice, so the concern is mitigated.
The Gemara resolves that the Sages instituted payment only once, not twice, so the concern about a second fee is unfounded.

items.text: משנת שכר דין, עדות והזיה
items.text_en: Mishnah: Payment for judging, testifying, and purification
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that one who takes payment to judge renders his judgments void; to testify, his testimony is void; to sprinkle and sanctify the purification water, his water is considered cave water and his ash is ash from the stove. However, if he is a priest, he may be paid to become impure for his terumah, and if he is an elder, he may be paid to ride on a donkey, with his wage being that of a laborer.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת שהנוטל שכר לדין – דיניו בטלים, לעדות – עדותו בטלה, להזות ולקדש – מימיו כמי מערה ואפרו כאפר מקלה. עם זאת, מותר לתת שכר כפועל לכהן או לזקן שנטמאו או טרחו עבור בעל הבכור.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that one who takes payment for judging renders his judgments void, for testifying renders his testimony void, and for sprinkling and sanctifying renders his water as cave water and his ash as oven ash.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין הנוטל שכר לדון, להעיד או להזות ולקדש, שפעולותיו בטלות.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah adds that if the recipient is a priest, the one who pays him may defile him from his terumah, and if he is an elder, he may transport him on a donkey and pay him as a laborer.
sub.desc: המשנה מוסיפה חריג: מותר לתת שכר כפועל לכהן שנטמא או לזקן שטרח, כפיצוי על הפסדם.

items.text: מקור איסור שכר לימוד תורה
items.text_en: Gemara: Source for teaching Torah for free
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites Rav Yehuda quoting Rav, deriving from the verse 'See, I have taught you' that just as Moses taught for free, so too must one teach for free. A baraita adds that if one cannot find free teaching, he may teach for a fee, but he may not sell the Torah he learned, as per the verse 'Buy truth, and do not sell it'.
items.desc: רב יהודה בשם רב דורש את הפסוק 'ראה למדתי אתכם' – מה אני בחינם, אף אתם בחינם. ברייתא מוסיפה: אם לא מצא בחינם – ילמד בשכר, אך לא ימכור את התורה לאחר שלמדה בשכר.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks the source for the rule that one must teach Torah for free, and Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav cites the verse 'See, I have taught you…' to derive that just as Moses taught for free, so too must others.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מה מקור האיסור לקחת שכר לדון.

sub.desc_en: A baraita supports this with the verse 'As the Lord my God commanded me,' and further derives that if one cannot find free teaching, he may teach for a fee (from 'Emet k'neh'), but may not sell it (from 'Emet k'neh ve'al timkor').
sub.desc: ברייתא תומכת בדרשה: 'כאשר צוני ה' אלהי' – מה אני בחינם, אף אתם בחינם.

sub.desc_en: A baraita supports the derivation, also citing the verse 'כאשר צוני ה' אלהי' (as the Lord my God commanded me) to show that teaching must be free.
sub.desc: ברייתא תומכת בדרשה: 'כאשר צוני ה' אלהי' – מה אני בחינם, אף אתם בחינם.

sub.desc_en: The baraita adds that if one cannot find free teaching, he may teach for a fee, derived from the verse 'אמת קנה' (Buy truth).
sub.desc: ברייתא תומכת בדרשה: 'כאשר צוני ה' אלהי' – מה אני בחינם, אף אתם בחינם.

sub.desc_en: The baraita further derives from 'אמת קנה ואל תמכר' (Buy truth and do not sell it) that one may not sell the Torah he learned for a fee.
sub.desc: ברייתא תומכת בדרשה: 'כאשר צוני ה' אלהי' – מה אני בחינם, אף אתם בחינם.

items.text: הבחנה בין שכר הבאה לשכר הזיה
items.text_en: Gemara: Contradiction regarding payment for sanctification
items.desc_en: The Gemara raises a contradiction: the Mishnah says that taking payment for sprinkling and sanctifying invalidates the water and ash, yet a baraita states that if one sanctifies with purification water and ash, the woman is sanctified even if he is an Israelite. Abaye resolves this: the Mishnah refers to payment for the act of sprinkling and sanctifying, while the baraita refers to payment for bringing and filling the water. The Gemara supports this from the wording of the Mishnah and baraita.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה ממשנה בקידושין המתירה לקדש במי חטאת ובאפר חטאת, ומתרצת: שם מדובר בשכר הבאה ומילוי, וכאן בשכר הזיה וקידוש עצמם. הלשון המדויקת במשנתנו תומכת בתירוץ זה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a contradiction: the Mishnah says that payment for sprinkling and sanctifying invalidates the water and ash, but a baraita states that if one sanctifies with water and ash of the sin-offering, it is valid even if he is an Israelite.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה ממשנה בקידושין המתירה לקדש במי חטאת ובאפר חטאת, בניגוד למשנתנו האוסרת הנאה מהם.

sub.desc_en: Abaye resolves the contradiction: the Mishnah refers to payment for the act of sprinkling and sanctifying, while the baraita refers to payment for bringing and filling the water and ash.
sub.desc: אביי מתרץ: המשנה בקידושין עוסקת בשכר הבאה ומילוי, המותר, ואילו משנתנו אוסרת שכר הזיה וקידוש עצמם.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara supports Abaye's distinction by noting that the Mishnah uses the phrase 'for sprinkling and sanctifying,' while the baraita uses 'sanctifies with water and ash,' confirming the difference.
sub.desc: הגמרא מוכיחה מלשון המשניות שהתירוץ מדויק: כאן נאמר 'להזות ולקדש', ושם 'מי חטאת ואפר חטאת'.

items.text: היתר כהן להיכנס לבית הפרס
items.text_en: Gemara: How the priest becomes impure for terumah
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks how the priest himself can go to become impure for his terumah, and answers that he goes to a beit hapras (a field with uncertain impurity) which is only rabbinically impure, as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav that one may sift through a beit hapras and walk.
items.desc: הגמרא שואלת כיצד מותר לכהן להיטמא עבור בדיקת בכור, ומתרצת שמדובר בבית הפרס דרבנן, ורב יהודה בשם רב מתיר לנפח את העפר וללכת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks how the priest himself can go to a place of uncertain impurity (בית הפרס) to defile the other, and answers that it is a rabbinic-level impurity.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: כיצד מותר לכהן עצמו להיטמא כדי לבדוק בכור?

sub.text_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav
sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav explains that one may sift the soil of a בית הפרס (a field with uncertain graves) and walk through it, as it is only a rabbinic impurity.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת שמדובר בבית הפרס דרבנן, ורב יהודה בשם רב מתיר לנפח את העפר וללכת.

items.text: דין בית הפרס שנדוש וטומאת כהן
items.text_en: Opening discussion on a Beit HaPras and the definition of a 'batel worker'
items.desc_en: Rav Yehuda bar Ami quotes Rav Yehuda that a Beit HaPras that was trampled is pure. Alternatively, this applies to other impurities. The Gemara then discusses the case of an elder who is carried on a donkey, and Abaye defines the term 'like a batel worker' as one who is idle from that specific craft.
items.desc: רב יהודה בר אמי בשם רב יהודה אומר שבית הפרס שנדוש טהור, אך כהן שנטמא בו אינו אוכל בתרומה עד שיטבול. הגמרא מבררת שמדובר בטומאה קלה שאינה מחייבת התרחקות מהמקדש.

sub.text: רב יהודה בר אמי משמיה דרב יהודה
sub.text_en: Rav Yehuda bar Ami quoting Rav Yehuda
sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda bar Ami quotes Rav Yehuda that a trampled Beit HaPras is pure.
sub.desc: רב יהודה בר אמי בשם רב יהודה פוסק שבית הפרס שנדוש טהור.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests an alternative interpretation: the mishna refers to other impurities where priests are not admonished.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבררת שהאיסור לכהן לאכול תרומה נובע מטומאה קלה שאין בה אזהרה על טומאת מקדש.

sub.desc_en: Abaye defines 'like a batel worker' as one idle from that specific craft.
sub.desc: אביי מבאר ששכר הפועל הבטל נמדד לפי אותה מלאכה שממנה הוא בטל.

items.text: משנה: החשוד על הבכורות
items.text_en: Mishnah: Purchasing from one suspected regarding firstborn animals
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that one suspected of mishandling firstborn animals may not be sold meat of deer or untanned hides. Rabbi Eliezer permits purchasing female hides but not combed wool or fleece, though spun wool and garments are permitted.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת שאסור לקנות מהחשוד על הבכורות בשר צבאים ועורות שאינם עבודים, אך רבי אליעזר מתיר עורות של נקבה. כמו כן, אסור לקנות צמר מלובן וצואי, אך מותר לקנות טווי ובגדים.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens by stating that one suspected regarding firstborn animals may not be sold deer meat or untanned hides.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדיני קנייה מהחשוד על הבכורות, ואוסרת בשר צבאים ועורות שאינם עבודים, מתירה עורות נקבה לרבי אליעזר, ואוסרת צמר מלובן וצואי אך מתירה טווי ובגדים.

sub.desc_en: רבי אליעזר (Rabbi Eliezer) permits purchasing hides of female animals from the suspect.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדיני קנייה מהחשוד על הבכורות, ואוסרת בשר צבאים ועורות שאינם עבודים, מתירה עורות נקבה לרבי אליעזר, ואוסרת צמר מלובן וצואי אך מתירה טווי ובגדים.

sub.desc_en: רבי אליעזר (Rabbi Eliezer) rules that one may not purchase bleached or dirty wool from the suspect.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדיני קנייה מהחשוד על הבכורות, ואוסרת בשר צבאים ועורות שאינם עבודים, מתירה עורות נקבה לרבי אליעזר, ואוסרת צמר מלובן וצואי אך מתירה טווי ובגדים.

sub.desc_en: רבי אליעזר (Rabbi Eliezer) permits purchasing spun thread and garments from the suspect.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדיני קנייה מהחשוד על הבכורות, ואוסרת בשר צבאים ועורות שאינם עבודים, מתירה עורות נקבה לרבי אליעזר, ואוסרת צמר מלובן וצואי אך מתירה טווי ובגדים.

items.text: Gemara: Reason for prohibiting deer meat and untanned hides
items.text_en: Gemara: Reason for prohibiting deer meat and untanned hides
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that deer meat is prohibited because it can be confused with calf meat. For untanned hides, the reason is that if it were from a firstborn, the owner would not have bothered to tan it, fearing the rabbis would confiscate it.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains why deer meat is prohibited: it can be confused with calf meat.
The Gemara explains that untanned hides are prohibited because if it were from a firstborn, the owner would not have bothered to tan it, fearing the rabbis would confiscate it.

items.text: Debate on Rabbi Eliezer's ruling and the Tanna Kamma's objection
items.text_en: Debate on Rabbi Eliezer's ruling and the Tanna Kamma's objection
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains Rabbi Eliezer's reasoning for permitting female hides: it is well known that a female animal cannot be a firstborn. The Tanna Kamma objects that even a male could be claimed to have been eaten by mice, but the Gemara responds that such a claim is also well known.

sub.desc_en: The mishna cites Rabbi Eliezer's ruling that one may purchase hides of female animals from one suspect with regard to firstborns.
The Gemara asks for the reason behind Rabbi Eliezer's ruling.
The Gemara answers that the difference between male and female hides is well known.
The Tanna Kamma objects that even a male hide could be sold by cutting off the reproductive organ and claiming mice ate it.
The Gemara rejects the objection, explaining that the place of mice is well known and distinguishable from a knife cut.

items.text: Clarification of wool and garments in the Mishnah
items.text_en: Clarification of wool and garments in the Mishnah
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah mentions both combed wool and fleece, explaining that it is one category: combed wool from its fleece. Similarly, it clarifies that 'garments' refers to felt cloaks (namtei), resolving the redundancy.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah mentions both bleached wool and dirty wool, since if bleached wool is prohibited, dirty wool should certainly be prohibited.
The Gemara answers that the Mishnah is teaching one case: bleached wool from its fleece, resolving the redundancy.
The Gemara questions why the Mishnah mentions both spun thread and garments, since if spun thread is permitted, garments should certainly be permitted.
The Gemara answers that 'garments' refers to felt cloaks (namtei), which are not made of spun thread, resolving the redundancy.

items.text: משנה וגמרא: החשוד על השביעית
items.text_en: Mishnah and Gemara on one suspected regarding shemittah
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that one suspected of violating shemittah may not be sold flax, even if combed, but spun or woven items are permitted. The Gemara clarifies that 'woven' refers to thick cloth (tichei).
items.desc: המשנה אוסרת לקנות מהחשוד על השביעית פשתן אפילו סרוק, אך מתירה טווי ואריג. הגמרא מבארת ש'אריג' הכוונה לתיכי (חוטים שזורים).

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah rules that one suspected of violating shemittah may not be sold flax, even combed, but spun or woven items are permitted.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין החשוד על השביעית, ואוסרת לקנות ממנו פשתן אפילו סרוק, אך מתירה טווי ואריג.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: since spun thread is permitted, is it necessary to mention woven fabric?
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: אם מותר לקנות טווי, כל שכן אריג, ומדוע המשנה צריכה להזכירו?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers: 'woven' here refers to thick cloth (תיכי), which is not made from spun thread.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: אם מותר לקנות טווי, כל שכן אריג, ומדוע המשנה צריכה להזכירו?

items.text: משנה וגמרא: החשוד על מכירת תרומה
items.text_en: Mishnah and Gemara on one suspected of selling terumah as non-sacred
items.desc_en: The Mishnah rules that one suspected of selling terumah as non-sacred may not be sold even water or salt, according to Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Shimon limits the prohibition to items with a connection to terumah and tithes. The Gemara explains that this includes fish innards mixed with olive oil, and cites a case of a butcher suspected of such sales.
items.desc: המשנה: רבי יהודה אוסר לקנות מהחשוד על מכירת תרומה אפילו מים ומלח; רבי שמעון אוסר רק דברים שיש בהם זיקת תרומה ומעשרות. הגמרא מבארת שרבי שמעון בא להוסיף קרבי דגים שמעורב בהם שמן זית. מסופר על טבח חשוד שמכר בשר בכור.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens with the case of one suspected of selling תרומה (priestly portion) as non-sacred, stating that one may not purchase even water and salt from him according to רבי יהודה (Rabbi Yehuda).
sub.desc: המשנה מציגה את מחלוקת רבי יהודה ורבי שמעון: רבי יהודה אוסר לקנות מהחשוד על מכירת תרומה אפילו מים ומלח, ורבי שמעון אוסר רק דברים שיש בהם זיקת תרומה ומעשרות.

sub.desc_en: רבי שמעון (Rabbi Shimon) limits the prohibition to items that have a connection to תרומה (priestly portion) and מעשרות (tithes).
sub.desc: המשנה מציגה את מחלוקת רבי יהודה ורבי שמעון: רבי יהודה אוסר לקנות מהחשוד על מכירת תרומה אפילו מים ומלח, ורבי שמעון אוסר רק דברים שיש בהם זיקת תרומה ומעשרות.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what additional item is included by רבי שמעון (Rabbi Shimon)'s statement.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת: מה בא רבי שמעון להוסיף באיסורו?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that it includes fish innards, because people mix olive oil with them, and the oil might be from תרומה (priestly portion).
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת: מה בא רבי שמעון להוסיף באיסורו?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a case of a certain butcher who was suspected of selling such items, providing a practical example of the ruling.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתחילה לספר על טבח שהיה חשוד למכור בשר בכור, כהמשך לעניין החשודים.

items.text: Rava's penalty for selling forbidden fat
items.text_en: Rava's penalty for selling forbidden fat
items.desc_en: Rava penalizes someone who sold forbidden fat (תַּרְבָּא דְּאַטְמָא) by requiring him to sell even nuts. Rav Pappa questions whether this follows Rabbi Yehuda's view, but Rava explains it follows Rabbi Shimon, because the seller's own violation (using the fat to season nuts for butchers' children) caused the problem.

sub.desc_en: Rava penalizes someone who sold forbidden fat (תַּרְבָּא דְּאַטְמָא) by requiring him to sell even nuts.
Rav Pappa questions whether Rava's penalty follows Rabbi Yehuda's view, objecting that if so, the seller should be allowed to sell even water and salt.
Rava explains that the penalty follows Rabbi Shimon's view, because the seller's own violation (using the fat to season nuts for butchers' children) caused the problem.

items.text: Mishnah: Suspected for one violation, not another
items.text_en: Mishnah: Suspected for one violation, not another
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that one suspected of violating Sabbatical-year laws is not suspected of tithe violations, and vice versa. However, one suspected of both is suspected of purity laws, and some are suspected of purity laws but not of the others. The general rule: one suspected of a matter cannot judge or testify about it.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that one suspected of violating Sabbatical-year laws is not suspected of tithe violations, and vice versa; one suspected of both is suspected of purity laws, and the general rule is that one suspected of a matter cannot judge or testify about it.

items.text: Gemara: Reasons for the Mishnah's distinctions
items.text_en: Gemara: Reasons for the Mishnah's distinctions
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains why one suspected of Sabbatical-year violations is not suspected of tithe violations: Sabbatical-year produce does not require an added fifth (חוֹמָה), while tithes do, making tithes more stringent. Conversely, one suspected of tithe violations is not suspected of Sabbatical-year violations because tithes have redemption, while Sabbatical-year produce is forbidden and has no redemption, making it more stringent.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why one suspected of Sabbatical-year violations is not suspected of tithe violations.

The Gemara answers that Sabbatical-year produce does not require an added fifth (חוֹמָה), while tithes do, making tithes more stringent and thus one suspected of the lighter violation is not suspected of the heavier.
The Gemara asks why one suspected of tithe violations is not suspected of Sabbatical-year violations.

The Gemara answers that tithes have redemption, while Sabbatical-year produce is forbidden and has no redemption, making it more stringent, so one suspected of the lighter violation is not suspected of the heavier.

items.text: Reason for suspected of both: Torah vs. Rabbinic
items.text_en: Reason for suspected of both: Torah vs. Rabbinic
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that one suspected of both Sabbatical-year and tithe violations (which are Torah laws) is certainly suspected of purity laws (which are Rabbinic).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains that one suspected of both Sabbatical-year and tithe violations (Torah laws) is certainly suspected of purity laws (Rabbinic).

items.text: Contradiction: Suspected of purity but not of Torah laws
items.text_en: Contradiction: Suspected of purity but not of Torah laws
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions the Mishnah's statement that one can be suspected of purity laws but not of Sabbatical-year or tithe laws, since purity is Rabbinic and the others are Torah laws. It cites a baraita that seems to contradict: one trusted for purity is trusted for Sabbatical-year, implying that if suspected for purity, he is suspected for Sabbatical-year.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions the Mishnah's claim that one can be suspected of purity laws but not Torah laws, since purity is Rabbinic and the others are Torah-based.
The Gemara cites a baraita that seems to contradict: one trusted for purity is trusted for Sabbatical-year, implying that if suspected for purity, he is suspected for Sabbatical-year.

items.text: Resolutions of the contradiction
items.text_en: Resolutions of the contradiction
items.desc_en: Rabbi Il'ai resolves that the Mishnah refers to one who privately observes purity laws but is suspected publicly. Rabbi Yannai bar Rabbi Yishmael explains that the Mishnah deals with one who was suspected of both, accepted upon himself both, and then was suspected of one again, so we say that since he is suspected of one, he is suspected of the other.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Il'ai resolves the contradiction by explaining that the Mishnah refers to one who privately observes purity laws but is suspected publicly.

Rabbi Yannai bar Rabbi Yishmael explains that the Mishnah deals with one who was suspected of both, accepted upon himself both, and then was suspected of one again, so we say that since he is suspected of one, he is suspected of the other.

items.text: Attribution of the Mishnah to Rabbi Akiva vs. Sages
items.text_en: Attribution of the Mishnah to Rabbi Akiva vs. Sages
items.desc_en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah cites Rabbi Yochanan that the Mishnah is the unattributed view of Rabbi Akiva, but the Sages say one suspected of Sabbatical-year is suspected of tithes. Two versions follow: one identifies the Sages as Rabbi Yehuda (for whom Sabbatical-year is stringent), and another as Rabbi Meir (who holds that suspicion of one matter makes one suspected of the entire Torah).

sub.text: Rabbah bar bar Chanah citing Rabbi Yochanan
sub.text_en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah citing Rabbi Yochanan
sub.desc_en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah reports in the name of Rabbi Yochanan that the Mishnah is the unattributed view of Rabbi Akiva, but the Sages hold that one suspected of violating the Sabbatical year is also suspected of violating tithes.
The Gemara identifies the Sages as Rabbi Yehuda, in whose locale the Sabbatical year is treated stringently, illustrated by a story of a man who swore he never ate Sabbatical produce.

An alternative version reverses the Sages' position: one suspected of violating tithes is suspected of violating the Sabbatical year, and identifies the Sages as Rabbi Meir, who holds that suspicion of one matter makes one suspected of the entire Torah.

items.text: Alternative tradition: Suspected of tithes is suspected of Sabbatical-year
items.text_en: Alternative tradition: Suspected of tithes is suspected of Sabbatical-year
items.desc_en: A dispute between Rabbi Yona and Rabbi Yirmeya (or Rabbi Yona and Rabbi Ze'ira) as students of Rabbi Ze'ira (or Rabbi Yochanan): one says that the Sages hold that one suspected of tithes is suspected of Sabbatical-year.

sub.desc_en: The gemara introduces an alternative tradition about the identity of the students and their teacher.

sub.text: First student (Rabbi Yona or Rabbi Yirmeya)
sub.text_en: First student (Rabbi Yona or Rabbi Yirmeya)
sub.desc_en: One student states that the Sages hold that one suspected of tithes is suspected of Sabbatical-year.

items.text: Dispute about who is suspected for tithes and the seventh year
items.text_en: Dispute about who is suspected for tithes and the seventh year
items.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir regarding who is considered suspected for tithes and the seventh year. It cites a baraita where Rabbi Meir holds that one suspected for one matter is suspected for the entire Torah, while the Sages disagree.

items.text: The rule for a convert who accepts the Torah
items.text_en: The rule for a convert who accepts the Torah
items.desc_en: The Gemara states that a convert who accepts the Torah and is suspected for one matter is considered suspected for the entire Torah, like a Jewish apostate. The practical difference is that his kiddushin is valid.

sub.desc_en: The baraita states that a convert who accepted the Torah and is suspected for one matter is considered suspected for the entire Torah, like a Jewish apostate.
The Gemara explains the practical difference: if he betroths a woman, his betrothal is valid.

items.text: קבלת דברי חבירות, תורה, לויה וכהונה חוץ מדבר אחד
items.text_en: Accepting a person except for one matter
items.desc_en: A baraita teaches that one who comes to accept the words of חברות except for one matter is not accepted. Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda adds that even one detail of the words of the Scribes is disqualifying. Similarly, a Levite or priest who does not accept all aspects of their service is not accepted, as derived from a verse.
items.desc: ברייתא קובעת כי הבא לקבל דברי חבירות, גר לקבל דברי תורה, בן לוי לקבל דברי לויה או כהן לקבל דברי כהונה, אם הם מסרבים לקבל אפילו דבר אחד, אין מקבלים אותם. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה מוסיף שאפילו דקדוק אחד מדברי סופרים מעכב.

items.text: דרכי קבלת חבירות: צינעה או לימוד תחילה
items.text_en: Procedure for accepting a candidate for חברות
items.desc_en: A baraita discusses the procedure for accepting a candidate: if he is observed acting discreetly at home, he is accepted first and then taught; otherwise, he is taught first and then accepted. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says that in either case, he is accepted and learns as he goes.
items.desc: ברייתא דנה כיצד מקבלים אדם לחבירות: אם נוהג בצינעה בתוך ביתו, מקבלים אותו ואחר כך מלמדים אותו; אם לא, מלמדים אותו ואחר כך מקבלים אותו. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי פוטר מכל זה ומקבל אותו מיד.

items.text: Accepting for different levels: garments and purity
items.text_en: Accepting for different levels: garments and purity
items.desc_en: A baraita teaches that one is accepted first for garments and then for purities. If he says he accepts only for garments, he is accepted; if he accepts for purities but not garments, he is not accepted even for purities.

items.text: Duration of acceptance: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel
items.text_en: Duration of acceptance: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel
items.desc_en: A baraita records a dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about the duration of acceptance: Beit Shammai says 30 days for liquids and 12 months for garments, while Beit Hillel says both for 12 months. The Gemara notes that this would make Beit Shammai lenient and Beit Hillel strict, so it corrects that Beit Hillel says both for 30 days.

sub.desc_en: The baraita opens with a question about the duration of acceptance and records the positions of Beit Shammai (30 days for liquids, 12 months for garments) and Beit Hillel (both for 12 months).
The Gemara objects that this version makes Beit Shammai lenient and Beit Hillel strict, which is unusual.
The Gemara corrects the baraita: Beit Hillel actually says both for 30 days, resolving the anomaly.

items.text: Siman (mnemonic)
items.text_en: Siman (mnemonic)
items.desc_en: A mnemonic is provided to aid memory of the following teachings.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara provides a mnemonic listing key topics (חָבֵר, תַּלְמִיד, תְּכֵלֶת, מֶכֶס, חָזַר, גַּבַּאי, בְּעַצְמוֹ) to aid memory of the following teachings.

items.text: קבלת חבירות בפני שלושה חברים ופטור זקן היושב בישיבה
items.text_en: Acceptance before three associates and exceptions
items.desc_en: A baraita teaches that one must accept before three associates, but his family members do not need to. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees. Another baraita adds that even a Torah scholar needs acceptance before three, except for an elder sitting in the yeshiva. Abba Shaul says a Torah scholar does not need acceptance, and others can accept before him.
items.desc: ברייתא קובעת שהבא לקבל חבירות צריך לקבל בפני שלושה חברים, ובני ביתו פטורים מכך לדעת תנא קמא, אך רבן שמעון בן גמליאל מחייב גם אותם. עוד נאמר שתלמיד חכם צריך קבלה בפני שלושה, אך זקן היושב בישיבה פטור, ואבא שאול פוטר גם תלמיד חכם ואף מאפשר לאחרים לקבל לפניו.

sub.desc_en: The baraita opens by stating that one who accepts the matters of חברות (associate status) must do so before three associates, but his children and household members are exempt from this requirement.
sub.desc: הברייתא פותחת בדין שהבא לקבל חבירות צריך לקבל בפני שלושה חברים, אך בני ביתו פטורים מכך.

sub.desc_en: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel) disagrees, arguing that even the children and household members must accept before three associates, because a associate who accepted himself is not comparable to the son of an associate who accepted only through his father.
sub.desc: הברייתא פותחת בדין שהבא לקבל חבירות צריך לקבל בפני שלושה חברים, אך בני ביתו פטורים מכך.

sub.desc_en: A second baraita reiterates the requirement for acceptance before three associates, adding that even a תלמיד חכם (Torah scholar) must do so, but an elder who sits in the yeshiva is exempt because he already accepted from the moment he sat.
sub.desc: ברייתא נוספת קובעת שגם תלמיד חכם צריך קבלה בפני שלושה, אך זקן היושב בישיבה פטור שכבר קיבל עליו משעה שישב.

sub.desc_en: אבא שאול (Abba Shaul) states that even a Torah scholar does not need to accept before three associates, and moreover, others can accept before him.
sub.desc: ברייתא נוספת קובעת שגם תלמיד חכם צריך קבלה בפני שלושה, אך זקן היושב בישיבה פטור שכבר קיבל עליו משעה שישב.

items.text: מעשה בבנו של רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס וטומאת טהרות
items.text_en: Story of Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus's son and the dispute about purity
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan says that a mishnah was taught in the days of the son of Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus. A story is told: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei were uncertain about a matter of purities and sent to the son of Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus to investigate. They found him carrying purities, and he sat the sages down while he stood to examine the matter. When they reported back, Rabbi Yehuda criticized him for disrespecting Torah scholars, but Rabbi Yosei defended him, saying that since the Temple's destruction, priests have been particular not to entrust purities to just anyone.
items.desc: רבי יוחנן מספר שבימי בנו של רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס נשנתה משנה זו. רבי יהודה ורבי יוסי שלחו אליו לברר ספק בטהרות, ומצאוהו נושא טהרות ומרחיק אותם מהם. רבי יהודה כעס על בזיון תלמידי חכמים, אך רבי יוסי תירץ שמאז חורבן הבית נהגו הכהנים סלסול בעצמם ואינם מוסרים טהרות לכל אדם.

sub.desc_en: רבי יוחנן (Rabbi Yochanan) states that the mishnah was taught in the days of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס (Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus).
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן פותח ואומר שבימי בנו של רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס נשנתה משנה זו.

sub.desc_en: The narrative recounts that רבי יהודה (Rabbi Yehuda) and רבי יוסי (Rabbi Yosei) were uncertain about a matter of purities and sent to the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס (Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus) to investigate; they found him carrying pure items, and he seated the sages while he stood to examine the matter.
sub.desc: הגמרא מספרת שרבי יהודה ורבי יוסי נסתפקו בדבר טהרות ושלחו לבנו של רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, ומצאוהו נושא טהרות ומרחיק מהם.

sub.desc_en: When the students reported back, רבי יהודה (Rabbi Yehuda) criticized the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס (Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus) for degrading Torah scholars, saying that his father also degraded them.
sub.desc: הגמרא מספרת שרבי יהודה ורבי יוסי נסתפקו בדבר טהרות ושלחו לבנו של רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, ומצאוהו נושא טהרות ומרחיק מהם.

sub.desc_en: רבי יוסי (Rabbi Yosei) defends the son, saying that since the destruction of the Temple, priests have been particular not to entrust purities to just anyone, and thus his honor should be left in place.
sub.desc: רבי יוסי מיישב את הדבר ואומר שכבוד הזקן במקומו מונח, ומאז חורבן הבית נהגו הכהנים סלסול בעצמם ואינם מוסרים טהרות לכל אדם.

items.text: Presumption of a deceased associate's family and a market for techelet
items.text_en: Presumption of a deceased associate's family and a market for techelet
items.desc_en: A baraita teaches that if an associate dies, his wife, sons, and household retain their presumption of trustworthiness until they become suspected. Similarly, a market where techelet is sold retains its presumption until it becomes invalid.

sub.desc_en: The baraita rules that the family of a deceased associate retains its presumptive status of trustworthiness, and a market selling תכלת (sky-blue dye) retains its presumption until proven invalid.

items.text: Status of family members moving between an am ha'aretz and a chaver
items.text_en: Status of family members moving between an am ha'aretz and a chaver
items.desc_en: A baraita discusses the status of a wife, daughter, or slave of an am ha'aretz who marries or is sold to a chaver: they need to accept חברות anew. Conversely, if they move from a chaver to an am ha'aretz, they do not need to accept anew. Rabbi Meir says they do need to accept anew. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar cites a story from Rabbi Meir about a woman who, when married to a chaver, would tie tefillin for him, but when married to an am ha'aretz, would tie tax collector's knots for him.

sub.desc_en: The baraita states the general rule: a wife, daughter, or slave of an am ha'aretz moving to a chaver must accept חברות anew, but those moving from a chaver to an am ha'aretz do not need to accept anew.
Rabbi Meir disagrees, ruling that even those moving from a chaver to an am ha'aretz must accept חברות anew.

sub.text: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar citing Rabbi Meir
sub.text_en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar citing Rabbi Meir
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar cites a story from Rabbi Meir about a woman who, when married to a chaver, tied תפילין (phylacteries) for him, but when married to an am ha'aretz, tied tax collector's knots for him, illustrating the influence of the husband on her behavior.

items.text: מחלוקת תנאים בקבלת חוזרים בתשובה
items.text_en: Dispute about accepting penitent sinners
items.desc_en: A baraita records a dispute between Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Shimon with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korha regarding whether penitent sinners are accepted back. Rabbi Yochanan rules in favor of the latter pair.
items.desc: ברייתא ראשונה מביאה מחלוקת בין רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, ורבי שמעון ורבי יהושע בן קרחה לגבי קבלת חברים שחזרו לסורם. רבי יוחנן פוסק כזוג האחרון.

items.text: דין חבר שנעשה גבאי וחזר בו
items.text_en: The status of a former associate who became a tax collector
items.desc_en: A baraita states that initially a former associate who became a tax collector was not accepted back, but later it was ruled that he is like any other person. The Gemara relates a story about Rav Huna bar Chiyya and the dispute between Rava and Rav Yosef over which version of the baraita applies.
items.desc: ברייתא שנייה דנה בחבר שנעשה גבאי (מוכס) – תחילה דוחים אותו ואין מקבלים אותו גם אם פרש, ולבסוף חזרו לומר שכשפרש הרי הוא ככל אדם. סיפור על רב הונא בר חייא שהפך לגבאי, ושלחו לו לחזור בו; רב יוסף ורבה נחלקו אם לקבלו לאור הברייתא.

items.text: Who may inspect blemishes on firstborn animals
items.text_en: Who may inspect blemishes on firstborn animals
items.desc_en: A baraita states that one may inspect all firstborn animals except his own, and he may inspect his own consecrated items and tithes. The Gemara questions this, explaining that it refers to a single expert, and clarifies the reasons for the exceptions.

items.text: משנת פסולי המוקדשים – דיני מכירה ושקילה
items.text_en: Mishnah: Sale and weighing of disqualified consecrated animals
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that disqualified consecrated animals may be sold and weighed in the market, except for the firstborn and tithe, whose benefit belongs to the owner. It also permits weighing a portion against a portion for the firstborn.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת שפסולי המוקדשים נמכרים באיטליז ונשקלים בליטרא, חוץ מבכור ומעשר שהנאתן לבעלים. מותר לשקול מנה כנגד מנה בבכור.

items.text: Gemara's question on the mishnah's first clause
items.text_en: Gemara's question on the mishnah's first clause
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions when the mishnah's statement that the benefit of disqualified consecrated animals belongs to the Temple applies. It considers whether it is before or after redemption, and raises difficulties with each possibility.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens by quoting the mishnah and immediately asks: when does this apply? It rejects the possibility of after redemption, since then the benefit belongs to the owner.
The Gemara considers the alternative — before redemption — but objects that slaughtering before redemption would violate the requirement of standing and valuation.

items.text: Distinction between views on העמדה והערכה
items.text_en: Distinction between views on העמדה והערכה
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes that the difficulty depends on whether one holds that animals consecrated for the altar require העמדה והערכה (standing and valuation) before redemption. For those who hold they do not, the question is resolved; for those who hold they do, the difficulty remains.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that the previous resolution works only for the view that animals consecrated for the altar do not require העמדה והערכה (standing and valuation), but for the view that they do, the difficulty remains.

items.text: Answer: the mishnah refers to the original value
items.text_en: Answer: the mishnah refers to the original value
items.desc_en: The Gemara answers that the mishnah refers to after redemption, but the benefit to the Temple is the original value. Since the animal may now be sold in the market, the owner pays more to redeem it, benefiting the Temple.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that the mishnah actually refers to after redemption, and the benefit to the Temple is the original redemption value.
The Gemara explains that since the Sage permits selling the animal in the market, the owner will pay more to redeem it, benefiting the Temple.

items.text: Difficulty with the exception of tithe animal
items.text_en: Difficulty with the exception of tithe animal
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions the mishnah's exception for a tithe animal, since a baraita states that a tithe animal cannot be sold at all, whether alive or slaughtered, perfect or blemished. This contradicts the mishnah's implication that it can be sold at home.

items.text: Rav Sheshet's resolution: orphan's tithe animal
items.text_en: Rav Sheshet's resolution: orphan's tithe animal
items.desc_en: Rav Sheshet resolves the contradiction by explaining that the mishnah deals with a tithe animal belonging to orphans, and the sale is permitted due to the concern for returning a lost object (השבת אבידה).

sub.desc_en: Rav Sheshet resolves the contradiction by explaining that the mishnah deals with a tithe animal belonging to orphans, and the sale is permitted due to the concern for returning a lost object (השבת אבידה).

items.text: סיפור רב אידי וכעסו של רב ששת
items.text_en: Story of Rabbi Idi and Rav Sheshet's anger
items.desc_en: Rabbi Idi heard Rav Sheshet's teaching and repeated it in the study hall without attribution. Rav Sheshet became angry and cursed him, citing verses about the importance of citing a teaching in the name of its original speaker, so that the speaker's lips move in the grave.
items.desc: רב אידי, שמשו של רב ששת, שומע את התירוץ ואומר אותו בבית המדרש שלא בשמו. רב ששת כועס ומקלל. הגמרא מסבירה שחשוב לומר דבר בשם אומרו, כפי שמלמדים הפסוקים על שפתותיו דובבות בקבר.

items.text: Abaye's interpretation of the baraita
items.text_en: Abaye's interpretation of the baraita
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks what baraita Rav Sheshet used. A baraita is cited: an orphan's tithe animal may be sold, and a slaughtered tithe animal may be disposed of by 'הבלעה' (blending its value into the hide, fat, etc.). Abaye explains that the baraita means the orphan's tithe animal is sold with הבלעה.

items.text: Comparison with the lulav and etrog case
items.text_en: Comparison with the lulav and etrog case
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why an adult cannot sell with הבלעה, comparing to the case of buying a lulav in the Sabbatical year where one may 'blend' the price of an etrog into the lulav. The distinction is that there the blending is not obvious, while here it is obvious, so it is prohibited for an adult.

items.text: פירוש רבא לברייתא ומקורו
items.text_en: Rava's alternative interpretation and proof
items.desc_en: Rava rejects Abaye's interpretation, arguing that the baraita's repetition of 'מעשר בהמה' indicates two separate cases: an orphan's tithe may be sold normally, while an adult's slaughtered tithe must be disposed of by הבלעה. Rava proves from the verse that a tithe animal is redeemable after slaughter, and the rabbis decreed otherwise only due to the concern of confusion with before slaughter.
items.desc: רבא חולק על אביי ומפרש שהברייתא מדברת על שני מקרים: מעשר של יתומים נמכר כדרכו, ושל גדול שנשחט נמכר בהבלעה. רבא מביא ראיה מהפסוק 'לא יגאל' שמעול שמעשל תתיר מכירה לאחר שחיטה, ורבנן גזרו אטו לפני שחיטה.

items.text: דין מכירת בשר מעשר בהמה של יתומים
items.text_en: Sale of orphan's animal tithe
items.desc_en: Rava's ruling that the rabbinic decree against selling animal tithe does not apply to orphans is supported by Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak, who derives from a verse that orphans may sell their animal tithe.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה את דעת רבא ורב שמואל בר רב יצחק שמותר למכור בשר מעשר בהמה בעל מום של יתומים כדרכו, משום שהאיסור למכור הוא רק מדרבנן בדבר שנשם מחיים, ובבהמה בעלת מום אין ברכה מחיים אלא לאחר שחיטה, כפי שנלמד מהפסוק 'רק בכל אות נפשך תזבח ואכלת בשר'.

items.text: מחלוקת על הבלעת בשר בעצמות
items.text_en: Including tithe value in bones
items.desc_en: A dispute between Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Shimon beRabbi about whether one may include the value of the tithe animal in the sale of its bones is resolved: they disagree only regarding small cattle, or they both refer to large cattle but follow local custom.
items.desc: נשאלה שאלה האם מותר להבליע את ערך בשר מעשר בהמה בעל מום בעצמות. רבי חייא ורבי שמעון ברבי נחלקו: האחד אוסר והשני מתיר. הגמרא מיישבת שאינם חלוקים, אלא האחד מדבר בבהמה דקה (שעצמותיה אינן נמכרות) והשני בגסה (שעצמותיה נמכרות), או שהם חלוקים לפי מנהג המקום.

sub.desc_en: A dilemma is raised: may one include the value of the tithe animal in the sale of its bones? Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Shimon beRabbi dispute — one permits inclusion, the other prohibits it.
The Gemara resolves that they do not disagree: one refers to small cattle (whose bones are not sold), the other to large cattle (whose bones are sold).
Alternatively, both refer to large cattle and do not disagree: each follows the custom of his locale.

items.text: איסור מכירת מעשר בהמה לעומת בכור
items.text_en: Source that ma'aser behemah cannot be sold
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks for the source that ma'aser behemah cannot be sold, and Rav Chinana citing Rav, and Rav Dimi citing Rabbi Yochanan, derive it via a gezerah shavah from charamim, where sale is also prohibited.
items.desc: הברייתא קובעת שבכור אסור בפדייה אך מותר במכירה, ואילו מעשר בהמה אסור גם בפדייה וגם במכירה, בין חי בין שחוט, בין תם בין בעל מום. הגמרא שואלת מהיכן נלמד איסור מכירה במעשר, ורב חננא ורב דימי בשם רבי יוחנן מביאים גזירה שווה מ'לא יגאל' בחרמים, שממנה נלמד שגם במעשר יש איסור מכירה.

items.text: דיון בלימוד גזירה שווה: איזה פסוק מפני?
items.text_en: Challenges and alternative derivations
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak challenges the gezerah shavah, noting that charamim have a unique stringency. The Gemara explores alternative derivations from ma'aser to charamim, from bekhor to charamim, and from bekhor to ma'aser, each refuted by a potential challenge, until it concludes that the verse 'veha'avarta' is extraneous and supports the derivation.
items.desc: רב נחמן בר יצחק מעלה את הצורך שהפסוק 'לא יגאל' יהיה מיותר (מפני) כדי שניתן יהיה ללמוד ממנו גזירה שווה. הגמרא דנה באפשרויות שונות: לימוד מחרמים למעשר, מבכור לחרמים, וממעשר לבכור, תוך ניסיון למצוא פסוק מיותר. בסופו של דבר, הגמרא קובעת שהפסוק 'והעברת' בבכור הוא מיותר ומאפשר לימוד גזירה שווה למעשר, ובכך 'לא יגאל' במעשר הופך להיות מיותר ללימוד מחרמים.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak objects that the verbal analogy requires the phrase to be free (מַפְנֵי), otherwise it can be refuted because חֲרָמִים (dedications) apply to all items, unlike מעשר (tithe).
The Gemara answers that the phrase is indeed free: if the verse omitted 'וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל' in חֲרָמִים, one could derive the prohibition from מעשר, so the extra phrase must be free for the analogy.
The Gemara objects that the derivation from מעשר can be refuted because מעשר has sanctity before and after (if one mistakenly designates the ninth or eleventh animal), unlike חֲרָמִים.
The Gemara suggests an alternative: omit 'וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל' in חֲרָמִים and derive the prohibition from בכור (firstborn), making the phrase free.
The Gemara objects that the derivation from בכור can be refuted because בכור's sanctity is from the womb, unlike חֲרָמִים.
The Gemara suggests another alternative: omit 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' in מעשר and derive the prohibition from a verbal analogy of 'הַעֲבָרָה' (passing) from בכור, making the phrase free.
The Gemara objects that the phrase in מעשר is also not free, as the analogy from בכור can be refuted similarly (since בכור's sanctity is from the womb).

The Gemara resolves that the verse 'וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ' (and you shall cause to pass) in the context of בכור is extraneous, providing a free term for the verbal analogy with מעשר, thus supporting the derivation.

items.text: דחיית לימוד גאולה מבכור לחרמים וקביעת האיסור במעשר
items.text_en: Why bekhor does not learn from charamim
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why bekhor does not also learn ge'ulah from charamim, and explains that ma'aser is used for the hekesh because it is similar to charamim in being subject to ge'ulah, while bekhor uses pidyon. The Gemara then addresses a potential alternative and concludes that ma'aser is like charamim in ge'ulah.
items.desc: הגמרא שואלת מדוע לא לומדים גם בבכור איסור מכירה מגזירה שווה מחרמים, ועונה ש'לא יגאל' בבכור אינו מיותר (מפני) כי הוא נצרך לגופו, ואילו במעשר הוא מיותר. הגמרא דנה באפשרות ההפוכה ודוחה אותה בטענה שדנים גאולה מגאולה ולא פדייה מגאולה. לבסוף, הגמרא דוחה אפשרות ללמוד איסור מכירה בבכור מהעברה במעשר, ומסבירה שהמילה 'הוא' בחרמים ממעטת את הבכור אך לא את המעשר, כי מעשר דומה לחרמים בגאולה.

items.text: דברי רבא: 'לא יגאל' בחרמים מיותר
items.text_en: Rava's alternative explanation
items.desc_en: Rava argues that the verse 'lo yiga'el' regarding charamim is unnecessary because charamim are either in the owner's domain (like hekdesh) or the priest's (like chullin), so the verse must be free for the gezerah shavah.
items.desc: רבא מסביר ש'לא יגאל' בחרמים מותר (מיותר) כי דין חרמים ברור: כשהם בבית בעלים הם הקדש, וכשהם ביד כהן הם חולין. לכן הפסוק בא ללמד גזירה שווה למעשר בהמה. רבא מביא ברייתא המבחינה בין חרמים בבית בעלים (כהקדש) לבין חרמים ביד כהן (כחולין).

items.text: Gemara's question on the need for "lo yiga'el"
items.text_en: Gemara's question on the need for "lo yiga'el"
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Torah wrote "lo yiga'el" (it shall not be redeemed) regarding a firstborn, suggesting it could apply to tithe instead, since both have a similar redemption process.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Torah wrote 'lo yiga'el' (it shall not be redeemed) regarding a firstborn, suggesting it could apply to tithe instead, since both have a similar redemption process.

items.text: Rav Ashi's interpretation: "lo yiga'el" means "lo yimakher"
items.text_en: Rav Ashi's interpretation: "lo yiga'el" means "lo yimakher"
items.desc_en: Rav Ashi argues that "lo yiga'el" regarding tithe means it cannot be sold. He proves this by noting that the verse mentions both substitution and redemption, implying that while alive it cannot be redeemed, but after slaughter it could be—yet this contradicts the requirement of standing and valuation, so the verse must teach that it cannot be sold.

sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi states that the phrase 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' (it may not be redeemed) regarding the animal tithe offering actually means it may not be sold, and he cites the verse as his proof.
Rav Ashi questions how the verse could be understood literally, since substitution applies only while alive and redemption would require standing and valuation, which is impossible after slaughter.
Rav Ashi concludes that the phrase 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' must be interpreted as a prohibition against selling, not literal redemption.

items.text: קושיה על פירוש רב אשי
items.text_en: Refining the proof for Rav Ashi's view
items.desc_en: The Gemara considers the dispute about whether consecrated animals for the altar require standing and valuation. It then reframes the argument: if a firstborn cannot be redeemed while alive due to its strong sanctity, it should certainly not be redeemable after slaughter when sanctity is weaker. Thus, "lo yiga'el" must mean it cannot be sold.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה על רב אשי: לשיטת האומר שקדשי מזבח אינם צריכים העמדה והערכה, ניתן לפרש את הפסוק כפשוטו. הגמרא דוחה קושיה זו בקל וחומר: אם בחיים לא נפדה, לאחר שחיטה קל וחומר שלא יפדה, ולכן הפסוק עוסק באיסור מכירה.

items.text: מדוע לא נכתב "לא ימכר"
items.text_en: Why the Torah wrote "lo yiga'el" instead of "lo yimakher"
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that if the Torah had written "lo yimakher" (it shall not be sold), one might think only sale is prohibited because it involves profane handling, but redemption would be permitted since the money enters the Temple treasury. Therefore, the Torah wrote "lo yiga'el" to prohibit both sale and redemption.
items.desc: הגמרא שואלת מדוע התורה כתבה "לא יגאל" במקום "לא ימכר", ועונה: אילו נכתב "לא ימכר" הייתי חושב שמותר לפדות, לכן נכתב "לא יגאל" לאסור גם מכירה וגם פדייה.

items.text: Mishnah: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel on counting with a priest for a firstborn
items.text_en: Mishnah: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel on counting with a priest for a firstborn
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that Beit Shammai says an Israelite may not be counted together with a priest to eat the firstborn, while Beit Hillel permits it, even with a gentile.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states the dispute: Beit Shammai prohibits counting an Israelite with a priest for a firstborn, while Beit Hillel permits it, even with a gentile.

items.text: Gemara: Identifying the Mishnah's author and the reasoning of Beit Shammai
items.text_en: Gemara: Identifying the Mishnah's author and the reasoning of Beit Shammai
items.desc_en: The Gemara identifies the Mishnah as following Rabbi Akiva, who permits even a gentile. It then explains Beit Shammai's reasoning: just as the priests eat the firstborn's meat exclusively (based on the verse "u'vesaram yihyeh lach"), so too only priests may be counted in the group to eat it.

items.text: מחלוקת בית שמאי ובית הלל על אכילת זר בבכור בעל מום
items.text_en: Beit Hillel's argument from a blemished animal and the refutation
items.desc_en: Beit Hillel argues that a blemished firstborn is permitted to a non-priest based on the verse 'the impure and the pure together shall eat it', reasoning that if an impure person (who cannot eat lesser holy offerings) may eat it, then a non-priest (who can eat lesser holy offerings) certainly may. The Gemara raises a refutation: the impure person is permitted in communal service, which is not comparable.
items.desc: בית הלל דורשים קל וחומר מטמא לזר להתיר אכילת בכור בעל מום לזרים. בית שמאי פרכים שהטמא הותר בעבודה, אך בית הלל דוחים שההשוואה היא באכילה ולא בעבודה.

sub.desc_en: Beit Hillel argues that a blemished firstborn is permitted to a non-priest, using a קל וחומר (a fortiori) from an impure person who may eat it despite being barred from lesser holy offerings.
The Gemara objects that the impure person is permitted in communal service, which is a unique leniency not applicable to a non-priest.
Beit Hillel responds that the discussion is about eating, not service, and a non-priest's eating is superior to an impure person's.

items.text: שיטת רבי עקיבא והסברת הפסוקים
items.text_en: Rabbi Akiva permits even a gentile, and the refutation
items.desc_en: Rabbi Akiva permits even a gentile to eat a blemished firstborn, deriving from the verse 'like the deer and like the hart' that just as these are permitted to a gentile, so too are disqualified consecrated animals. The Gemara counters that the three occurrences of 'deer and hart' are needed for other expositions, and another refutation argues that the comparison teaches that disqualified consecrated animals are exempt from the firstborn offering, not that they are permitted to gentiles.
items.desc: רבי עקיבא מתיר אפילו לגוי לאכול מבכור בעל מום, על פי היקש לצבי ואיל. החכמים החולקים דורשים את שלושת הפעמים שכתוב 'צבי ואיל' לדרשות אחרות, ומסבירים שההיקש בא לפטור מבכורה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Akiva permits even a non-Jew to eat blemished consecrated animals, deriving it from the verse 'כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל' (like the deer and the hart).
sub.desc: רבי עקיבא מתיר אפילו לגוי לאכול מבכור בעל מום, על פי היקש לצבי ואיל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks how the other rabbis interpret the three instances of 'צְבִי וְאַיָּל' (deer and hart) in the verse, and answers that each is used for a different teaching.
sub.desc: החכמים החולקים דורשים את שלושת הפעמים שכתוב 'צבי ואיל' לדרשות אחרות.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara presents an alternative interpretation: just as deer and hart are exempt from firstborn status, so too blemished consecrated animals are exempt from firstborn status.
sub.desc: ההיקש בא לפטור פסולי המוקדשין מבכורה, ולא להתיר אכילה לגוי.

items.text: מחלוקת על אכילת נדות בבכור בעל מום
items.text_en: Baraita on feeding the firstborn to menstruants
items.desc_en: A baraita records a dispute: Beit Shammai prohibits feeding a firstborn to menstruants, deriving from the verse 'and their flesh shall be yours' that just as in the case of a priest's wife, menstruants are forbidden, so too here. Beit Hillel distinguishes between a perfect firstborn (where the restriction applies) and a blemished one, citing the verse 'the impure and the pure together shall eat it'. Beit Shammai counters that this applies only where impurity does not emanate from the animal itself, but where it does (as with a menstruant), it is forbidden, citing a precedent from the Paschal lamb brought in impurity. Beit Hillel responds that there the Torah specified 'impure of soul', whereas here it writes 'impure' generally.
items.desc: בית שמאי אוסרים להאכיל בכור בעל מום לנדות, בהשוואה לחזה ושוק. בית הלל מתירים, ומבחינים בין תם לבעל מום. בית שמאי מבדילים בין טומאה היוצאת מגופו לטומאה חיצונית, על פי דין פסח הבא בטומאה. בית הלל דוחים שהכתוב 'טמא' סתמא מתיר כל טמא.

sub.text_en: Baraita on feeding firstborn to menstruants
sub.desc_en: A baraita records a dispute: Beit Shammai forbids feeding a firstborn to a menstruant, deriving from the verse 'וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָךְ' (and their flesh shall be yours) that just as in the original context menstruants are excluded, so here.
sub.desc: הברייתא מציגה את מחלוקת בית שמאי ובית הלל: בית שמאי אוסרים להאכיל בכור בעל מום לנדות, ובית הלל מתירים; ומסבירה את טעם בית שמאי מהיקש לחזה ושוק.

sub.desc_en: Beit Hillel responds that the restriction applies only to an unblemished firstborn, but a blemished one is permitted by the verse 'הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יֹאכְלֶנּוּ' (the impure and the pure together shall eat it).
sub.desc: בית הלל משיבים שההיקש לחזה ושוק נאמר רק בתם, אבל בבעל מום הכתוב מתיר בפירוש 'הטמא והטהור יאכלנו'.

sub.desc_en: Beit Shammai objects that the leniency applies only where impurity does not emanate from the animal's own body, citing a mishnah about the Paschal lamb brought in impurity where those with bodily emissions are excluded.
sub.desc: בית שמאי מחלקים בין טומאה חיצונית, המותרת בבעל מום, לבין טומאה היוצאת מגופו (כנדה), האסורה.

sub.desc_en: Beit Hillel responds that there the Torah specified 'טְמֵא נֶפֶשׁ' (impure of soul), but here the general term 'טָמֵא' (impure) is written, making no distinction.
sub.desc: בית הלל דוחים את הראיה: בפסח הכתוב מיעט 'טמא נפש', אבל בבכור כתוב 'טמא' סתמא, ואין חילוק בין טומאות.

sub.desc_en: Beit Hillel resolves that there the Torah specified 'טְמֵא נֶפֶשׁ' (impure of soul), whereas here it writes 'טָמֵא' (impure) generally, so the distinction does not apply.
sub.desc: בית הלל דוחים את הראיה: בפסח הכתוב מיעט 'טמא נפש', אבל בבכור כתוב 'טמא' סתמא, ואין חילוק בין טומאות.

items.text: איסור הפשטת עור מבהמה ביום טוב ובבכור
items.text_en: Baraita on not 'making it walk' on Yom Tov and identifying the tannaim
items.desc_en: A baraita states that one may not 'make an animal walk' (to improve its appearance) on Yom Tov, and similarly not with a firstborn or disqualified consecrated animals. The Gemara explains that on Yom Tov it is forbidden due to unnecessary exertion. Rav Chisda identifies the firstborn clause as Beit Shammai's view, who prohibit feeding it to menstruants (implying it is not for consumption). He identifies the clause about disqualified consecrated animals as Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon's view, who prohibits eating such meat after the blood of the perfect offering has been sprinkled. The Gemara questions why Rav Chisda did not attribute the entire baraita to Beit Shammai, and answers that Beit Shammai's leniency applies only to a firstborn (whose sanctity is from the womb), not to other disqualified consecrated animals.
items.desc: ברייתא אוסרת להרגיל (להפשיט עור) ביום טוב, בבכור ובפסולי המוקדשין. רב חסדא מסביר שהאיסור בבכור הוא לשיטת בית שמאי, ובפסולי המוקדשין לשיטת רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. הגמרא דוחה אפשרות לומר שהכל כבית שמאי, כי בית שמאי מחמירים רק בבכור שקדושתו מרחם.

sub.text: Baraita on not inviting guests on Yom Tov
sub.text_en: Baraita on not inviting guests on Yom Tov
sub.desc_en: A baraita states that one does not invite guests on Yom Tov, and similarly not for a firstborn or blemished consecrated animals.

sub.text: Gemara's question about the firstborn clause
sub.text_en: Gemara's question about the firstborn clause
sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains that Yom Tov is understandable due to unnecessary exertion, but asks who is the Tanna of the firstborn clause, and Rav Chisda answers it is Beit Shammai who forbids feeding it to menstruants.

sub.text: Gemara's question about blemished consecrated animals
sub.text_en: Gemara's question about blemished consecrated animals
sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks who is the Tanna for the clause about blemished consecrated animals, and Rav Chisda answers it is Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon, citing a mishnah where he holds that even if the meat is in the pot, once the blood of the unblemished offering is sprinkled, the blemished one is forbidden.

The Gemara objects that Rav Chisda could have established the entire baraita as Beit Shammai, and answers that Beit Shammai's stringency applies only to a firstborn whose sanctity is from the womb, not to blemished consecrated animals whose sanctity is not from the womb.
Rav Chisda identifies the clause as Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon's view, who prohibits eating such meat after the blood of the perfect offering has been sprinkled.
The Gemara objects that Rav Chisda could have attributed the entire baraita to Beit Shammai.
