The Gemara objects that the statement might mean feeding dry fruits from Elul and Tishrei during Adar and Nisan, not that the animal eats dry during the dry season.
The Gemara asks how much to feed, and Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Pinchas ben Arova answers: a fig-bulk.

sub.text: Rava's report of a question from the West
sub.text_en: Rava's report of a question from the West
sub.desc_en: Rava reports that in the West they asked whether the fig-bulk measure applies to one meal.

items.text: חקירת דרכי האכלה לבדיקת מום קבוע
items.text_en: Gemara's series of unresolved questions about the blemish
items.desc_en: The Gemara raises a series of hypothetical questions about the circumstances under which a blemish is considered effective, such as whether it is during the first meal or every meal, before or after eating or drinking, tied or untied, alone or with a friend, in the city or field, and even in a garden near the city. Each question ends with 'what?' and the last one concludes with 'teiku' (let it stand unresolved).
items.desc: הגמרא בוחנת את אופן האכלת הסובין לבהמה לצורך בדיקת מום קבוע: האם האכלה היא בכל סעודה או רק בראשונה, לפני או אחרי אכילה ושתייה, כשהיא קשורה או מותרת, לבדה או עם חברתה, בעיר או בשדה. כל ספק נותר בתיקו.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a series of unresolved questions about whether the blemish's effectiveness depends on the first meal or every meal, before or after eating or drinking.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת האם האכלת הסובין היא בכל סעודה או רק בראשונה, ומפרטת ספקות לגבי מועד ההאכלה ביחס לאכילה ושתייה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara continues with questions about whether the blemish is effective when tied or untied, alone or with a friend.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת האם הבהמה צריכה להיות קשורה או מותרת, ולבדה או עם חברתה בשעת האכלה.

sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi adds a question about whether the blemish is effective in the city or field, and even in a garden near the city, concluding with 'teiku' (let it stand unresolved).
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת האם ההאכלה צריכה להיות בעיר או בשדה, ורב אשי מוסיף ספק לגבי גינה הסמוכה לעיר; כל הספקות נותרו בתיקו.

items.text: דין שלוש בדיקות תוך שמונים יום
items.text_en: Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonus's statement and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak's qualification
items.desc_en: Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonus states a condition, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak adds that it only applies if the blemishes are triangular (or in a specific arrangement).
items.desc: רב נחמן בר יצחק מבהיר שבדיקת שלוש פעמים תוך שמונים יום צריכה להיות במרווחים שווים, כלומר שלישים שווים בזמן.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonos states a condition, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak explains that the blemishes must be triangular.
sub.desc: רבי חנניה בן אנטיגנוס קובע כי בודקים את הבהמה שלוש פעמים בתוך שמונים יום.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak qualifies the statement, adding that the blemishes must be triangular (or in a specific arrangement).
sub.desc: רבי חנניה בן אנטיגנוס קובע כי בודקים את הבהמה שלוש פעמים בתוך שמונים יום.

items.text: שאלת פינחס: מום למפרע או מכאן ולהבא
items.text_en: Pinchas's question to Shmuel about retroactive blemish
items.desc_en: Pinchas, brother of Mar Shmuel, asks Shmuel whether an animal that ate something and was not healed is considered blemished retroactively or only from now onward. The practical difference is whether it can be redeemed retroactively. Shmuel quotes a verse in response.
items.desc: פינחס אחי שמואל שואל: אם בהמה אכלה סובין ולא נרפאה, האם המום נחשב למפרע (משעת הגילוי) או מכאן ולהבא? הנפקא מינה היא למעילה בפדיון. שמואל מודה שאינו יודע את התשובה.

sub.text_en: Pinchas, brother of Mar Shmuel, to Shmuel
sub.desc_en: Pinchas asks Shmuel whether a blemish that appears after eating but without healing is considered retroactively effective or only from now onward.
sub.desc: פינחס שואל את שמואל: אם בהמה אכלה סובין ולא נרפאה, האם המום נחשב למפרע או מכאן ולהבא?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies the practical difference: whether the animal enters the redemption fund retroactively or only from now.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה את הנפקא מינה: אם המום למפרע, מי שנהנה מכספי הפדיון מעל.

sub.desc_en: Shmuel exclaims the verse 'פסחים בזזו בז' (the lame have taken spoil), indicating the question remains unresolved.
sub.desc: שמואל מודה שאינו יודע את התשובה, וקורא על אחיו את הפסוק 'פסחים בזזו בז'.

items.text: משנת מומי האף והשפה
items.text_en: Mishnah and Gemara on pierced nose and lip
items.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes of the nose (pierced, cracked, split) and lip (pierced, cracked, split). The Gemara cites a baraita that distinguishes between a hole from outside (a blemish) and from inside (not a blemish), and Rav Pappa explains a phrase about the outer lip.
items.desc: המשנה מונה מומין באף (נקב, פגימה, סדק) ובשפה (נקב, פגימה, סדק). הגמרא מבהירה שנקב בחוטם מבחוץ הוא מום, מבפנים אינו מום, ושפתיים מתייחסות לשורה החיצונה.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes of the nose (pierced, cracked, split) and lip (pierced, cracked, split).
sub.desc: המשנה מונה מומין באף ובשפה: נקב, פגימה וסדק.

sub.desc_en: A baraita distinguishes between a hole in the nose from outside (a blemish) and from inside (not a blemish).
sub.desc: ברייתא מבהירה שנקב בחוטם מבחוץ הוא מום, מבפנים אינו מום.

sub.desc_en: Rav Pappa explains that the phrase 'תּוֹרָא בָּרָא דְּשִׂיפְתֵּיהּ' refers to the outer lip.
sub.desc: ברייתא מבהירה שנקב בחוטם מבחוץ הוא מום, מבפנים אינו מום.

items.text: מחלוקת במומי החניכיים והתיומת
items.text_en: Mishnah and Gemara on outer and inner eyelashes and the 'teyomet'
items.desc_en: The Mishnah discusses blemishes of the outer and inner eyelashes, with Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonus saying not to examine from the 'teyomet' inward. The Gemara clarifies the baraita, explaining that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kapotsai and Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonus argue about whether the inner ones disqualify, and the Gemara resolves the apparent redundancy.
items.desc: המשנה מבדילה בין חניכיים חיצוניות (שנפגמו או נגממו – מום) לבין פנימיות (שנעקרו – מום). רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס פוטר בדיקת התיומת. הגמרא מבררת את מחלוקת התנאים: יש אומרים ששוחטים רק על חיצוניות, ורבי חנינא אומר שאין משגיחין על התיומת כלל.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes of outer and inner eyelashes, and Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonus rules that one does not examine from the teyomet inward, nor even the teyomet itself.
sub.desc: המשנה קובעת שחניכיים חיצוניות שנפגמו או נגממו הן מום, וחניכיים פנימיות שנעקרו הן מום; רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס מוסיף שאין בודקים מן התיומת ולפנים.

sub.desc_en: A baraita defines the teyomet as being considered inward, and records the positions of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kapotsai (only outer lashes qualify) and Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonus (the teyomet is entirely disregarded).
sub.desc: ברייתא מביאה שלוש דעות: הראשונה מגדירה תיומת כחלק הפנימי, השנייה (רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי) מתירה שחיטה רק על חיצוניות, והשלישית (רבי חנינא) פוטרת את התיומת לגמרי.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions the baraita's phrasing and notes that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kapotsai's position appears redundant with the Tanna Kamma.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מה אמר התנא הראשון? ועוד, רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי הרי חוזר על דברי התנא הראשון.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the baraita is missing a clause: the Tanna Kamma's ruling applies only to blemishes of breakage or tearing, but for uprooted inner lashes, slaughter is permitted.
sub.desc: הגמרא מיישבת: הברייתא חסרה; הכוונה: פנימיות שנפגמו או נגממו אינן מום, אבל אם נעקרו – שוחטין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara completes the baraita: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kapotsai says only outer lashes qualify for slaughter, but uprooted inner lashes disqualify; Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonus says the teyomet is entirely disregarded, not even disqualifying.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה: רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי מתיר שחיטה רק על חיצוניות, אבל פנימיות שנעקרו פוסלות; רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס פוטר את התיומת לגמרי – אפילו אינה פוסלת.

items.text: דיון בחסרון אבר מבפנים
items.text_en: Debate on whether there is a missing limb from within
items.desc_en: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami asks whether there is a concept of a missing limb from within (internal missing organ). The Gemara clarifies the question is about disqualification, not slaughter or redemption. It cites verses about kidneys to explore the issue, with various Amoraim debating whether the dispute is about the existence of a creature with one kidney, or about the status of a missing internal limb, and whether it applies before or after slaughter.
items.desc: רב אחדבוי בר אמי שואל אם חסרון אבר פנימי נחשב מום. הגמרא מביאה ברייתא הסותרת לכאורה בעניין כליות: יש אומרים שבעל כליה אחת פסול, ויש אומרים כשר. דעות שונות: רב חייא בר יוסף מיישב בכך שיש בריה עם כליה אחת; רבי יוחנן מיישב בחסרון לפני או אחרי שחיטה.

sub.desc_en: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami asks whether there is a concept of a missing limb from within (internal missing organ), and the Gemara clarifies the question is about disqualification, not slaughter or redemption.
sub.desc: רב אחדבוי בר אמי שואל אם חסרון אבר פנימי נחשב מום, ומברר שהשאלה היא לעניין פסול הקרבן, לא לשחיטת בכור או פדיון קדשים.

sub.text: הצגת שתי אפשרויות על ידי הגמרא
sub.desc_en: The Gemara presents two possible interpretations of the verse 'תָּמִים יִהְיֶה לְרָצוֹן' (it shall be perfect to be accepted): either any internal deficiency disqualifies, or only external blemishes disqualify.
sub.desc: הגמרא מציגה שתי אפשרויות: או שפסוק 'תמים יהיה לרצון' כולל כל חסרון, אפילו פנימי, או ש'כל מום לא יהיה בו' מלמד שרק חסרון חיצוני נחשב.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites two baraitot: one excludes a creature with one or three kidneys from the sacrifice, and another includes a creature with one kidney.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה שתי ברייתאות סותרות בעניין בעל כליה אחת: האחת פוסלת, והשנייה מכשירה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara initially assumes all agree a creature cannot naturally have one kidney, and the dispute is whether internal deficiency is considered a deficiency.
sub.desc: הגמרא מניחה שכולם מודים שאין בריה עם כליה אחת, ולכן המחלוקת היא אם חסרון פנימי נחשב חסרון.

sub.desc_en: Rav Chiya bar Yosef argues that all agree a creature can have one kidney and internal deficiency is a deficiency; the baraitot differ on whether the creature was born with one kidney or lost one.
sub.desc: רב חייא בר יוסף מיישב את הסתירה בכך שיש בריה עם כליה אחת מלכתחילה, והברייתא הפוסלת עוסקת במי שנולד עם שתיים ואחת חסרה.

sub.text: קושיית הגמרא על רב חייא בר יוסף
sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that the baraita compares one kidney to three, implying both are original conditions, not acquired losses.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: הברייתא הראשונה מקישה בעל אחת לבעל שלוש, ומשמע שגם אחת וגם שלוש מלכתחילה, ולכן אין מקום לתירוץ של רב חייא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the dispute is actually about whether a creature can be born with one kidney at all.
sub.desc: הגמרא מיישבת שהמחלוקת היא עצם קיום בריה עם כליה אחת: חכם אחד סובר שיש, והשני סובר שאין.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan argues that all agree a creature cannot have one kidney and internal deficiency is a deficiency; the baraitot differ on whether the kidney was lost before or after slaughter, and raises a further question about the status after slaughter but before receiving the blood.
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן מיישב שהסתירה נובעת מזמן החסרון: ברייתא אחת עוסקת בחסרון לפני שחיטה (פסול), והשנייה בחסרון לאחר שחיטה (כשר), והגמרא מקשה על יישוב זה.

items.text: Gemara's question on the timing of a blemish
items.text_en: Gemara's question on the timing of a blemish
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites Rabbi Zeira's statement that if one cuts the ear of the bull after receiving its blood, it is invalid, as the verse requires the bull to be as it was. It then distinguishes between a blemish that occurred before receiving the blood and after.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a contradiction: Rabbi Zeira said that cutting the ear of the bull after receiving its blood invalidates it, yet the Mishnah implies a blemish after receiving the blood is permitted, and resolves that one case is a blemish before receiving the blood and the other after.

items.text: Gemara's objection and resolution regarding the timing of blemishes
items.text_en: Gemara's objection and resolution regarding the timing of blemishes
items.desc_en: The Gemara objects that a blemish after receiving the blood but before sprinkling should still invalidate, citing a baraita that requires the animal to be perfect and within its first year at the time of slaughter. It then derives that all stages (receiving, carrying, sprinkling) require perfection. The Gemara resolves that the baraita refers only to the age requirement, not blemishes, and supports this with Rabbi Yehoshua's statement.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that a blemish after receiving the blood but before sprinkling should still invalidate, citing a baraita that requires the animal to be perfect and within its first year at the time of slaughter.
The baraita derives from the verse 'יִהְיֶה' that all stages of the service (receiving, carrying, sprinkling) require the animal to be perfect and within its first year.

The Gemara resolves that the baraita refers only to the age requirement (בן שנה), not to blemishes, and supports this with Rabbi Yehoshua's statement that leftover meat or fat does not prevent sprinkling the blood.

items.text: Rava's principle that hours disqualify in sacrifices
items.text_en: Rava's principle that hours disqualify in sacrifices
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions how an animal can be within its first year at slaughter but two years old at receiving, and Rava answers that this teaches that hours disqualify in sacrificial matters.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions how an animal can be within its first year at slaughter but two years old at receiving and conveying the blood.
Rava answers that this teaches that hours disqualify in sacrificial matters, meaning the animal must be within its first year at every stage of the service.

items.text: מחלוקת התנאים במומי ביצים וגיד
items.text_en: Dispute among Tannaim regarding blemishes on the testicles or the penis
items.desc_en: The Gemara presents a dispute about whether the blemishes of 'crushed, pounded, torn, or cut' apply to the testicles or the penis. Rabbi Yehuda says all apply to the testicles, Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says all apply to the penis, and Rabbi Yosei distinguishes between them. The Gemara initially suggests the dispute is about whether an internal defect is considered a blemish, but rejects this and explains that the dispute is about external blemishes: Rabbi Yehuda considers both types blemishes, Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov considers neither, and Rabbi Yosei considers only those that are missing.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא ובה מחלוקת בין רבי יהודה, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב ורבי יוסי בשאלה האם מומים כמו מעוך, כתות, נתוק וכרות נחשבים מום בביצים או בגיד. הגמרא דוחה את האפשרות שהמחלוקת היא על חסרון פנימי, ומסבירה שכולם עוסקים במומים גלויים, ונחלקו בשאלה האם השינוי ניכר לעין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara introduces a dispute among Tannaim about whether the blemishes 'מעוך וכתות ונתוק וכרות' (crushed, pounded, torn, cut) apply to the testicles or the penis, citing the positions of Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, and Rabbi Yosei.
The Gemara suggests the dispute is about whether a חסרון מבפנים (internal defect) is considered a blemish.
The Gemara rejects the suggestion, arguing that Rabbi Yosei's position is inconsistent with either view of internal defects.

The Gemara resolves that the dispute is about external blemishes: Rabbi Yehuda considers both 'מעוך וכתות' (crushed and pounded) and 'נתוק וכרות' (torn and cut) as blemishes, while Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov considers neither.
Rabbi Yosei distinguishes: 'מעוך וכתות' (crushed and pounded) are blemishes because the organs are missing, but 'נתוק וכרות' (torn and cut) are not blemishes because the organs are still present.

items.text: Mishnah: Blemishes of the penis, tail, and skin
items.text_en: Mishnah: Blemishes of the penis, tail, and skin
items.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes: a damaged penis, a damaged tail from the bone (not from the joint), a split tail tip, skin peeled off leaving the bone exposed, or flesh between vertebrae the width of a finger.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes that disqualify an animal: a damaged penis, a damaged tail from the bone (not the joint), a split tail tip, skin peeled off leaving the bone exposed, or flesh between vertebrae the width of a finger.

items.text: Gemara on the damaged penis and a story about a wolf
items.text_en: Gemara on the damaged penis and a story about a wolf
items.desc_en: Rabbi Elazar explains that the Mishnah means the penis was damaged but not removed, and the scrotum but not the testicles. A baraita supports this, and Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam recounts a case where a wolf removed a testicle and it returned to its original state.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Elazar explains that the Mishnah's 'damaged penis' means the organ was damaged but not removed, and the scrotum but not the testicles.
A baraita is cited that supports Rabbi Elazar's interpretation, stating the same distinction.
Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam recounts a case where a wolf removed a testicle from a firstborn animal and it returned to its original state, illustrating the halachic principle.

items.text: שיעור האצבע להלכות ציצית ואמות
items.text_en: Gemara on the measure of a finger and its applications
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that the finger mentioned in the Mishnah is one-quarter of a handbreadth of an average person. It then discusses two applications: for the blue thread in tzitzit (where Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel dispute the number of threads and the length of the fringe), and for the two cubits (citing a Mishnah about two cubits).
items.desc: הגמרא דנה בשיעור 'אצבע' הנזכר במשנה, ומסבירה שהוא אחד מארבעה בטפח של כל אדם. רבא מייחס שיעור זה להלכות ציצית, ורב הונא בר יהושע מייחסו למידת שתי אמות בכלים.

sub.desc_en: The Tanna teaches that the finger mentioned in the Mishnah is one-quarter of a handbreadth of an average person.
The Gemara asks: For what halachic application is this measure relevant?
Rabbah answers that it applies to the blue thread (תְּכֵלֶת) in tzitzit, citing a baraita where Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel dispute the number of threads and the length of the fringe.
The baraita specifies that the third (the fringe length according to Beit Hillel) is one-quarter of a handbreadth of an average person, directly linking the finger measure to tzitzit.

sub.text: Rav Huna brei d'Rav Yehoshua's alternative answer
sub.text_en: Rav Huna brei d'Rav Yehoshua's alternative answer
sub.desc_en: Rav Huna brei d'Rav Yehoshua offers an alternative application: the finger measure is used for the two cubits, citing a Mishnah that states there were two cubits.

items.text: פתיחה: מידות האמה בשושן הבירה
items.text_en: Opening discussion on the fingerbreadth measure
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains the two cubit measures in Shushan, one larger by half a fingerbreadth and another larger by a full fingerbreadth, to prevent misuse of sacred vessels. It then connects this to a baraita about flesh between vertebrae.
items.desc: הקטע מתאר את מידות האמות שהיו בשושן הבירה, אחת גדולה ואחת קטנה, ומסביר את מטרתן: למנוע מעילה בהקדש. כמו כן מובאת דעת רב נחמן בר יצחק על שיעור אצבע כרבע טפח.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah describes two cubit measures in Shushan, one larger by half a fingerbreadth and another larger by a full fingerbreadth.
sub.desc: מתאר את מידות האמות שהיו בשושן הבירה ואת ההפרשים ביניהן.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why one measure was larger and one smaller, and answers that craftsmen would take from the smaller and return to the larger to prevent misuse of sacred vessels.
sub.desc: שואל מדוע היו שתי אמות שונות, ומסביר את מטרתן למנוע מעילה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why two measures are needed, and answers that one was for silver and gold and the other for building.
sub.desc: מבאר את הצורך בשתי אמות גדולות: אחת לכסף וזהב ואחת לבניין.

sub.text_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak (or Rav Huna bar Natan)
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak (or Rav Huna bar Natan) connects the fingerbreadth measure to a baraita about flesh between vertebrae being a full fingerbreadth.
sub.desc: מקשר את שיעור האצבע (רבע טפח) למשנה הקודמת העוסקת במומי בכור.

items.text: משנה: מום באשכים
items.text_en: Mishnah: Blemishes of testicles
items.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes related to missing or single testicle, with Rabbi Yishmael's test of two pouches and Rabbi Akiva's method of pressing. A story is told where Rabbi Akiva permitted and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri forbade.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת שבכור חסר ביצים או בעל ביצה אחת נשחט. רבי ישמעאל ורבי עקיבא נחלקו כיצד לברר את המצב, ומובא מעשה שבו נמצאה ביצה דבוקה בכסלים.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens by stating that an animal lacking testicles or having only one testicle is blemished.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין בכור בעל מום באשכים: חסר ביצים או ביצה אחת – נשחט.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yishmael provides a diagnostic criterion: two pouches indicate two testicles, one pouch indicates only one testicle.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין בכור בעל מום באשכים: חסר ביצים או ביצה אחת – נשחט.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Akiva proposes a physical test: seat the animal and press; if a testicle exists, it will eventually emerge.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין בכור בעל מום באשכים: חסר ביצים או ביצה אחת – נשחט.

sub.desc_en: A story is told where Rabbi Akiva pressed and the testicle did not emerge; after slaughter it was found attached to the flanks, and Rabbi Akiva permitted it while Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri forbade it.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין בכור בעל מום באשכים: חסר ביצים או ביצה אחת – נשחט.

items.text: Gemara: Clarifying the Mishnah's cases
items.text_en: Gemara: Clarifying the Mishnah's cases
items.desc_en: The Gemara resolves an apparent redundancy in the Mishnah by explaining that the case of 'only one testicle' is actually a missing condition: two testicles in one pouch or one testicle in two pouches. It then contrasts Rabbi Yishmael's reliance on pouches with Rabbi Akiva's physical examination.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions the Mishnah's phrasing: if 'only one testicle' is a blemish, then 'no testicles at all' should be even more obvious.
The Gemara resolves the redundancy by explaining that the Mishnah is missing a condition: it refers to having two testicles in one pouch or two pouches with one testicle.
Rabbi Yishmael states that two pouches indicate two testicles, while one pouch is like having only one testicle.
Rabbi Akiva rejects reliance on pouches and requires physical examination by sitting the animal on its rump and pressing.

items.text: The story of the pressed testicle and the dispute
items.text_en: The story of the pressed testicle and the dispute
items.desc_en: A baraita recounts a similar case in Peiran, where Rabbi Akiva permitted and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri forbade. Their heated exchange reveals the underlying issue: whether the animal is a tereifah or whether it was sacrificed outside the Temple.

sub.desc_en: A baraita recounts a case in Peiran where Rabbi Akiva permitted and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri forbade an animal whose testicle was pressed out and found stuck to the flanks.

sub.text: Rabbi Akiva's objection to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri
sub.text_en: Rabbi Akiva's objection to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Akiva objects that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri is wasting Israel's money by forbidding the animal.
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri retorts that Rabbi Akiva is feeding Israel neveilot (carcasses), since the animal was slaughtered without proper shechita.
The Gemara rejects the objection by noting that the animal was not a neveila but a tereifah (torn animal), which is also forbidden.
The Gemara resolves that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri's real objection was that Rabbi Akiva was causing Israelites to eat קדשים (sacred offerings) outside the Temple, which is forbidden.

items.text: Mishnah: Blemishes of limbs
items.text_en: Mishnah: Blemishes of limbs
items.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes of extra or missing legs, cloven hooves like a donkey, and dislocated or sunken hip (shachul and kasul).

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes of extra or missing legs, cloven hooves like a donkey, and dislocated or sunken hip (shachul and kasul).

items.text: Gemara: Extra limb and definitions of shachul and kasul
items.text_en: Gemara: Extra limb and definitions of shachul and kasul
items.desc_en: Rav Huna distinguishes between extra hand (blemish) and extra leg (terefah). Rav Pappa clarifies the condition for cloven hooves. A baraita defines shachul as a dislocated hip and kasul as one leg inside the flank, and adds sarua (protruding hip) and kalut (cloven like a donkey or horse).

sub.desc_en: Rav Huna distinguishes between an extra limb on the hand (a blemish) and on the leg (a terefah), applying the principle that anything extra is considered as if removed.
Rav Pappa clarifies that cloven hooves are a blemish even if the hoof is split, as long as it is rounded.
A baraita defines shachul as a dislocated hip, kasul as one leg inside the flank, and adds sarua (protruding hip) and kalut (cloven like a donkey or horse).

items.text: Mishnah: Broken bone and additional blemishes
items.text_en: Mishnah: Broken bone and additional blemishes
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that a broken limb bone is a blemish even if not externally visible, and lists three additional blemishes added by Rabbi Ilai in Yavneh (round eye, pig-like mouth, missing most of the tongue's speaker), which were later accepted by a later court.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that a broken limb bone is a blemish even if not externally visible.
The Mishnah reports that Rabbi Ilai enumerated these blemishes in Yavneh and the Sages agreed with him.
The Mishnah notes that Rabbi Ilai added three more blemishes, but the Sages initially said they had not heard of them.
The Mishnah lists the three added blemishes: a round eye like a human's, a mouth like a pig's, and removal of most of the speaker of the tongue.
The Mishnah concludes that a later court ruled that these are indeed blemishes.

items.text: Gemara: Clarifying the broken bone and the additional blemishes
items.text_en: Gemara: Clarifying the broken bone and the additional blemishes
items.desc_en: Rav Pappa explains that the broken bone is not visible by itself but is noticeable during work. The Gemara then addresses a contradiction regarding the round eye, resolved by Rav Yosef distinguishing between black and white animals. Rav Pappa clarifies the pig-like mouth, and the Gemara identifies the Mishnah's ruling on the tongue as following Rabbi Yehuda.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions how a broken bone that is not visible can be considered a blemish.
Rav Pappa explains that the broken bone is not visible by itself but is noticeable during work.
The Gemara raises a contradiction regarding the round eye from a baraita about miscarriages.
A baraita is cited stating that a woman who miscarries a non-human species must observe impurity according to its sex, per Rabbi Meir.

sub.text: Rabbi Yochanan (via Rabba bar bar Chana)
sub.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan (via Rabba bar bar Chana)
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan explains that Rabbi Meir's reasoning is based on the round eye of the fetus being like a human's.
Rav Yosef resolves the contradiction by distinguishing between black animals (where the round eye is normal) and white animals (where it is a blemish).
Rav Pappa clarifies that the pig-like mouth is defined by a split lip (פְּרִוס), even if not elongated (שְׁפִיד).
The Gemara identifies that the Mishnah's ruling on the tongue follows Rabbi Yehuda, who defines the blemish as the removal of most of the speaking part of the tongue.

items.text: משנה וגמרא: לסת תחתונה עודפת
items.text_en: Mishnah and Gemara: Lower jaw protruding
items.desc_en: The Mishnah recounts a case where the lower jaw protrudes, and Rabban Gamliel's court declared it a blemish. The Gemara explains that the Mishnah uses 'ma'aseh' because the Sages disagreed with Rabbi's ruling on the upper lip protruding, but agreed on the lower jaw protruding.
items.desc: המשנה מביאה מעשה שבו הלחי התחתון עודף על העליון, ורבן גמליאל פסק שזהו מום. הגמרא מבארת שהמחלוקת הקודמת על 'פה כחזיר' הייתה דווקא כשהשפה העליונה עודפת, אבל כשהתחתונה עודפת – כולם מודים שזה מום.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah recounts a case where the lower jaw protrudes beyond the upper, and Rabban Gamliel asked the sages, who ruled it a blemish.
sub.desc: המשנה מביאה מעשה שבו הלחי התחתון עודף על העליון, ורבן גמליאל שאל את החכמים ופסקו שזהו מום.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah uses the term 'ma'aseh' (story), and explains that it is because the sages disagreed with Rabbi's ruling on an upper lip protruding over the lower, but agreed that a lower jaw protruding over the upper is a blemish.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת: מהו התנא שהשמיענו את המעשה הזה? כלומר, מה החידוש שבא ללמדנו?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains that the Mishnah uses 'ומעשה' because the Sages disagreed with Rabbi regarding the upper lip protruding, but agreed that the lower jaw protruding is a blemish.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת: מהו התנא שהשמיענו את המעשה הזה? כלומר, מה החידוש שבא ללמדנו?

items.text: לסת תחתונה בולטת – מום בבהמה
items.text_en: Protruding lower jaw as a blemish
items.desc_en: The Mishnah recounts a case where the lower jaw protrudes, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel asked the Sages, who declared it a blemish. The Gemara questions why this applies to animals, given that for humans a similar condition is a blemish only for priests, based on a verse. Rav Pappa resolves the contradiction by distinguishing whether the protrusion contains a bone.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה מעשה שבו הלחי התחתונה בולטת על העליונה, ונפסק שזה מום. נשאלת קושיה מדוע זה נחשב מום בבהמה, הרי לגבי אדם נאמר שזה מום רק משום 'איש מזרע אהרן'. רב פפא מתרץ: ההבדל הוא אם יש עצם בלסת או לא.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah recounts a case where the lower jaw protrudes, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel asked the Sages, who declared it a blemish.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה מעשה שבו הלחי התחתונה בולטת על העליונה, ורבן שמעון בן גמליאל שואל את החכמים והם פוסקים שזה מום.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why this applies to animals, given that for humans a similar condition is a blemish only for priests, based on a verse.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: הרי לגבי אדם נאמר שזה מום רק משום 'איש מזרע אהרן', אבל בבהמה לא.

sub.desc_en: Rav Pappa resolves the contradiction by distinguishing whether the protrusion contains a bone.
sub.desc: רב פפא מתרץ: אין קושיה, כי כאן יש עצם בלסת התחתונה ושם אין עצם.

items.text: Mishnah: Doubled ear and pig-like tail
items.text_en: Mishnah: Doubled ear and pig-like tail
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that a kid's ear that is doubled is a blemish if it has a bone, but not if it lacks one. Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel adds that a kid's tail resembling a pig's, or lacking three vertebrae, is a blemish.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens with the rule that a kid's doubled ear is a blemish only if it contains a bone.
Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel adds that a kid's tail resembling a pig's or lacking three vertebrae is a blemish.

items.text: Gemara: Details of doubled ear and pig-like tail
items.text_en: Gemara: Details of doubled ear and pig-like tail
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites a baraita about a mouth or legs that are swollen due to wind (not a blemish) or bone (a blemish), and ears that are doubled in one cartilage (a blemish) or two (not). Rabban Gamliel discusses the pig-like tail, and Rav Pappa clarifies that it is not thin but curled, even if thick.

sub.desc_en: A baraita lists blemishes: a swollen mouth or legs from wind is not a blemish, but from bone it is; a doubled ear in one cartilage is a blemish, in two it is not.
Rav Pappa clarifies that the pig-like tail of a goat is not thin but curled, even if thick.

items.text: Number of tail vertebrae for a blemish
items.text_en: Number of tail vertebrae for a blemish
items.desc_en: Rav Huna rules that for a kid, two missing vertebrae is a blemish, three is not; for a lamb, three is a blemish, four is not. A challenge from a baraita states that for a kid, one is a blemish, two is not; for a lamb, two is a blemish, three is not. The Gemara concludes that Rav Huna was mistaken because he thought the entire Mishnah referred to a kid, but the first clause is about a kid and the latter about a lamb.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that a tail lacking three vertebrae is a blemish.
Rav Huna rules: for a goat, two missing vertebrae is a blemish, three is not; for a lamb, three is a blemish, four is not.
A baraita contradicts Rav Huna: for a goat, one missing vertebra is a blemish, two is not; for a lamb, two is a blemish, three is not — a refutation of Rav Huna.
The Gemara explains that Rav Huna was misled by the Mishnah: he thought the entire Mishnah referred to a goat, but the first part is about a goat and the latter part about a lamb.

items.text: Mishnah: Other blemishes (yabelet, eye, ear, etc.)
items.text_en: Mishnah: Other blemishes (yabelet, eye, ear, etc.)
items.desc_en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus lists blemishes: a yabelet in the eye, a broken bone in hand or foot, a dislocated jawbone, one eye or ear larger than the other in appearance but not in measurement. Rabbi Yehuda adds that one testicle being as large as two of the other is a blemish, but the Sages disagree.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes: a יבלת (wart) in the eye, a broken bone in hand or foot, a dislocated jaw, one eye or ear larger than the other (in appearance but not measure), and Rabbi Yehuda's disputed case of one testicle twice the size of the other.
Rabbi Yehuda adds that one testicle being as large as two of the other is a blemish.
The Sages disagree with Rabbi Yehuda and do not consider this a blemish.

items.text: Gemara: Resolving contradictions about yabelet
items.text_en: Gemara: Resolving contradictions about yabelet
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether a yabelet is a blemish, citing a contradiction from a baraita that lists a ba'al yabelet as one who may not be slaughtered in the Temple or the provinces. It resolves that the Torah's yabelet (with a bone) is a blemish only on the body, while the Mishnah's yabelet (without a bone) is a blemish in the eye. Further distinctions are made regarding location (black vs. white of the eye) and presence of hair.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether a yabelet is a blemish, citing a contradiction from a baraita that lists a ba'al yabelet as one who may not be slaughtered in the Temple or the provinces.
The Gemara initially resolves that the Torah's yabelet (with a bone) is a blemish on the body, while the Mishnah's yabelet (without a bone) is a blemish in the eye.
The Gemara objects that the verse is general, so the distinction between body and eye is insufficient, and refines the resolution: the Torah's yabelet has a bone, the Mishnah's does not.
The Gemara clarifies that the Torah's yabelet (with a bone) is a blemish in the eye, but on the body it is not a blemish.
The Gemara objects that a yabelet without a bone on the body is still a disqualifying growth, citing a baraita about ba'alei tilulin.
The Gemara resolves that both cases are in the eye, distinguishing between the black and white of the eye.
The Gemara objects that there are no blemishes in the white of the eye, and resolves with Reish Lakish's distinction: one with hair, one without.

items.text: Gemara: Size of eye and ear differences
items.text_en: Gemara: Size of eye and ear differences
items.desc_en: A baraita defines a large eye as like a calf's and a small one as like a goose's. Regarding the ear, the Rabbis discuss the measure, and Acheirim say that even if the smaller ear is only a fold compared to the larger, it is still fit.

sub.desc_en: A baraita defines the size of a large eye as like a calf's and a small eye as like a goose's.
The Gemara asks about the measure for a large and small ear.
Acheirim answer that even if the smaller ear is only a fold compared to the larger, it is still fit.

items.text: זנב עגל שאינו מגיע לערקוב
items.text_en: Mishnah: Tail of a calf and the definition of arkub
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that a calf's tail that does not reach the arkub (hock) is not a blemish because all calves are initially that way and grow. Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus defines the arkub as the one in the middle of the thigh.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת שזנב עגל שאינו מגיע לערקוב (מפרק שבאמצע הירך) הוא מום, שכן כל העגלים גדלים כך שזנבם נמתח. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס מפרש שמדובר בערקוב שבאמצע הירך.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah discusses a calf's tail that does not reach the ערקוב (hock), stating that all calves are initially that way and grow, and Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonos defines the ערקוב (hock) as the one in the middle of the thigh.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין זנב עגל שאינו מגיע לערקוב, וקובעת שזהו מום, שכן כל העגלים גדלים וזנבם נמתח.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus defines the arkub as the one in the middle of the thigh.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בדין זנב עגל שאינו מגיע לערקוב, וקובעת שזהו מום, שכן כל העגלים גדלים וזנבם נמתח.

items.text: פתיחת הגמרא על קפץ העליון
items.text_en: Opening Tosefta on a camel's blemish
items.desc_en: A Tosefta is cited describing a blemish in a camel that is analogous to the upper and lower eyelid in an animal.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא המבארת את המונח 'קפץ העליון' במשנה הקודמת, ומבדילה בינו לבין קפץ התחתון, תוך ציון ההבדל בין עגל לגמל.

sub.desc_en: A Tosefta is cited describing a blemish in a camel analogous to the upper and lower eyelid in an animal.

items.text: משנה: מומין המתירים שחיטה ופדייה
items.text_en: Gemara's question on the Mishnah's redundancy
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah repeats the list of blemishes for slaughtering a firstborn, and explains that the latter part is necessary to include that disqualified consecrated animals may be redeemed for these blemishes, and that the Mishnah is a unified statement of an individual opinion.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת שעל המומין המנויים שוחטים את הבכור ופודים קדשים פסולים. הגמרא דנה בצורך במילים נוספות אלו, ומסיקה שהן באות לקבוע הלכה כדעת היחידים שהוזכרו קודם.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that for these blemishes one slaughters the firstborn and disqualified consecrated animals may be redeemed.
The Gemara questions the redundancy of the Mishnah's statement and asks why the latter clause about redemption is needed.
The Gemara explains that the Mishnah's latter clause is necessary to establish the halakha as a unified statement of individual opinions, countering the earlier dispute about additional blemishes.

items.text: משנה: מומין שאין שוחטים עליהם
items.text_en: Mishnah: Blemishes that do not permit slaughter
items.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes for which a firstborn may not be slaughtered either in the Temple or in the provinces, including certain skin conditions, old age, sickness, and others. It also discusses the tumtum and androgynos, with Rabbi Shimon and the Sages disputing their status.
items.desc: המשנה מפרטת מומין שאינם מתירים שחיטת בכור לא במקדש ולא במדינה, כולל גרב, חזזית, זקן, חולה, מזוהם, טומטום ואנדרוגינוס, ומביאה מחלוקת בין רבי שמעון לחכמים.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes for which a firstborn may not be slaughtered either in the Temple or in the provinces, including eye conditions, skin diseases, old age, sickness, foul odor, and animals involved in transgression or killing.

The Mishnah states that a tumtum and androgynos are not slaughtered in either location; Rabbi Shimon considers the androgynos a major blemish, while the Sages rule it is not a firstborn and may be shorn and worked.

items.text: גמרא: בירור מומין גרב וחזזית
items.text_en: Gemara's resolution of contradictions regarding garav and yalefet
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why garav and yalefet are listed as non-permitting blemishes when they appear in the Torah as blemishes. It resolves by distinguishing between moist and dry forms, and between Egyptian and ordinary yalefet, and further explains three types of garav.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה שגרב וחזזית מופיעים בתורה כמומין, ומתרצת שיש הבדל בין גרב לח (מתרפא) לגרב יבש (שאינו מתרפא), וכן מבחינה בין שלושה סוגי גרב.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why garav and yallefet are listed as non-blemishes, citing verses and a baraita with Resh Lakish's explanation.
The Gemara resolves the contradiction by distinguishing between Egyptian and ordinary yallefet, and between moist and dry garav.
The Gemara objects that moist garav is also incurable, citing the verse about the Egyptian boil.
The Gemara resolves by positing three types of garav: dry inside and out, moist outside and inside, and the Egyptian type with dry inside and moist outside.

items.text: גמרא: מקור לפסול זקן, חולה ומזוהם
items.text_en: Source for excluding old, sick, and repulsive animals
items.desc_en: The Gemara derives from a verse that old, sick, and repulsive animals are excluded from being offerings, and explains why each exclusion is necessary.
items.desc: הגמרא דורשת את הפסולים 'זקן', 'חולה' ו'מזוהם' ממילות המיעוט 'מן' שבפסוק, ומסבירה מדוע יש צורך בשלושתן.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks the source for the exclusion of the old, sick, and repulsive animals, and cites a baraita deriving it from verses.
The Gemara explains why all three exclusions are necessary, as each alone might not cover the others.
The Gemara further explains that even two exclusions would not suffice, so all three are needed.

items.text: גמרא: מקור לפסול בעלי עבירה והורג אדם
items.text_en: Source for animals that committed a transgression
items.desc_en: The Gemara derives from verses that animals that have been used for bestiality, worshipped, set aside, or gored are excluded, and notes that these are capital cases but the Mishnah allows slaughter based on one witness or the owner's testimony.
items.desc: הגמרא דורשת פסולים אלו ממילות המיעוט שבפסוק, ומסבירה שהפסול חל גם על פי עד אחד או בעלים, אף שאין בהם דין מיתה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks for the scriptural source of the Mishnah's list of animals that committed a transgression.
A baraita derives from the verse 'מן הבהמה' (from the animal) that animals used for bestiality, worshipped, set aside, or gored are excluded from the category of firstborn.
The Gemara objects that these animals are capital cases (liable to execution), yet the Mishnah allows slaughter based on one witness or the owner's testimony.
The Gemara resolves that the Mishnah's leniency applies specifically to slaughter based on one witness or the owner's testimony, not to the capital case itself.

items.text: גמרא: דין טומטום ואנדרוגינוס
items.text_en: Discussion of tumtum and androgynos
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains why a tumtum cannot be slaughtered in the Temple or provinces, and questions why an androgynos cannot be slaughtered in the provinces since its female organ could be considered a חָרוּץ. Abaye and Rava debate whether a חָרוּץ in a fleshy place is a blemish, and Rabbi Yishmael's opinion is reconciled.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה בטעם הפסול של טומטום ואנדרוגינוס, ומביאה מחלוקת בין אביי, רבא ורבי ישמעאל בשאלה אם נקבות האנדרוגינוס נחשבת מום 'חרוץ' המתיר שחיטה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains why a tumtum cannot be slaughtered in the Temple (possibly female) or in the provinces (possibly male without a blemish).
The Gemara questions why an androgynos cannot be slaughtered in the provinces, since its female organ could be considered a חָרוּץ (a blemish).
Abaye argues that a חָרוּץ (a split) is only a blemish when it is in a bony place, like a fracture, not in a fleshy place.
Rava argues that a חָרוּץ in a fleshy place is not a blemish, as proven by the Torah's inclusion of גָּרָב (a dry scab) alongside חָרוּץ, implying that a simple split in flesh is not a blemish.

The Gemara reconciles Rabbi Yishmael's opinion that an androgynos has a great blemish: he does not accept Abaye's or Rava's reasoning, but considers the androgynos a ״מוּם רָע״ (a severe blemish) because it is recognizable.

items.text: קושיית רבא על טעמו של רבי ישמעאל
items.text_en: Rava's inquiry about Rabbi Yishmael's position
items.desc_en: Rava asks whether Rabbi Yishmael is certain that an androginos is a firstborn with its blemish, or whether he is uncertain and speaks hypothetically. The practical difference concerns liability for shearing and work, and giving it to a priest.
items.desc: רבא מעלה ספק האם רבי ישמעאל רואה באנדרוגינוס בכור ודאי עם מומו, או שמא הוא מסתפק ואומר 'אם תמצא לומר'. הגמרא מבהירה את הנפקא מינה: מלקות על גיזה ועבודה, או נתינה לכהן.

sub.desc_en: Rava asks whether Rabbi Yishmael is certain that an androginos is a firstborn with its blemish, or whether he is uncertain and speaks hypothetically.
sub.desc: רבא מעלה ספק האם רבי ישמעאל רואה באנדרוגינוס בכור ודאי עם מומו, או שמא הוא מסתפק ואומר 'אם תמצא לומר'.

sub.desc_en: The gemara clarifies the practical difference: liability for shearing and work, or giving it to a priest.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה את הנפקא מינה: מלקות על גיזה ועבודה, או נתינה לכהן.

items.text: ברייתא ראשונה: רבי אילעאי בשם רבי ישמעאל
items.text_en: First attempted proof from Rabbi Ila'i's statement
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites Rabbi Ila'i in the name of Rabbi Yishmael who states definitively that an androginos is a firstborn with its blemish. This suggests certainty, but the Gemara deflects that it might still be a hypothetical statement.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא שבה רבי אילעאי אומר בשם רבי ישמעאל שאנדרוגינוס בכור הוא ומומו עמו. הגמרא דנה האם זה מוכיח שרבי ישמעאל פשיטא ליה, או שמא גם כאן אמר 'אם תמצא לומר'.

sub.desc_en: The gemara brings a baraita where Rabbi Ila'i says in Rabbi Yishmael's name that an androginos is a firstborn with its blemish, suggesting certainty.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא בשם רבי אילעאי ורבי ישמעאל הקובעת שאנדרוגינוס בכור הוא ומומו עמו, ומסיקה מכאן שרבי ישמעאל פשיטא ליה.

sub.desc_en: The gemara objects that Rabbi Ila'i might be speaking hypothetically, not from certainty.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא בשם רבי אילעאי ורבי ישמעאל הקובעת שאנדרוגינוס בכור הוא ומומו עמו, ומסיקה מכאן שרבי ישמעאל פשיטא ליה.

items.text: Second proof from the baraita on 'zakhar'
items.text_en: Second proof from the baraita on 'zakhar'
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita that excludes tumtum and androginos from the firstborn law based on the word 'zakhar'. It questions who authored it: if the first tanna, who treats it as a doubt, a verse would not exclude a doubt; if later rabbis, they derive from one verse, but the Gemara notes that only one 'zakhar' is written regarding firstborns.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita that excludes tumtum and androginos from the firstborn law based on the word 'zakhar'.
The Gemara questions who authored the baraita: if it is the first tanna, who treats the case as a doubt, would a verse come to exclude a doubt?
The Gemara answers that the baraita must be from the later rabbis (רבנן בתראי), who derive from one verse, but notes that only one 'zakhar' is written regarding firstborns.

items.text: Resolution: Rabbi Yishmael is certain
items.text_en: Resolution: Rabbi Yishmael is certain
items.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that Rabbi Yishmael must be certain, because if he were uncertain, a verse would not be needed to exclude a doubt. The verse is necessary only if he is certain, to exclude the androginos from the law.

sub.desc_en: The gemara resolves that Rabbi Yishmael is certain, because if he were uncertain, a verse would not be needed to exclude a doubt.

items.text: תירוץ: שני כתובים בבכור
items.text_en: Alternative: Two verses for later rabbis
items.desc_en: The Gemara offers an alternative: the later rabbis might rely on two verses ('hazakhar' and 'hazekharim') written regarding firstborns, so the proof is not decisive.
items.desc: הגמרא מתרצת שהברייתא היא כרבנן בתראי, ובבכור יש שני כתובים ('הזכר' ו'הזכרים') – אחד למעט נקבה ואחד למעט טומטום ואנדרוגינוס, כך שאין קושיה.

sub.desc_en: The gemara objects that the later rabbis might have two verses, 'הַזָּכָר' and 'הַזְּכָרִים', to exclude both cases.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת שהברייתא היא כרבנן בתראי, ובבכור יש שני כתובים – אחד למעט נקבה ואחד למעט טומטום ואנדרוגינוס, כך שאין קושיה.

items.text: Rav Chisda's distinction between androginos and tumtum
items.text_en: Rav Chisda's distinction between androginos and tumtum
items.desc_en: Rav Chisda states that the dispute between Rabbi Yishmael and the Sages is only about an androginos, but regarding a tumtum, all agree it is a doubt and it is sanctified as a firstborn only doubtfully.

sub.desc_en: Rav Chisda states that the dispute is only about an androginos, but regarding a tumtum, all agree it is a doubt and it is sanctified as a doubt.

items.text: Rava's challenge from valuations
items.text_en: Rava's challenge from valuations
items.desc_en: Rava challenges Rav Chisda: if a tumtum is a doubt, then should it be valued in valuations (arakhin)? This begins a new discussion.

sub.desc_en: Rava asks Rav Chisda whether, according to his position, a tumtum would be valued in the system of valuations (ערכין).

items.text: ניסיונות לפשוט את הספק מברייתאות על ערכין וקרבנות
items.text_en: Four baraitot excluding tumtum and androgynos from firstborn and valuations
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings four baraitot that each derive from a verse that tumtum and androgynos are excluded from the laws of firstborn (bekhor) and valuations (arakhin). Each baraita ends with the phrase 'סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם' (rely on this for tumtum).
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ארבע ברייתאות המלמדות שטומטום ואנדרוגינוס אינם בכלל 'זכר' לעניין ערכין, קרבן שלמים ועולה. בכל פעם הגמרא דוחה את הראיה ואומרת 'סמי מיכן טומטום', כלומר יש למחוק את המילה 'טומטום' מהברייתא, כי הברייתא עוסקת רק באנדרוגינוס.

sub.desc_en: The first baraita derives from the verse 'הַזָּכָר' (the male) that tumtum and androgynos are excluded from the law of firstborn, and concludes with the phrase 'סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם' (rely on this for tumtum).
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה מברייתא האומרת שטומטום ואנדרוגינוס אינם בכלל 'זכר' לעניין ערכין, ודוחה את הראיה באומרה שיש למחוק את המילה 'טומטום' מהברייתא.

sub.desc_en: The second baraita considers whether a tumtum or androgynos might be subject to valuations (ערך) as a woman, and derives from the verse 'הַזָּכָר... אִם נְקֵבָה' that they are excluded.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא נוספת המלמדת שטומטום ואנדרוגינוס אינם בכלל 'זכר' או 'נקבה' לעניין ערכין, ודוחה אותה באותו אופן.

sub.desc_en: The third baraita interprets 'אִם זָכָר אִם נְקֵבָה' (if male if female) to mean a definite male or definite female, excluding tumtum and androgynos.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא שלישית המלמדת שטומטום ואנדרוגינוס אינם בכלל 'זכר' או 'נקבה' לעניין קרבן שלמים, ודוחה אותה באותו אופן.

sub.desc_en: The fourth baraita derives from the repetition of 'זָכָר' (male) in the verse that it comes to exclude tumtum and androgynos.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא רביעית המלמדת שטומטום ואנדרוגינוס אינם כשרים לעולה, ודוחה אותה באותו אופן.

items.text: ברייתא על טומאת בגדים בבית הבליעה
items.text_en: Rabbi Eliezer's dispute about tumtum and androgynos in bird offerings
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita where Rabbi Eliezer rules that tumtum and androgynos do not defile garments at the gullet (beit ha-beli'ah) for bird offerings, because the verse says 'zakar u'nekevah' which excludes them. For birds, where no such verse is said, they are not excluded. The Gemara again concludes 'סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם'.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא שבה נחלקו תנאים אם טומטום ואנדרוגינוס מטמאים בגדים בבית הבליעה. רבי אליעזר פוטר, משום שסובר שהם כשרים לקרבן עוף, שכן לא נאמר בו 'זכר ונקבה'. מכאן משמע שטומטום אינו ספק, שהרי התנא הראשון מטמא אותו. הגמרא דוחה שוב: 'סמי מיכן טומטום'.

sub.desc_en: The baraita lists animals that are disqualified for sacrifice, including tumtum and androgynos, and states that all of them defile garments at the gullet (בית הבליעה) for bird offerings.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא הקובעת שטומטום ואנדרוגינוס מטמאים בגדים בבית הבליעה, ומכאן שהם נחשבים לבעלי חיים פסולים ולא ספק.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Eliezer disputes the Tanna Kamma, ruling that tumtum and androgynos do not defile garments at the gullet, because the verse uses 'זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה' (male and female), which excludes them.
sub.desc: רבי אליעזר חולק ופוטר טומטום ואנדרוגינוס מטומאת בגדים, משום שסובר שהם כשרים לקרבן עוף, שכן לא נאמר בו 'זכר ונקבה'.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that for bird offerings, where the verse does not say 'זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה' (male and female), tumtum and androgynos are not excluded, so the baraita's ruling stands; the Gemara marks this with 'סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם' (draw from here regarding tumtum).
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה את הראיה מהברייתא באומרה 'סמי מיכן טומטום', כלומר יש למחוק את טומטום מהברייתא, כי היא עוסקת רק באנדרוגינוס.

items.text: ברייתא על טריפה, כלאיים ויוצא דופן
items.text_en: Rabbi Elazar's list of animals that cannot be consecrated or cause temurah
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita where Rabbi Elazar lists tereifah, kil'ayim, yotzei dofen, tumtum, and androgynos as animals that are not holy and cannot make something else holy through temurah. Shmuel explains that 'not holy' means for temurah, and 'cannot make holy' means to effect temurah. The Gemara again concludes 'סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם'.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא שבה רבי אלעזר מונה חמישה שאינם קדושים ואינם מקדישים, ובהם טומטום ואנדרוגינוס. שמואל מבאר שאינם קדושים בתמורה ואינם מקדישים לעשות תמורה. הגמרא דוחה שוב: 'סמי מיכן טומטום'.

sub.desc_en: A baraita is cited in which Rabbi Elazar lists tereifah, kil'ayim, yotzei dofen, tumtum, and androgynos as animals that are not holy and cannot cause temurah.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא שבה רבי אלעזר מונה טומטום ואנדרוגינוס בין חמישה שאינם קדושים ואינם מקדישים.

sub.desc_en: Shmuel explains that 'not holy' refers to temurah and 'cannot make holy' refers to effecting temurah.
sub.desc: שמואל מבאר שהכוונה שאינם קדושים בתמורה ואינם מקדישים לעשות תמורה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that this baraita also supports the proof regarding tumtum.
sub.desc: שמואל מבאר שהכוונה שאינם קדושים בתמורה ואינם מקדישים לעשות תמורה.

items.text: גרסה אחרת של ברייתא רבי אלעזר
items.text_en: Objection from a different version of Rabbi Elazar's list
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings another version of Rabbi Elazar's list that includes only five items: tereifah, kil'ayim, yotzei dofen, tumtum, and androgynos. If one were to say 'סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם' from the previous baraita, that would make four items, but here there are five. The Gemara resolves that the extra item is 'yatom' (an orphaned animal), not tumtum.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה גרסה אחרת של ברייתא רבי אלעזר, שבה נמנים חמישה: טריפה, כלאיים, יוצא דופן, טומטום ואנדרוגינוס. אם נאמר 'סמי מיכן טומטום', נשארו רק ארבעה. הגמרא מתרצת: יש למחוק את טומטום ולהכניס במקומו 'יתום' (בן שנולד לאחר מיתת אמו).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that if one were to exclude tumtum from Rabbi Elazar's list of five items, only four would remain, contradicting the explicit count of five.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה גרסה אחרת של ברייתא רבי אלעזר, שבה נמנים חמישה: טריפה, כלאיים, יוצא דופן, טומטום ואנדרוגינוס.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the list actually substitutes 'yatom' (an orphaned animal) for tumtum, preserving the count of five.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה גרסה אחרת של ברייתא רבי אלעזר, שבה נמנים חמישה: טריפה, כלאיים, יוצא דופן, טומטום ואנדרוגינוס.

items.text: מחלוקת התנאים: טומטום כיצור מובחן או ספק
items.text_en: Dispute among tanna'im about androgynos and tumtum as firstborn
items.desc_en: The Gemara presents a dispute: Rabbi Il'ai in the name of Rabbi Yishmael says an androgynos is a firstborn with its blemish, but the Sages say no sanctity applies. Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Shimon says the verse 'hazakhar' excludes tumtum and androgynos. The Gemara questions whether Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda is the same as the Sages, and concludes that the difference is tumtum: the first tanna holds no sanctity for androgynos but tumtum is a safek and is holy from safek, while Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda holds that tumtum is also excluded.
items.desc: הגמרא מציעה שהמחלוקת היא בין תנאים: רבי שמעון בן יהודה אומר שטומטום ואנדרוגינוס אינם בכלל 'זכר', משמע שהם יצור מובחן. חכמים חולקים וסוברים שאנדרוגינוס אינו קדוש, אבל טומטום הוא ספק ולכן קדוש מספק. הגמרא מסיקה שזו היא המחלוקת האמיתית.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks whether the dispute about tumtum and androgynos aligns with a tannaic dispute.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת בהצעה שהמחלוקת היא בין תנאים, ומביאה את דברי רבי אילעאי בשם רבי ישמעאל, חכמים, ורבי שמעון בן יהודה בשם רבי שמעון.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Il'ai in the name of Rabbi Yishmael states that an androgynos is a firstborn and its blemish is with it (i.e., it is sanctified but can be redeemed).
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת בהצעה שהמחלוקת היא בין תנאים, ומביאה את דברי רבי אילעאי בשם רבי ישמעאל, חכמים, ורבי שמעון בן יהודה בשם רבי שמעון.

sub.desc_en: The Sages disagree and say that no sanctity applies to an androgynos as a firstborn.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת בהצעה שהמחלוקת היא בין תנאים, ומביאה את דברי רבי אילעאי בשם רבי ישמעאל, חכמים, ורבי שמעון בן יהודה בשם רבי שמעון.

sub.text_en: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda citing Rabbi Shimon
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Shimon cites the verse 'hazakhar' to exclude both tumtum and androgynos from firstborn sanctity.
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה את האפשרות שדעת רבי שמעון בן יהודה זהה לחכמים, ומסבירה שהמחלוקת האמיתית היא על טומטום: חכמים רואים אותו כספק וקדוש מספק, ואילו רבי שמעון פוסל אותו לחלוטין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda's position is identical to the Sages, and if so, what is the difference between them.
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה את האפשרות שדעת רבי שמעון בן יהודה זהה לחכמים, ומסבירה שהמחלוקת האמיתית היא על טומטום: חכמים רואים אותו כספק וקדוש מספק, ואילו רבי שמעון פוסל אותו לחלוטין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the difference is tumtum: the first tanna holds no sanctity for androgynos but tumtum is a safek and is holy from safek, while Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda holds that tumtum is also excluded.
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה את האפשרות שדעת רבי שמעון בן יהודה זהה לחכמים, ומסבירה שהמחלוקת האמיתית היא על טומטום: חכמים רואים אותו כספק וקדוש מספק, ואילו רבי שמעון פוסל אותו לחלוטין.

items.text: Question about Ben Yehuda's statement on tumtum
items.text_en: Question about Ben Yehuda's statement on tumtum
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether Ben Yehuda's statement implies that a tumtum is a distinct creation (beriah) and not sanctified. It clarifies that the dispute is not about a tumtum being a beriah, but about a safek of male or female.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether Ben Yehuda's statement implies that a tumtum is a distinct creation (בריה) and therefore not sanctified.
The Gemara rejects the implication, clarifying that the dispute is not about a tumtum being a distinct creation, but about it being a ספק (doubt) of male or female.

items.text: Dispute about a creature that urinates from the female organ
items.text_en: Dispute about a creature that urinates from the female organ
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that all agree a creature urinating from the male organ is male; the dispute is about one urinating from the female organ. One opinion fears the male organ may have inverted to female, while the other does not. Rabbi Elazar ruled that such an animal is chullin (non-sacred).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara states that all agree a creature urinating from the male organ is male, and the dispute is only about one urinating from the female organ: one opinion fears the male organ may have inverted, the other does not.
Rabbi Elazar ruled that an animal urinating from the female organ is חולין (non-sacred), supporting the position that does not fear inversion.

items.text: תמיהת רבי יוחנן על רבי אלעזר
items.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan's objection and resolution
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan questions Rabbi Elazar's ruling, asking who disregards the first tanna and Rabbi Yishmael. The Gemara suggests Rabbi Yochanan could have cited Rav Chisda's distinction between androgynos and tumtum, but Rabbi Yochanan does not accept that. He instead aligns with the later rabbis, noting that one does not abandon two opinions for one.
items.desc: רבי יוחנן תמה על רבי אלעזר שאינו חושש לדעת התנא קמא ורבי ישמעאל. הגמרא מסבירה שרבי יוחנן אינו סובר כרב חסדא, ולכן שואל מי עוזב שניים ועושה כאחד.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan objects to Rabbi Elazar's ruling, asking who disregards both the first tanna and Rabbi Yishmael.
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן תמה על רבי אלעזר שאינו חושש לדעת התנא קמא ורבי ישמעאל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests that Rabbi Yochanan could have cited Rav Chisda's distinction between an androgynos (אנדרוגינוס) and a tumtum (טומטום), where all agree the tumtum is a case of ספק (doubt).
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן תמה על רבי אלעזר שאינו חושש לדעת התנא קמא ורבי ישמעאל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains that Rabbi Yochanan does not accept Rav Chisda's position, and instead aligns with the later rabbis, noting that one does not abandon two opinions for one.
sub.desc: הגמרא מסבירה שרבי יוחנן אינו סובר כרב חסדא, ולכן שואל מי עוזב שניים ועושה כאחד.

items.text: שיטת רבי אלעזר וריש לקיש
items.text_en: Reish Lakish's explanation and Rav Oshaya's objection
items.desc_en: Reish Lakish explains that the doubt about a tumtum applies only to humans, because their male and female organs are in the same place, but for animals, urination location determines sex. Rav Oshaya objects, fearing inversion of the organ, but Reish Lakish dismisses this as following Rabbi Meir's concern for a minority.
items.desc: רבי אלעזר סובר כריש לקיש, המבחין בין אדם לבהמה: באדם הספק קיים כי מקום הזכרות והנקבות שווה, אך בבהמה ניתן לקבוע מין לפי מקום ההשתנה. רב אושעיא מקשה שמא נהפכה זכרותו לנקבותו, ועונים לו שזו דעת רבי מאיר החושש למיעוט.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks whose opinion Rabbi Elazar follows in his ruling about a tumtum animal.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת לאיזה חכם נשען רבי אלעזר בפסקו, ומשיבה שסבר כריש לקיש המבחין בין אדם לבהמה: בבהמה מקום ההשתנה קובע את המין.

sub.desc_en: Reish Lakish explains that the doubt about a tumtum applies only to humans, because their male and female organs are in the same place, but for animals, urination location determines sex.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת לאיזה חכם נשען רבי אלעזר בפסקו, ומשיבה שסבר כריש לקיש המבחין בין אדם לבהמה: בבהמה מקום ההשתנה קובע את המין.

sub.desc_en: Rav Oshaya objects, fearing that the organ might have inverted, making urination location unreliable.
sub.desc: רב אושעיא מקשה שיש לחשוש שמא זכרותו נהפכה לנקבותו, ועונה לו אביי שזו דעת רבי מאיר החושש למיעוט, ואין הלכה כמותו.

sub.desc_en: Reish Lakish dismisses the objection, noting that such a concern follows only Rabbi Meir, who worries about a minority case.
sub.desc: רב אושעיא מקשה שיש לחשוש שמא זכרותו נהפכה לנקבותו, ועונה לו אביי שזו דעת רבי מאיר החושש למיעוט, ואין הלכה כמותו.

items.text: דין 'הואיל ואישתני אישתני'
items.text_en: The principle of 'ishtani' (changed status)
items.desc_en: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Chananya bar Avin state that even according to the rabbis, since the tumtum's status has changed (ishtani), it is considered changed. There is a dispute whether we say 'ishtani' or not.
items.desc: אביי בר אבין ורב חנניא בר אבין מציעים שאפילו לרבנן יש לחשוש לשינוי, משום שכבר השתנה. מובאת מחלוקת אם אומרים 'הואיל ואישתני אישתני' או לא.

sub.text: אביי בר אבין ורב חנניא בר אבין
sub.text_en: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Chananya bar Avin
sub.desc_en: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Chananya bar Avin state that even according to the rabbis, since the tumtum's status has changed (ishtani), it is considered changed.
sub.desc: אביי בר אבין ורב חנניא בר אבין מציעים שאפילו לרבנן יש לחשוש לשינוי, משום שכבר השתנה, ומציינים שיש מחלוקת אם אומרים 'הואיל ואישתני אישתני' או לא.

sub.text: אביי בר אבין ורב חנניא בר אבין
sub.desc_en: The gemara records a dispute: one opinion says we apply the principle of ishtani (changed status), and another says we do not.
sub.desc: אביי בר אבין ורב חנניא בר אבין מציעים שאפילו לרבנן יש לחשוש לשינוי, משום שכבר השתנה, ומציינים שיש מחלוקת אם אומרים 'הואיל ואישתני אישתני' או לא.

items.text: Tannaitic dispute about tumtum's halakhic status for yibbum and chalitzah
items.text_en: Tannaitic dispute about tumtum's halakhic status for yibbum and chalitzah
items.desc_en: The Gemara examines two baraitot: one allows a tumtum to perform chalitzah and yibbum, the other only allows chalitzah. It initially suggests the dispute is about the 'ishtani' principle, but concludes both agree on 'ishtani'; the difference is between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva. The Gemara then identifies the tanna behind Rabbi Akiva's view as Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda, who fears the tumtum might be found to be a saris chamah or a female.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks whether the dispute about the tumtum's status for yibbum and chalitzah is based on the principle of 'ishtani' (changed), citing two baraitot: one allowing both chalitzah and yibbum, the other only chalitzah.

The Gemara assumes both baraitot follow Rabbi Akiva, who says a saris chamah does not perform chalitzah or yibbum, and proposes that the dispute is about whether we apply the principle 'ishtani' (changed) to the tumtum.
The Gemara rejects this, stating that both baraitot agree on the 'ishtani' principle; the difference is between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva.
The Gemara asks who is the tanna behind Rabbi Akiva's view, and rejects Rabbi Yehuda because he explicitly considers a tumtum found to be male as a saris.
The Gemara identifies the tanna as Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda, who fears the tumtum might be found to be a saris chamah or a female.

items.text: Rava's question on the difference between the opinions
items.text_en: Rava's question on the difference between the opinions
items.desc_en: Rava asks what practical difference exists between the two explanations of Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda's concern (fear of finding a female vs. fear of finding a saris chamah).

sub.desc_en: Rava asks what practical difference exists between the two explanations of Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda's concern (fear of finding a female vs. fear of finding a saris chamah).

items.text: Conclusion of previous discussion
items.text_en: Conclusion of previous discussion
items.desc_en: The Gemara concludes a prior debate about the difference between disqualifying a priest from service when there are other priests and exempting him from the firstborn redemption when there are no other priests.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes the prior debate by stating that the difference between disqualifying a priest from service when there are other priests and exempting him from the firstborn redemption when there are no other priests is the practical distinction between the two cases.

items.text: Return to the Mishnah
items.text_en: Return to the Mishnah
items.desc_en: The Gemara signals a return to the Mishnah's list of blemishes.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara marks the end of the previous chapter and the beginning of a new one with the formula 'we return to you, regarding these blemishes'.

items.text: משנת מומין הפוסלים באדם
items.text_en: Mishnah: Additional blemishes in humans
items.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes that disqualify a priest, including the kilon, laftan, makkan, a sunken head, a skull that is flat, and those with warts. Rabbi Yehuda permits those with warts while the Sages disqualify them. The Mishnah also defines a bald person as one without a continuous line of hair from ear to ear.
items.desc: המשנה מפרטת מומין הפוסלים כהן לעבודה, כולל מומין המשותפים עם בהמה ומומין מיוחדים לאדם, כגון ראש כילון, לפתן, מקובן, שקוט, סקיפס, בעלי חטרות, וקירח.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah lists blemishes that disqualify a priest, both permanent and temporary, and adds additional ones specific to humans: the כילון (pointed head), הלפתן (turnip head), המקבן (hammer head), one whose head is שקט (sunken), and סקיפת (a skull with a flat back).
The Mishnah records a dispute: Rabbi Yehuda validates a priest with bald patches (בעלי חטרות), while the Sages disqualify him.
The Mishnah rules that a bald priest (קֵּרֵחַ) is disqualified, defining it as one who lacks a continuous line of hair from ear to ear; if he has such a line, he is fit.

items.text: קושיית הגמרא על שוויון המומין
items.text_en: Gemara's question and derivation via gezerah shavah
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah lists blemishes not explicitly written in the Torah for humans (yabelet) and for animals (dak tevallul). It answers via a gezerah shavah from the words 'garav' and 'yallefet' that appear in both contexts. The Gemara explains that the gezerah shavah is 'free' (mufneh) to prevent refutation.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מדוע המומין הפוסלים בבהמה פוסלים גם באדם, הרי יש מומין שלא נכתבו באדם (יבלת) ובבהמה (דק תבלול)? התשובה: לימוד בגזירה שווה מ'גרב' ו'ילפת'.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah lists yabelet (a wart-like blemish) for humans and dak tevallul (a thin white spot) for animals, since these are not explicitly written in the Torah for their respective categories.

A baraita is cited, teaching that the words 'גָּרָב' (garav) and 'יַלֶּפֶת' (yallefet) appear in both the human and animal contexts, forming a גזירה שווה (verbal analogy) to exchange the blemishes between the two categories.

The Gemara objects that without the גזירה שווה being 'free' (mufneh), it could be refuted: humans cannot learn from animals because animals themselves are offered on the altar, and animals cannot learn from humans because humans are obligated in more commandments.

The Gemara resolves that the גזירה שווה is indeed 'free' (mufneh), because the Torah could have written only 'יַלֶּפֶת' and derived 'גָּרָב' by a קל וחומר (a fortiori argument), so the extra 'גָּרָב' is superfluous and serves only to make the analogy immune to refutation.

items.text: דיון בצורך בכתיבת כל המומין
items.text_en: Why not write all blemishes in one place?
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Torah did not write all blemishes in one place and derive the rest from there. It considers writing them in humans or animals, but each option leads to potential exclusions. The Gemara concludes with the principle of Rabbi Yishmael's school: a paragraph that is repeated is only repeated for the sake of something new.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה מדוע לא נכתבו כל המומין במקום אחד ונלמדו בגזירה שווה, ומסיקה שחזרה נצרכת בגלל מומין ייחודיים לכל אחד, כדברי בית רבי ישמעאל שכל פרשה שנשנית – נשנית בשביל דבר שנתחדש בה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Torah did not write all blemishes in one place, with גרב (scab) and ילפת (lichen) repeated in both human and animal contexts, and derive the rest from that single list.
The Gemara considers writing all blemishes in humans or in animals, but each option would lead to the exclusion of blemishes unique to the other category.
The Gemara considers writing all blemishes in animals, but that would exclude human-specific blemishes like גבן (hunchback) and חרום (snub nose).

The Gemara proposes writing all common blemishes in one place, writing unique blemishes in their respective categories, and repeating גרב (scab) and ילפת (lichen) in both, then deriving the rest from each other.
The Gemara resolves the question by invoking the principle of the school of Rabbi Yishmael: any paragraph that is repeated is only repeated for the sake of something new introduced in it.

items.text: צורך בכתיבת מום בשלושה מקומות
items.text_en: Rava's explanation for three separate blemish sections
items.desc_en: Rava explains why the Torah wrote blemishes separately for humans, consecrated animals, and firstborns. Each has a unique characteristic that prevents deriving one from another. The Gemara then considers deriving one from two, but each potential source has a unique feature that prevents derivation, so all three are necessary.
items.desc: רבא מבאר מדוע נכתבו מומין באדם, בקדשים ובבכור – כל אחד נצרך, שכן אי אפשר ללמוד אחד מהשני בשל חומרות שונות בכל אחד.

sub.desc_en: Rava asks why the Torah wrote separate sections for blemishes in humans, consecrated animals, and firstborns.
Rava explains that each section is necessary because each category has a unique characteristic that prevents deriving its laws from the others.
The Gemara asks: if one cannot be derived from another, perhaps one can be derived from the other two combined?
The Gemara considers omitting the firstborn section and deriving it from humans and consecrated animals, but notes that those two share a greater sanctity.
The Gemara concludes that all three sections are necessary, as each potential derivation fails due to a unique feature of the source categories.

items.text: מקור המומין הנוספים באדם
items.text_en: Source for additional blemishes in humans
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan derives the additional blemishes in humans from the verse 'Any man who has a blemish from the seed of Aaron', interpreting 'man' as one who is equal in his seed of Aaron, i.e., a priest without blemish.
items.desc: רבי יוחנן דורש מהפסוק 'כל איש אשר בו מום מזרע אהרן' – איש השווה בזרעו של אהרן, כלומר שצורתו דומה לשאר הכהנים, ומכאן המומין הנוספים.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks for the source of the additional blemishes listed in the Mishnah that apply only to humans.

Rabbi Yochanan answers that the verse 'כֹּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ מוּם מִזֶּרַע אַהֲרֹן' (any man with a blemish from the seed of Aaron) teaches that a priest must be a 'man' who is comparable to the rest of Aaron's seed, excluding those with unusual physical features.

items.text: הבחנה בין מום לאי-שווי בזרע אהרן
items.text_en: Distinction between mum and eino shaveh
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks what difference exists between a permanent blemish (mum) and a condition that is not equal in Aaron's seed (eino shaveh). It answers that a mum disqualifies from service, while eino shaveh does not, and further distinguishes between eino shaveh and mar'it ha'ayin by noting a positive commandment.
items.desc: הגמרא מבחינה בין כהן בעל מום הפוסל לעבודה לבין כהן שאינו שווה בזרע אהרן. ההבדל הוא בכך שמום מחיל חילול עבודה, בעוד שאי-שווי בזרע אהרן אינו מחיל חילול. כמו כן, נדונה ההבחנה בין אי-שווי בזרע אהרן לבין מראית העין, וההבדל הוא באיסור עשה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what difference exists between a permanent blemish (mum) and a condition that is not equal in Aaron's seed (eino shaveh).
The Gemara answers that a mum disqualifies from service (מחיל עבודה), while eino shaveh does not.
The Gemara asks what difference exists between eino shaveh and mar'it ha'ayin (appearance-based disqualification).
The Gemara answers that the difference is a positive commandment (עשה) — eino shaveh is a Torah disqualification, while mar'it ha'ayin is only rabbinic.

items.text: Definitions of kilon and makaban
items.text_en: Definitions of kilon and makaban
items.desc_en: The Gemara defines kilon as one whose head resembles a turnip, and makaban as one whose head resembles a hammer. It cites a baraita describing the neck position for each, and elaborates on the terms shakut and shamut.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara defines a kilon as one whose head resembles a turnip, and a lafta as one whose head resembles a turnip bulb.
A baraita is cited describing that the neck of a kilon stands in the middle of his head.
The Gemara defines a makaban as one whose head resembles a hammer, and explains the terms shakut (sunken in front) and skifat (protruding behind) with a folk saying.
A baraita is cited describing that the neck of a makaban is shakut (pressed down) and shamut (long and stretched).

items.text: Dispute on ba'alei chatarot
items.text_en: Dispute on ba'alei chatarot
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Sages regarding ba'alei chatarot (those with growths). When there is a bone, all agree it disqualifies; the dispute is when there is no bone, with one opinion considering it eino shaveh and the other merely a lump of flesh.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens by stating the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Sages regarding ba'alei chatarot (those with growths), noting that when there is a bone, all agree it disqualifies.

The Gemara resolves that the dispute is specifically when there is no bone: one opinion considers it an אֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה (a disqualifying irregularity), while the other considers it merely a lump of flesh (קִרְקוּרָא דְּבִישְׂרָא).

items.text: דין הקרח (קרחה) – שתי גרסאות
items.text_en: Rava's ruling on the kerach
items.desc_en: Rava clarifies the Mishnah's ruling on the kerach (bald person). In one version, he says the disqualification applies only when there is no hair behind but hair in front; if there is hair behind, he is valid. In another version, he rules that having hair both behind and in front disqualifies, and having no hair at all also disqualifies.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה שתי גרסאות בדינו של הקרח. לפי גרסה אחת, קרח פסול רק כשאין לו שיער מאחור ויש לו מלפנים, אך אם יש לו מאחור כשר. לפי גרסה שנייה, כשר רק כשיש לו מאחור ואין לו מלפנים, אבל אם יש לו גם מלפנים וגם מאחור – פסול.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that the kerach (bald person) is disqualified from priestly service.

Rava clarifies that the Mishnah's disqualification applies only when there is no hair behind but hair in front; if there is hair behind, he is valid, and certainly if there is hair behind but not in front.
An alternative version reports Rava's ruling on the Mishnah's end clause: having hair both behind and in front disqualifies, and having no hair at all also disqualifies.

items.text: דברי רבי יוחנן: קרחנין, ננסין, זבלגנין
items.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan on kerchanin, nanasin, and zavlegganin
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan states that kerchanin (bald-headed), nanasin (dwarfs), and zavlegganin (those with drooping eyelids) are disqualified because they are not equal in Aaron's seed. The Gemara questions why these are needed, as some are already taught, and resolves that the ruling excludes a baraita that declared them valid, attributing that baraita to Rabbi Yehuda.
items.desc: רבי יוחנן פוסל קרחנין, ננסין וזבלגנין משום שאינם שווים בזרע אהרן. הגמרא דנה מדוע היה צורך לומר זאת, ומסיקה שבא להוציא מדעת רבי יהודה הסובר שהם כשרים מדאורייתא ורק פסולים משום מראית העין.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan rules that kerchanin (bald-headed), nanasin (dwarfs), and zavlegganin (those with drooping eyelids) are disqualified because they are not equal in Aaron's seed.
The Gemara questions why Rabbi Yochanan needed to mention kerchanin and nanasin, as they are already taught in the Mishnah.
The Gemara explains that zavlegganin needed to be taught, lest one think they are only disqualified due to mar'it ha'ayin (appearance).
The Gemara objects that wherever there is a disqualification due to mar'it ha'ayin, the Mishnah explicitly teaches it, as with the case of loosened eyelids.
The Gemara rejects the objection, suggesting that the Mishnah taught one case and the same applies to all.
The Gemara objects further that the Mishnah repeats the disqualification due to mar'it ha'ayin in the case of lost teeth.
The Gemara resolves that Rabbi Yochanan's ruling comes to exclude a baraita that declared these individuals valid, only disqualifying them due to mar'it ha'ayin.
The Gemara identifies the author of that baraita as Rabbi Yehuda, who derives from the verse 'the priests' to include kerchanin.

items.text: דין הגיבן – מחלוקת תנאים
items.text_en: Mishnah and Gemara on gibben
items.desc_en: The Mishnah defines gibben as one without eyebrows or with only one eyebrow, with additional opinions from Rabbi Dosa and Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus. The Gemara questions the meaning of gibben, cites a baraita, and resolves a contradiction regarding a creature with two spines, concluding that the Mishnah refers to a curved spine.
